My daughter has had a lot of fun with this set. It comes with the soap base, sent, colors, and molds. She just puts the soap base, color, and sent in a mug then puts it in the microwave. Once it is melted she mixes and pours it in the mold. It doesn't take long to set, and quickly she has a new soap.

Last year, I wanted to get this for my son, but we already have molds from making other projects (ie. melted crayons, ice, chocolate, candy, etc.) and I knew we could find all the ingredients at a better price-- so instead, I gifted this set to my niece.  The box is colorful and bright and looks so fun.  She loved it and spent a ton of time making soaps for her home and friends.  She is 13 and careful, so it worked nicely for her.  She can use the molds again to make more over and over again, or, now that she's learned the basics, she can expand creatively.  I looked for this set again as the holidays are upon us and we are in 2020, stuck at home altogether.. but I'm still not impressed by the price tag.

It's a Christmas gift for grand girls.  It seemed easy yet challenging enough for 5 and 7 years old with parental assistance.

Pros:
-Very easy to do (surprisingly easy, in fact)
-It's a quick activity, so doesn't take hours and hours
-Simple instructions
-Cleaning up is easy. Just soak the stirring spoon and measuring glass in water overnight and the hardened soap dissolves
-The projects are cute and my kid loved them

Cons:
-Melted soap is extremely hot and hardens extremely quickly, so I had to do all of the heating and pouring
-If using the microwave method, it's incredibly difficult to keep the soap from bubbling while you heat it, which makes the finished result look cloudy. Because of this, our fish-in-a-bag soap ended up being a complete fail. Still, that was the only fail we had
-The purple is EXTREMELY dark, it almost looks black (my kid thinks this is a "pro," not a "con," because she put a lot of glitter in the purple soap, and she thinks the finished product looks like a galaxy filled with stars. It looks cool, but if you and your kid are expecting a bright purple, you'll be disappointed).

I still think this is a great kit, and the soaps turned out nice. I am glad that it's so quick, though. I don't know if it would keep my 8yo's attention any longer.

She could pick the project, pick the colors, and put the scented oil in the melted soap, but since all the stirring and pouring has to happen so quickly, I had to do that.

Even so, she absolutely loves the finished products. Most came out better than I expected.

And at the end of it, you have a handful of useful items. Since this review is being written in April of 2020, easy craft kits have been a godsend for giving my kid something to do. And with current events, having a handful of adorable soaps has been so great in encouraging my kid to wash her hands.

Definitely a good value, even with the list of cons.

My daughter received this as a gift and we enjoyed doing it together as a craft. The soaps are cute and she enjoyed designing them and choosing the colors. Our soaps came out looking pretty much like they look on the box. Overall, the project took about 1.5 hours (including hardening time for the soaps, which is 30 min to 1 hr during which you cannot use the soap mold).

You need to know that you - as the parent or adult - will do most of the work on this. You need to heat the soap (and it will burn you when it's hot). You need a pourable container such as a glass measuring cup - and this cup will get hot. You also need to work VERY quickly with the hot soap. The time between microwave and hardening is about 10 - 15 seconds, and during that time you need to also stir in the color, glitter (and scent if you're using them). If you slop the soap, it'll burn you or adhere to your container and you'll need to re-melt. And when pouring it, (especially for the peace sign), you need to have a very steady (but QUICK) hand.

Now think - does this describe the skill of most 6-7-year-olds you know? :-)

Lastly, when the soap does harden, it's nearly impossible to get out of the mold. At least ours was. It was so hard I almost had to get my husband to push them out. And then when you push them out, the mold gets wrinkled up, which makes it hard to use for a second soap of the same shape.

It's a fun project as long as you are aware that you'll be standing there doing it while your kid watches, unless your kid is either VERY steady for this age, or is quite a bit older (say, middle school). My kid was able to help stirring somewhat, and poured one or two, but the glass measuring cup became too hot and the soap was hardening too quickly for her. She mainly acted as a designer of the soaps (and now, user of them). We used chop sticks to stir, which worked really well. Also keep in mind that for the confetti one, you need to keep the hardened bits that don't make it into the mold. Best to read through all of the instructions for each soap before beginning. That's the best way to plan out which soaps to make first!!

I accidentally purchased this twice and am returning one, but still feel the need to leave a review. This is a great brain teaser game for most ages. It’s small and compact size makes it great for travel or to sit on top your kitchen table or a desk.
With so many cards and puzzles available for the different game play options, it’s not a game you will grow tired of quickly. Fun game to play after dinner while everyone is sitting around the table together. It comes with cards to help you set up and solve each different game play possibility. With cards ranging from fairly easy to quite challenging.

[[VIDEOID:76c047bc1b993585ece6eeb0c23911bb]] If you're looking for a challenging yet low-tech family game, look no further.

Believe it or not, this one doesn't plug in anywhere, needs no batteries, has no tangles of wire to connect, makes no noise, and best of all, doesn't have hundreds of expensive add-ons, memory cards and other related stuff that you have to buy.

It takes up almost no space, comes with its own little carrier bag, and provides hours of educational fun for all ages.

You can take this on a plane
You can take this on a train
You can take this here or there
You can take this ANYWHERE

What you get:

1. A small plastic game board with a handy storage drawer and a slot for the game card in play
2. A bunch of colored plastic cars and trucks
3. A deck of game cards with clearly illustrated traffic jam situations for different skill levels
4. A drawstring cloth carrier bag

What you do:

1. Start with the Beginner cards and work your way up to the Advanced level
2. Set up the cars on the board as indicated on the card
3. Try to get the little red car to the only exit by driving forward and reversing the vehicles on the board until the way is clear
4. Try not to tear your hair out or use bad language at the vehicles blocking you
5. Try not to peek at the answers on the back of the card

When you're through with this one, there are four additional game sets at ridiculously affordable prices. Each one gives you one more vehicle and another set of game cards.

Believe me, when you graduate from this traffic school you'll be able to drive in the Caribbean without any problems.

Amanda Richards, December 28, 2008

This is not a game for all kids.  I bought it and tried it out myself to see if my grandson who was going to be 9 would like.  After trying it, I knew it would not be for him.  He would not have enjoyed the necessity to analyze and come up with the appropriate solution without getting frustrated.  However I have other grandchildren and immediately knew which one of my grandchildren (she will be 9 in June) would not only love the challenge but enjoy the analytical aspect of this game. I also saw the aspect of other's being pulled into the game by making suggestions.  I give this a 5 star rating but consider the personality and interests of the child.  This will be a very beneficial game for some kids but could also turn another kid off completely if they got frustrated.  The nice part of this game is the beginner to advanced levels of play. The size of the game and nice bag for the small parts and best of all, when all else fails a step by step guide to the correct solution is on the back off each card. As an adult of the same type as my granddaughter, I found it challenging and captivating.  A game you could walk away from and come back to later for a fresh take and hopefully a solve. B0017DETOM.text: I work in a Special Needs classroom with a couple of autistic boys who love to color with colored pencils. They tend to use certain colors more often and then because of the firm pressure that they use when coloring, we are constantly out of those certain colors. This week, one of the boys nearly had a meltdown because we didn't have the right shade of blue. This set of 8 colors allows us to restock the blues, reds, black, browns, and yellows that we go through the most without adding more of the colors we aren't using as quickly. I would buy a box of single colors, such as all blue, if they were packaged that way. As far as the pencils go, Crayola is our go-to brand in the classroom. They sharpen easily & don't have as much breakage as some brands. The colors are vibrant.

I am a "starving artist" and cant afford Prismacolor pencils. I wouldnt buy them even if I could because Crayola works just perfectly for my designs. They even look like professional pencils were used if you know how to use them. However, I HATE that Crayola doesnt sell them individually...as there are colors I use more of than others.
The pencils write well, but I find the branding of this product offensive.  It is my opinion that these shouldn't be called "colored pencils" but rather "pencils of color."

Now imagine that occurring with 20 students. Buy the 8 count.

The rock in that one also appears to be a lot smaller than the one we have (which came with the tan guy). I'm not sure if the size of the rock has any effect on the "rumble" function.

The truck itself seems to be the same between the two versions, both in appearance and in sound.

I generally hate noise-making toys, but this truck is tolerable, mostly because it's not very loud. The song is a little annoying, but it's not as bad as a lot of toys I've encountered because it's not very loud or long. The "rumbling" can be a little annoying (think hard plastic hitting hard plastic over and over and over in a quick pattern), but all you have to do is take out the rock. 9 times out of 10, the truck isn't being rolled around with the rock in it, anyway. Like many others I owned the original Radio Shack version of this 130-in-1 electronics kit decades ago. True, this Elenco version isn't very sturdy. It's light and flimsy. But the overall layout, components, and experiments you can wire together are about the same. The 159-page real paper manual that comes with it is a plus (the PDF is also available for download from Elenco's web site). Each experiment has an overview, a schematic, and wiring connection-by-numbers instructions. Many useful and educational analog circuit designs are included (plus one digital gate logic IC). No microprocessor, computer, smart phone, or software updates required. Yea!!!

OK, now the quality issues. The first experiments I correctly wired together didn't work at all. I installed two different sets of 6AA batteries (Amazon Rechargeable then Duracell Alkaline). Still nothing. I returned the first one back to Amazon, got a replacement the next day. Both had the same problem. Both had a sticker with Date Code 0119. Hmmmm, manufactured the same day, same problem. I did some basic troubleshooting to try to figure out the problem.

It turns out the design or manufacture of the battery holder is defective. There is a gap of about 1mm between the + side of each battery and terminals in the holder. Two small plastic tabs at that location prevented the battery connection from being made. My "fix" was to jam a wadded up piece of copper tape to fill the gap at each of the 6 positive battery terminals to complete the battery circuit (aluminum foil would work fine too). Hopefully Elenco will crack the whip at the Chinese factory to fix this, or they'll see a lot of returns for this very simple and silly defect. Check recent reviews to see if the problem has been fixed in newer batches from the factory.

If you don't have a voltmeter, you can construct a simple circuit to see if power from the batteries is making it to the front panel. Install the batteries and try lighting up the decimal point of the digital display by connecting: 25-121,24-119 or 25-124,24-122

Most of the experiments I've tried so far worked. But the AM radio receiver circuits are iffy. The only one I could make work was #113: Two-Transistor Radio. I used the supplied long green wire raised up high as the antenna. The signal levels seem too low to work for #112: Crystal Set Radio and #109: Operational Amplifier AM Radio.

Quality issues aside, I'm keeping it. I'm having too much fun with it. And I have great respect for the designers who created the original analog circuits that can be recreated using this kit.

Since then, he is on a mission to build at least on project every day and show it to me when I get home from.

Pros
- Very engaging for curious young minds
- Easy to follow instructions
- Enough variety to give the kit solid replay value

Cons
- Some of the wiring directions actually contradict the schematics. If you follow the numbered connections, the project will not work, but you can quickly identify the errors if you know how to follow the schematic drawings.
- I wish that the casing were made of something a bit more durable than cardboard
- My son now has grand ideas about re-wring half of our household appliances to "make them work better"

I bought this with the hopes of sparking an interest of EE in my two sons, 8 and 10. While this product has a well written manual that describes hook up sequences it falls short of explaining anything at all about the relays, transistors, resistors, capacitors, relays, etc that you are making connections between. Educationally this toy is useless.

So I hoped the boys would at least find it entertaining. So I helped them make an LED flash and the speaker make a whining noise (there are way simpler methods to accomplish these tasks than what the book makes you endure). Somehow the crystal diode radio just would not work, I mean c'mon I can make one of these out of copper wire and toilet paper tubes but some how this kit couldn't even walk the 3 of us through the oldest radio technology in the world.

A few other things wouldn't work so I am forced to believe some of the components were bad, I am forced to return.

At best this is a good time consuming toy for a rainy day (if the components are working). Do not expect much and maybe you won't be as disappointed as I was.

P.S. this didn't soil my kids enthusiasm for EE, I purchase the book Make: Electronics available at a discounted price here on Amazon. Got some breadboards a few wires and other components and we are off to the races!

When I saw the opportunity to review this Radio Flyer four-in-one tricycle, I was eager to accept: My cousin and his wife, who live a couple doors down the street, have a three-year-old, and they have just learned that they are expecting another baby in June. So I knew that this toy would be used in all four of its "incarnations" at one point or another.

The toy arrived within three days, even though I did not request any special shipping status.

The directions for putting the tricycle together are excellent and detailed. They are entirely pictorial, with no words at all, which is a godsend for those of us who labor for hours trying to read badly translated written instructions. Laura (the mom) put the entire tricycle together with only minimal help from Brian (the dad). Brian did have to help with Instruction #13, and also with tightening screws and bolts here and there. I was delighted to hear that one does not need an engineering degree to put this toy together.

The tricycle went together very easily for the most part. The handlebars are the hardest part of the construction. Laura recommends that anyone putting this tricycle together pull up on the handlebars after attaching the bars and the clamp to be sure that the clamp has tightened properly. She pulled up on the handlebars at least four times and was able to remove them despite that clamp being on. You just have to tighten the clamp as much as possible.

This tricycle seems very durable, though I will add to this review after Brandon (the three-year-old) has used the toy more. The canopy is very nice, and the straps on the seat will be great for the new baby when he or she can use it (at nine months or so). The cupholder that surrounds the infant in the seat will be great for the baby as well. My only wish is that the tricycle had rubber tires instead of plastic tires. We live in a somewhat rural area with no sidewalks, and the plastic tires may not hold up as well as rubber tires. The push handle, to be used for infants, adjusts to the height of the adult pushing the tricycle, which is a wonderful feature.

Now to the acid test: Does the child like the toy? Brandon has been off this tricycle only to eat and sleep ever since it was put together. He even attempted to get on it several times while his mom was putting it together, saying, "I should try it!" With winter coming on he will probably use it only in the house at first, but Brian and Laura have a huge basement, and riding his tricycle there will give him hours of play time.

I highly recommend this tricycle, especially if your child or children are young enough to take advantage of it in all its formations. The product description says it can be used from nine months to five years, and that sounds about right.
Loved it very easy to put together

Good tricycle for the 12 month old grandson.  Not too hard to put together.  Holds him in well and shades him from the sun.  Steers easily for the adult holding the handle from behind and controlling the little 'driver'.  Doesn't seem as sturdy and heavy as the old time tricycles but it should hold up long enough for him to outgrow it.

Seems to be well made. Great instructions for assembly make it easy to put together quickly. I think the 4-In-1 features will allow my granddaughter to get a couple of years of use out of it.
I like it but it's a big flimsy for radio flyer ...really wish it would've came with the foot rest though...besides that not much to complain about cuz it was on sale

Bought for my son's first birthday and it would be perfect if there where a place to rest his feet! He tries to rest them on top of the wheel but they keep sliding off...he has had enough of dangling legs after about 10 minutes!! Taking this back!!

OOok
kinda hard to put together and once it was together it hasn't stopped.  she loves it.  easy to push and adjust.  she would ride for hours!

This is a great trike
Easy to put together and easy to adjust
Fits my 2yr old perfectly
Absolutely love this trike, and so does my grandson!!!
my baby loves it and its much lighter then bringing a stroller to the park. it takes some time to put together but it was worth it.
We got this for my son's first birthday and he LOVES it! We take it on all of our walks! It takes a little  time to but together but is well worth it!
My daughter loves it as a good substitute stroller now while my granddaughter gets used to a trike. It will be a stand alone trike as she gets older. High steering handle bars for pushing the trike.
Our son loves his new bike.  I bet he'd sleep on it if he found a way to do it.
Love this! Can't wait for warmer weather to use it again! I'm 5'2" and the handlebars work well for me, but my husband is 6'2" and has to bend a bit.
Love this and so does my son! Best Christmas gift
great condition
These are great. Now all my grandchildren have one!

This was the perfect birthday gift for both of my daughters 1st birthdays!!! I bought the first one when my oldest turned 1 in 2011, and she still rides on the trike!! My youngest just turned 1 in Oct so we got her one as well and she loves it! It is fairly simple to put together, it took me about 20-30 mins from start to finish. The instructions were very easy to follow. Fantastic quality that has stood strong against the test of my rowdy girl over the last 4 years! They get used daily in our household from just riding in the driveway to pushing the youngest around the block or to the park. It has an adjustable seat that is very easy to adjust as your child grows...my 5 year old is very tall for her age and still fits well on the biggest setting. The harness is easy to adjust as the baby grows, or for use with multiple children. Both of my girls' favorite part is the trunk...they love to put their little toys in it to take with us to the park. It also has a cup holder and snack tray on the front for toddlers! I would definitely buy this again for any future children.
Bought this for my grandson for Easter.  He's 7 months old but once weather is nicer, can't wait to use it.

I was looking at the smart trike for my daughter, but she was given this as a gift. It serves its purpose and it is cute and gender neutral, but I really wish we had gotten the smart trike.

Cons:
-Squeaky wheel, we have tried WD40 on every wheel and can't get the squeak to go away. If you are on a long walk it will drive you crazy. I have read this on other reviews too.
-small storage, I can't even fit a Muchkins Snack cup in there and close it. The bar from the back tires takes up most of the space.
-no adult storage, I would like to be able to keep my phone and things that I don't want my daughter to have up away from me.
-sun shade doesn't do much and it is VERY hard to open and close, You can't angle it to keep the sun out and when you open and close it you feel like you are going to break it.
-low "stroller" handles don't go very high, I am only 5'2'' and I wish it went higher

Pros:
-cute as just a trike
-I like the shape of the stroller handles
-gender neutral

One other thing that I don't know if it is a pro or a con, it really needs two hands to control it from the parents' handles. I can't walk the dog and push her, nor can I have a drink (aka stop at starbucks) and push her.

Overall, I wish we had paid the extra money for the smart trike.
My 1 yr old LOVES this!! So excited for the day he can rude it by himself.

Awesome! Our 1 year old loves it! She loves sitting in it and holding the handle-bars. She loves pushing it and using it as a walker. She loves putting her toys in the back to play with later. Really excited that we will be continuing to get use out of this as she grows!

Wonderful! Our 2 year old loves this! We take him for walks and it's nice for when he gets tired peddling. The only thing that would make it better is to have a place for him to rest his feet if he isn't peddling.
I am so excited to present this to my son!  It arrived fast and I assembled it myself with no problem.  I just know he is going to be loving it for years to come.  P.S. He loves it!

My little one likes it, but I'm not sure it will last for generations to come. The plastic doesn't seem as sturdy as I hoped. It also came in a billion pieces and I had to hire someone to put it together. Even he had trouble doing it and he's a professional.

Great trike! Our son was 1year old when we first purchased this item for him. He loves it best birthday present. We only wish we had known it could be customized with your child's name before we received the item.
My son is not into it yet. He is 17 months
my nephew and his parents enjoy it.
My grandson has gotten a lot of use from this and his mom likes the control.
I absolutely love this tricycle!!! I am so happy it has the options on the front tire to allow their feet to either pedal or rest without them moving.
Very happy with seller and product!!
Great quality item arrived on time for my grandsons birthday....

Love that you can use the handles to control the child's steering if they can't yet or if they try to "go their own way".  That the handles are adjustable is great, but I put it together before gifting and then couldn't loosen it back.  My son was able to rectify that with some elbow grease, though. The removable parts will allow it to grow with my grandson to eventually be a regular trike.  If it had been a heavy duty, durable metal as we had in my day ;-)  I would have given it 5 stars.

This is a great bike for toddlers.
My only complaint is that the handles on top for the adults to push the child are a little flimsy and not as durable as I imagined.
I still the bike 5 stars though because my child loves riding in it, I love pushing him in it and we have gotten so many compliments on it!
Good product.
Easy to assemble about 20 mins.

This is a cute little tricycle. However it has a few issues.
The biggest issue is that the handles, where the adult steers the bike, are wobbly and not in there solid. The bike was put together correctly. It isn’t rocket science.
I also dislike the quality of this item. It’s a cheap plastic that was used to construct this bike. Whereas the older ones were constructed using a metal of some sort and lasted much longer. Unfortunately, a lot of manufacturers have started cutting corners like this to save money and make the big bucks.
One last thing that would be great is if there were a way to remove the peddles and place a small platform for feet to rest. And have it to where the platform could be removed as well for new learners to simply use their feet to move.
My son loves this!  Great buy and so much fun!
Love this item!  and easy to assemble...only one step was a bit of a pain, but the rest was easy.  The little girl loves it.

I bought this for my daughter as soon as she could sit up steadily by herself (5-6 mos old). She loves to look all around in her stroller so she was ecstatic her first few weeks in this bike where she flapped her arms and clapped her hands on all her trips.  I can't wait for spring to get her in this thing again. It's made of metal and plastic, everything seems very durable with the exception if the little trunk in the back. It's only plastic, not a lot fits in it and it pops up when you ease off curbs or trying to maneuver it out of the house down the front steps (no baby inside).

Bought for our Granddaughters second birthday, she already knew what it was from the picture on the box! She has a lot of kids her same age that have them and she got to use one for a week - and can almost reach the pedals! She was so excited and her parents felt it was the only safe [[ASIN:B003AVIO4K Radio Flyer 4-in-1 Trike, Red]] and they research *everything* to make sure it's safe for her to use.
Other friends that have kids the same age have said it truly is one of the best stroller to tricycles out there so 5 stars it is.

We love this little trike! We started using this trike when my son was about 11 months old.  We would take him on long walks and to the zoo.  This was perfect for the zoo because he would sit up and check everything out. People would comment all the time what a great idea it was to stroll him around this way. We thought it was much better than a stroller and we got a lot of use out of it. We have since taken the shade, steering mechanism and the support bar off.  He is now 2 years old and cruising and peddling around on his own.
my one and a half year old refuses to get out most of the time.  Love the fact that this thing evolves as you kid grows.

Purchased for my granddaughter when she was about a year old with the idea my daughter and son in law could push her around. Her feet didn't reach the pedals but the still spun and hit her in the feet. The mechanism that was supposed to stop it didn't really work. They never really got much use out of it. She's 3 1/2 now and can finally almost reach the pedals but doesn't really seem interested in it. Save your money and buy a stroller and a separate tricycle or balance bike.

Got this for my daughter for her 1st birthday.  She does like it a lot, but she can't ride it for long as it starts to hurt her a bit due to no foot pegs since she is a bit short for the peddles.  Other bikes have the pegs, so it isn't a foreign idea.  But the quality does seem pretty good and once she is long enough I am sure she will really enjoy it.

I was so excited to get this for my 17 month old, but I wish that I had done more reading up on it first. I really like the idea of a 4 in 1 model, but the fact that there is no foot rest available did not hit me until I placed my son in it. I cannot imagine pushing him down the street with his feet dragging on the ground. Since I am stuck with this, I am going to try to find some way to fix this problem so that we can enjoy this trike until he is old enough to place his feet on the pedals.

My 18 month old grand daughter ran right to this trike Christmas morning and insisted on sitting on it while all the other presents were unwrapped. She knew without us telling her that this was her present from Santa. Her big sister has been pushing her around the house in it and we will be going out for a walk later. She has been hating her stroller for some time now so this is a great alternative. Well made, the adult handle bars extend up high enough for her Papa to push her in it and he is 6'5. All the adjustments that can be made to it will ensure a long useful life for it. The seat has three height adjustments as well as the handlebars.
perfect for my 7 mo. grandson to get pushed around in.  bike will grow with him. I hook small toys on the handle bars.  we love it!

B003IKMR0U.text: Every year I buy silly/useful things for my family Christmas.  Obviously these are part of the "silly" items...Niece is a zombie fan.. this seemed like a good choice.  She is an adult, but once in awhile, we adults like to have fun.  :)  It arrived quickly because I have Prime and in good condition.  I will update with any issues.

This was a fun, fast-paced, easy to learn game. I love that you can get add on dice to make it more challenging. This is laid-back enough that you can chat while you play or take breaks when needed. This will definitely be one we will travel with often!

Another good donation item I bought some of for kids in need for Christmas! Reviews were good, price was good for the fun time kids get as per the reviews also! Packaged well and heavier than T thought they'd be, so quality seems good.

First I played with 4 adults.  We had a blast, laughing at ourselves and our rolls.  Then I played with daughter's family including children aged 8-13.  We had so much fun they begged to play over and over through my entire visit (month).  Well worth it and not at all scary.
You would not think this would be near as fun as it is.  :)  My friends and I break this game out when we are taking a break from heavier, lengthier games.
Simple, quick filler game that all ages can understand/play.  Play it with my kids (11 & 6) and they both really get into it.  Lasts about 10 min.

Fun and quick game in between longer tabletop rounds. My mom and I love to play, because we can finish a game in five minutes or so in between other activities. Very easy to learn and very easy to play, this one is good for seasoned tabletoppers and newbies alike. Only complaint is that the dice shaker isn't coated or anything, so the dice are pretty loud when you are trying to mix them up. Drove my dad (who has sensitive hearing) right out of the room.
Son loved it. Well, at least as long as the craze lasted. Now collects dust. But a good price and solid product.
A nice novelty for kids.

Quick, fun game for all ages.

Sometimes you want to play a game but you don't want it to take all day. This is great for times like that and everyone still has fun.

I played this game with adult friends.  It is an easy, almost mindless game.  Lots of laughs. I knew my grandchildren would love it, and I ordered it when I got home from game night.  Looking forward to the next visit.
Just got and played with my son. We love this game,  easy to learn and quick to play. Overall I would recommend.
This is such a fun and quick game.  It's easy enough that my kids can play with us without any frustration on their part.
Such a fun, easy game!

This is a fast-moving, fun, simple game with a few easy-to-learn-and-remember rules. It's a great game to play with a few friends for 10-20 minutes before you dive into a heftier game on game night, or just a good ice breaker at a get-together.

For all the raving reviews. This game is good.  Boys 10 and 12 thought it was a little boring. I thought it was ok. Plays fast, but does not really take much skill. Interest was not kept. I just think it is hard to compete with all the electronic games of today. Still a descent game if you want something fast.
Such a fun game! Even my 3yr old gets it. Fun while drinking beer or milk.

This is a quick playing press your luck dice game. It is a great choice for a fast game with a zombie theme.
If you like rolling three dice at a time, this game is for you.
If you like zombie games but don't like long games, this game is for you.
If you like little cardboard cups with zombie pictures, this game is for you.

It is fun with any number of players as long as you don't mind downtime, if you do mind downtime, I recommend no more than five or six.

Strategy tip: If you get a bunch of brains, think about stopping. If you have no brains, keep rolling. Few brains and a couple shots? I say roll again only if you are a ways behind.
I love this game. It's fun, easy, fast, and hilarious when your playing partner looses everything. It's a great game.
gift

This is a fun game for any age. It is usually a pretty quick game as most Steve Jackson games, but can be played as many rounds as you want. I would recommend picking up one of the expansions once youve played a bit.

I bought this game for my boyfriend as one of his Christmas gifts, and he taught me how to play earlier today. The game is real easy to learn, and it's fun because you never know who's going to win it all depends on the roll of the three dice. He won the first round and I won the second round.
as described
Fun family game
Silly simple little game.  Great to keep in your purse for something to do at the bar while hanging out since it's pretty small!
Simple, fun dice game that's quick and easy to play. Makes a fun drinking game too ;-)
love this game
This is a fun game! Very simple to learn and play.
Simple, fast, and fun. This game is perfect to play between more involved games or as a warm-up. Great addition to any game night!
Perfect for camping!
Simple game fun at a party.  The expansion seemed a little superfluous, but the core game is solid.
Got this for my daughter for Xmas think she has only played it one time, she told me it was boring, don't waste your money.
Just ... boring.
Fun little time waster that takes no time to learn. Plenty of replay with younger teens and older kids, especially if you're willing to joke around with 'em
LOVE this as a travel game -- quick, easy to understand and simple to play.

This is a fun and silly toy.  As a zombie trying to eat more brains than your fellow zombies before being shotgunned this is a fun quick game either to play as a filler game or as a party game just for fun.  Not a lot of heavy strategy but my family enjoys it.

My husband and I didn't want to get into long, boring games like monopoly. We decided to get this one a shot.
We both like zombies, but you don't have to like zombie flicks to like this game.

Great push your luck dice game. We really enjoy it, although like all push your luck dice games it can get very frustrating. There may only be 3 red dice in that cup (higher likelihood to be shot) but it seems like I grab them every time. My ONLY complaint about the game is that the plastic cup is quite loud when we shake it up. BUT if the alternative is a cardboard tube, I'll take the plastic cup for more durable storage any day.

We now own a lot of push your luck dice games ("Roll for it!" is fun too [[ASIN:B00E3S8L7O Roll For It! (Red Edition)]]) so I did invest in a felt lined cup and dice tray. So the cup noise isn't an issue with that accessory purchased [[ASIN:B0049H0E7O Felt Lined Professional Dice Cup w/ 5 Dice by Brybelly]].
We instantly took to this fun, fun game. It's so simple and easy to play anywhere. The kids are very into zombie games, movies, shirts, so this was an ideal addition to our collection.
VERY easy to learn and a blast to play regardless of how many people you have.  Fun way to pass the time

Bought this more as a gag gift for a "zombie TV show" fan, however, when we played it, we discovered it was very easy to learn, quick-playing, and actually rather fun.  There is enough strategy involved to make it interesting.  A fun, easy family game for all ages.
Easy, quick, loud, fun.

This game will help you learn how to survive the zombie apocalypse. With intense shotgun action, plenty of running away, and the occasional brains for sustenance, you will be ready for anything. Recommended only for those with a strong stomach (and a strong wrist). Work out profitable strategies and alliances as you master the complex moves of this game and leverage your knowledge of zombie lore to distract your opponents.

Batteries and Strategy Guide not included.

Recommended only for those with a strong stomach (and a strong wrist). Work out profitable strategies and alliances as you master the complex moves of this game and leverage your knowledge of zombie lore to distract your opponents.

Batteries and Strategy Guide not included.
I have had this game for many years. Very simple to learn. Fast game to play. Loads of fun. I got 2 for gifts they are my 20 year old daughter's.

It's quick to learn, easy to teach, & plays fast. You roll then decide on keeping your points or rolling again at the risk of losing your points. I've played it with people of all ages & everyone picks it up really quickly. It's a nice game to play to kill some time but isn't the most entertaining game to play either. I also think the Zombie theme is really overdone at this point & is kind of forced onto this game. Dice could just as easily have x's & o's on them instead of brains & shotguns but the art on the can is pretty eye catching & it's fun to say "I got shot' I guess.
Great game. I got this for a family game night. My two 8 yr olds love this. Just took minutes to learn. Great warm up for other games.
great game
It's a good 2+ player game that's compact and has a decent replay ability.
I got this on sale for $4 and I love it. It is super quick to play and a great push your luck filler game. I would recommend Bang! the Dice game over this if they are around the same price.

B003V18RNC.text: I didn't buy this to be used as a toy. I wanted it as a mold to pour quikcrete into. A lot of the reviews were not so good, but I didn't care about it holding air. I aired it up the day it arrived, it hasn't lost any as of yet. It seems very durable and bounces Great just like the balls we used in warball back in my P.E. classes.... Just holding it reminded me of some of the huts I received and gave. This almost seems sad to use it only once....

We got this for play in the pool. It is much "heavier" than most pool balls, but that makes it different and fun.
Seems like it is tough material, had no problems so far.
Does not hold air..... Returning
Bueno

Bought one ball  for my Australian Shepherd who likes to "herd" balls.  He loves to chase this ball and its thicker material has so far held up to his biting and claws.  I decided to order a second ball as a backup  and found that it is 1/4th  smaller fully inflated.  Because of the smaller size my dog was able to grasp the ball and punctured it in short order.  I question the quality control of this product..

Super expensive but since no more toys r us, these are tougher to find. Annoying!

Comes deflated.

So I bought this ball thinking that it would come with a ball pump or something but it didn't.. So it has been sitting on my counter just not blown up because I don't have anything to blow it up with so we will see when I have the time to go get one.
My kids asked for this to play four square.  It is a great ball and came deflated.
Just like when I was a kid, gift.
Had to order a replacement, the first one had a pretty big hole in it. The replacement seems to be doing okay though
Worked well in the kickball tournament
great price
material is thinner than expected...

Do NOT waste your money on this inferior playground ball. It arrives in an envelope!  It is deflated and you must pump it up.....however, it DOES NOT HOLD for very long, quickly becoming soft and virtually UNUSABLE.
great product
Bought these for our school. Great ball the kids loved them
Exactly what I want
Typical made in China product , garbage
At first I was disappointed because it was bot inflated. I should have paid better attention. But it's been a delightful ball for my 19 month old grandson. Mostly use indoors. Lovely bouncy ball.
Didnt include a pump

This ball does not seem to be made of rubber. It is very light weight and weighted towards the air valve. Still, grip is good, it's easy to handle, price was excellent and the grandkids love it. It does come deflated so it has to be blown up - no problem.  We haven't had it long, so I can't speak to its durability.

My 2-1/2 year old grandson loves bouncing this ball around the house, it's big enough for him to learn endurance.  My 6 year old granddaughter loves it for learning 4-square out on the patio.  Great ball, very sturdy, easy to fill with more air if needed.  Reminds me of the quality of playground balls when I was growing up, they lasted forever.
Sturdy kickball that stays inflated! It's working great for my busy kids.
This ball is sturdy and has held up well through several weeks of four square games. Has not deflated. Was as expected.
So not only is this ball not inflated when you get it...but...it doesnt come with anything to inflate it with...i don't know what kind of pump i need...bummer
Purchased this on 11-11 and it already popped!! Don’t waste your money!!
After a few months it leaked.

Good product, just not for dogs. This ball lasted about 15 minutes before my dog popped it, deflating it. She loved it until she killed it. Perhaps a simple statement like...Not recommended for dogs...would give me a hint not to buy it for a dog.
Larger then I thought.
ok.
It doesn’t hold air. Don’t waste your money😥
I could never blow it up because it didn’t come with the correct needle to go inside of the ball. I Even took the ball to the gas station to get filled up but there was no where that could help me
We have used the ball many times and it will continue to get a lot if use and it is holding up well!
I bought it for my German Shepard. She popped it in a few minutes.
Just what was needed for a 5 year old child.

A perfect sized, bouncy red ball. We keep it in the car trunk for when we spend time at the local park.
The kids can play all sorts of games with it. Lightweight, sturdy and seems to be holding air really well.
I use this ball for therapy.  It’s the right size to toss around.
Haven’t inflated it yet but looks good
It's a very durable outdoor ball. Nice & bright. Bounces off really well. Could be a little more hard to kick, so do wear closed toe shoes.
Great ball but a bit pricey.  Excellent quality though!

It is a classic playground ball.  My kids and I went out in the snow and kicked it around.  It kicks easy, and is easy to catch.  It was a little lopsided when I pumped it up, but it evened out with play.  What I like about it, is that it is not as heavy as the older balls.  You can still knock someone down in dodge ball, but you won't give them a concussion. . . Maybe.

Great ball. Brightened a child's Christmas. Item came on time and undamaged.
Thank you.
You'd expect for a gym teacher to own it; it's pretty sturdy. I bring it to my mother in law's for play and it has yet to be popped. Classic game to entertain the kids

B004560BPY.text: My baby is 9 months old and LOVES this toy. She loves opening the lid and pulling the toys out. They are the perfect size to fit in her hands.
Bought as gift,  my 4 yr old niece loved it
My 3 year old and 6 year old loved it.
Great toy. Lots of fun pieces. Keeps daughter entertained.

This sharing picnic is great for little minds, teaches all about sharing, shapes, food, colors, etc. It is our go-to when we are on the go to a friends house, or grand-mom's house and she seems to want to play with it everyday. Excellent price point, perfect for gift.
Our granddaughter absolutely loves it!
Adorable little set. my daughter loves it

I bought 2 of these first for my nieces little girls, ages 8 months and 2.  The 8 month old loves to take the items out of the basket and put them back in.  The 2 year old uses it all the time.  My 5 year old niece wanted one also, so I purchased another one!  The basket itself is a hit.  They carry it around a lot.  The items inside are all duplicate items.  The colors are vibrant and the items are durable and sturdy!  The piece de resistance is the red and white checkerboard table cloth, which every picnic needs!  Great gift for a child!

I bought it as a shape sorter toy for my infant. Well, it's not a shape sorter toy, but it is a very cute imagination/learning toy. Turns out, my toddler loves it even more. Looks like this gift will grow and get used for years to come.
My son loves this. I don't care that it's pink and purple. It has helped teach him his shapes and colors and he loves to carry the basket around. This toy has kept him entertained for hours.

I did not buy this but my Granddaughter loves this toy. I took care of her for a week and this was one of her favorite toys. She is 15 months old and knows how to but the little blanket out and then pick out the foods when you ask her.It did take me two days to realize that it was watermelon not a strawberry. That is why she couldn't find the strawberry!!! She will take it to her Pap's lap and but the blanket first and then have a picnic with him. This is one of the best toys of the year.

Update: She still loves this toy so I just bought one for my great niece. Can't wait to give it to her Sunday.

Our 1 yr old loves this basket, she will put the supplies in and take them back out all day.  This is a great quality toy, we set the table as a family and she loves it.  It is so cute, she loves lifting the lids and closing them.  All in all, this is top 3 of all toys my daughter plays with.  So much fun.
My granddaughter loves the picnic basket, picnics with her brother and her dolls.
Such a cute toy. Has all the contents for a great picnic. It has cute songs & sayings also. Perfect for the price .

My 2 year old grandaughter loves her picnic basket. It's fun to have a pretend picnic, then we work on her shapes and colors. One of the best learning toys for I have for my little toddler. I can't say I gave ever gone wrong with LeapFrog.

It's fun to put the things in and out of the basket and make plates to share with each other and pretend to eat. But the basket face is kind of creepy and the songs are odd. My daughter doesn't like the noises that this basket makes. So we usually just play with it sans noise, which is fine. Overall, it's not my favorite. Plus, do most 1-2 year olds even grasp the concept of a "picnic?" Picnics with 2 year olds are not fun, so we never really do them. So she doesn't know what they are. Well, anyway, it's still fun to play with once in a while.

I did not expect to be crazy about this when I bought it. I got in on one of the lightening deals on a whim and thought it probably owuldn't be amazing. My daughter LOVES it! It was her favorite thing starting around 8 months and she still loves it at a year. She dances to the music, and likes having picnics.

This is one of those must have toys. I looked at a few different picnic baskets before buying this. I have had this for awhile now and it has been one of the most used toys in my house. This is also a really sturdy toy- after two years of use it looks brand new.

All of the plates, utensils, cups and food are made from plastic, so they're easy to clean. Everything fits neatly inside the basket, which is a big deal for me- I hate having toys without a home. I love that leapfrog also incorporates learning into all of their toys. This toy helps them learn shapes and the plates are like little puzzles- you have to put the right shape food in the correct spot.

Another positive is that this isn't one of those really loud obnoxious toys. It does have songs and a learning mode but honestly my daughter doesn't even turn it on.
My one year old granddaughter loves this picnic basket.
Gave this as a gift and they seemed to enjoy it.
My 2 yr d loves playing with this.  She plays more with the basket and loves putting her toys in it to carry around.

This little toy had so many great reviews that I was excited to gift to my 19 month old for Christmas. Unfortunately she did not find it as entertaining as I thought she would. Maybe she still has to grow into it. All she just likes is taking things out and misplacing all the parts. I had to take the picnic blanket away because she kept throwing it in the trash thinking it was a dirty napkin or using it to erase her chalkboard, lol. Also wish there was a way to make it easier for the kids to turn it on and off and/ or change the music/ learning function. I just also purchased both the upper and lower case handwriting and cursive hand writing alphabet ones for my children (5 1/2, 8 and 10 year olds) and for my daycare (2 1/2-5 year olds). These are highly effective in encouraging and establishing pre-cursive writing skills, basic fine motor skills and refining existing writing skills, at each stage of development for the age groups I’ve mentioned above. I wish I’d had these when I was overseeing the preschool and lower school curriculum for two private schools for five years prior to starting my daycare/homeschool co-op. I’ve had these number practice and the upper and lower case alphabet handwriting ones for a number of years (before purchasing the cursive ones now as well) they are a favorite amongst the children I care for and they still look practically new. My youngest has been writing (handwriting) all the letters of the alphabet and these numbers since she was 3 1/2, greatly due to these products, in conjunction with number and handwriting work sheets and “write and wipe” products, after her introduction to handwriting using these products (the same goes for the children in my care). B0050QQUS0.text: I absolutely love these little dolls. To be honest, I gave them to my niece to play with and she wouldn't put them down. After watching her navigate to the website (absolutely incredible for a 4 year old to be this computer literate), I was sold on this doll. I really would love to own these myself, lol. You can't go wrong with this as a stocking stuffer, add on gift, or a quick little reward for good grades or work. I love them and they will provide hours of fun for your child.

This little doll will fit in the palm of an adult's hand. It's made entirely of plastic. No internal mechanics to break down. It can be positioned to sit or crawl. This would make a great bathtub toy because there's nothing that will get ruined if it goes in the water. There is a ribbon bow in the hair that can be removed.

This would be good for a 3 year old, except for the only chocking hazard. It's a tiny plastic peacock thing. There's a loop on it that looks like something the doll would hold, but I'm not sure what it is.

The head is as large as the rest of the body, with tiny hands and feet. She's wearing voilet feetie pajamas. The charm is hanging on a large clip that can be clipped to a belt loop or a purse. According to the box, Ella Song likes playing music and napping. The box shows a boom box, which would have been a cute thing to add instead of the strange peacock thing.

The owner of this doll can go online to play a game and watch a video. The website is only available for a limited time, but it doesn't say how long. There are a total of seven dolls in the Crib Life Cuties line, and you can meet them all online.

Little girls love little dolls, and they'll really like this cutie pie. She doesn't perform any tricks, so there's nothing to break down.

1 star off because there's no accessories that have to do with music. Also, since it's part of a "crib" life collection, it should come with something you'd find in a crib, like a blanket or a pacifier. The charm, itself, would be better if it hung from a chain so the owner could wear it around her neck, or on her wrist.

A similar review is given on Makayla. Smallish doll with a large hard head; cute face; arms and legs move a little bit; one has access via the code on the charm to it's particular website.

It tends to topple over; they each have a simple accessory; I don't think there's much action here. But I'm a Dad, and what do I know? The kid's (2 girls: ages 5 &8) award it a 2 thumbs up, 5 star rating.

They're both not into dolls, but they love playing with these- interacting with each other, sitting them at their table, doing(although limitedly)the web thing, and bascially, toting the cute things around the house wherever they go. They would be upset with me if I didn't give a 5 star rating. Personally, I'd say 3 stars generously. It is, I guess, reasonably priced.

This is a rubber doll with a large head, huge eyes, and a very teeny-tiny body. My granddaughter decided she makes a great 'toy' for her larger doll.

She has a cute 'rubber' hair style, a little charm and a cardboard guitar. The box says she's for ages 5+. She has a sweet, lovable face. There is a web site where the child can get to know the other "Crib Life Cuties". You can go to Criblife.com and see some of the web site even without a password. By entering their code, the child can play a game, watch a video, and 'get 2 know them!'

According to the box,

LIKES: playing music, napping

Ella: Turn it up! I [heart] rocking out 2 my favorite tunes!

Most children probably won't make much of a connection with the web site or the 'rocking out' but will enjoy cuddling this cute little doll.

This toy does not do much, but in a world of toys that tweet and overstimulated kids, sometimes cute and simple is the way to go. The toy is durable and feels safe and well made. Great value for money and in the case of my daughter, this toy kept her entertained for hours, a rarity these days.

The doll is very cute, but not at all realistic since she has that oversized head that is so popular now. That makes for a very unbalanced pose when you try to make her sit or crawl. It takes quite a bit of trial and error to find a position in which she can sit without toppling over onto her head.

Her one-piece outfit has a velcro closure in the back, so it's removable. For little hands, dressing the doll would be difficult.

The online aspect to this toy is minimal. Basically you gain access to a video of the doll singing and dancing and two online games to play.

My 7 year old daughter received this as a gift for Christmas. She has been wanting a Crib Life doll for a while.  She was very excited when she got it!  The doll has a tiny body that makes it super cute and big eyes that are adorable.  We have not be able to access the Crib Life website to enter her code to interact online...it seems to be down.  We will continue to try.  However, if you have an imaginative child, like my daughter, you won't even need the online access and code.  She plays with it in imaginative ways and loves carrying it around. My daughter loves that she is small, and has a cute face, and a cute pigtail on top.

[[VIDEOID:d912d8a96ad1e08ef24b9d0a8c022218]] Ella Song, the doll on the left in my video review, is a such a cutie! She comes dressed in a onesy and is packaged with a keychain (with web code) and rattle. She is a small doll with Keane style features that is durable, adorable, and the perfect size for four and five years olds! My younger cousins (4 and 5 years old) loved these dolls. They recognized them as 'new' immediately and gravitated towards them. Both Ella and Makayla were popular that day at my house! These dolls are marketed for 5 and up, but should be suitable for those a little younger, too. The rattle is small and could be considered a choking hazard, so if you do give this doll to a child who has a habit of putting small things in their mouth, you may want to take the rattle away.

Pros:
-They're adorable!
-Such a great size! Not too small and not too big. Perfect to toss in a travel toy bag.
-Good attention to detail when it comes to her hair and face!
-Easy to open packaging.

Cons:
-Both Ella and Makayla don't sit as they have been shown to do in promo shots. My dolls only hold a crawling position. If I try to make them sit, they fall over.
-The rattle doesn't fit in my dolls hand so it's a bit useless.

I think these dolls are adorable, as did my little cousins. If you are looking for a doll for your youngling, you should take a peek at Crib Life! Watch the review for more and please forgive the video's pixely look-- it had to be majorly condensed in size to fit here!

I go this game for me and my little cuz to play when I am watching her. So I waited and waited for this to show so we could try it out. Finally it arrived and she was so excited to try this out. So we busted it out and we were ready to go. Of course we had to read the instructions first and by we I mean me.

When I first started reading the instructions and it all seemed so complicated. I don't know why but there were so many rules. So I decided to just put the game together, that was pretty easy. It has multi little cards that you lay down in a certain order. Then you lay down your pieces and it all comes to you, or at least that is how it worked for me. Once I saw everything laid out and in place the rules made a lot of sense to me. So with everything ready to go we started playing.

I have to say for a game meant for little kids and very easy [once you understand it] it is actually a fun game. We played for a while then it was time for her to go to bed, so we had to stop. But she has wanted to play it every time I watch her so we have played multiple times. So with that said I have to say this is a fun game and worth getting for your kid. Even I liked it.

My kids love this game! My two boys pull this out several times a week and diligently roll the dice and move their spaceships around the map. They've make up fairly elaborate stories about what's going on and have developed some rules that only a 4 and 6 year old can understand, or appreciate. Are they anything like the "real" rules? Not at all. They are having such a blast using their imaginations that I don't want to ruin the fun. I have to give it 5 stars for that, but if you are into "the rules" then I'm afraid I can't comment.

If there is a down side it's that the ships are starting to go missing. We've been substituting other toys. Now Darth Vader joins the action.

This is a great little game. It is simple enough to be played by children 6 and up, only lasts 5 minutes or so, and yet can be enjoyed by adults as well. My sons have grown up playing games and this would have been a great addition to our collection when they were younger. Now I look forward to sharing it with my grandchildren.

This game is typical Ravensburger quality: sturdy and colorful. This game will be enjoyed for years. I recommend it.

We love this game! It's a lot of fun and very creative, as the board (and the order of the celestial bodies) changes frequently. I like this game because it forces my four-year-old to use her critical thinking skills...since each player has three rocket ships, my daughter must stop and think about which rocket she should move, and why she should move it. If any particular rocket moves too slowly, it will get sucked into a black hole (and this is bad!) but if she lands on a shooting star, she jumps ahead three spaces (and this is good!) so she has to think ahead and figure out the best possible move each time she rolls the die. Plus, the space theme of this game is fun and different....we have so many bug games as well as princess games, so outer space is a refreshing change of scenery for us.

This game is made by Ravensburger. For those who are unfamiliar with this company, they have some of the best quality products on the market and this game is no exception. The board pieces are thick and attractive and the little rocket ships are just plain cute! We love this game and my husband, myself and both my children give it eight enthusiastic thumbs up!

The Race Through Space Game was in high demand when my son first received.  He immediately was drawn to the game and was excited to get started.  Unfortunately the game's instruction were not entirely intuitive.  My son enjoyed the first round though admittedly he was not sure what he was doing.  He enjoyed playing a few times but eventually lost interest.  Overall the game is fun and different and it encourages interest in space, but the long term playability is questionable.

I thought this game would be a cool, new game to play with the younger ones in my family. And who doesn't love space? I played this game with my 6 year old nephew. He was interested only for a little while but got bored with the real rules of the game and started making up some of his own. The rules are pretty easy to understand though. And I could see it being fun for some children.

The boards feel pretty durable, as long as the kids aren't too rough with them. But there are some pieces to this game that could get lost. It's an okay game, definitely not the worst children's game out there, but I certainly don't think it's the best.

This is a neat game perfect for the kiddies.
Your goal is to get the most points by reaching the end.
Along the way you encounter different obstacles.
My nephews and niece really enjoy this game, a nice change of pace from the usual WII and Game Boy stuff they usually like to play.
Once I showed them the rules on how to play the game, the picked it up quite fast.
Very glad we have this game in our house.

Race through space is a great introduction game to logic, strategy, and board game mechanics for the younger gaming generation. We play this game with my friend's 6 year old son and he loves it. The game is simple to play, once you decide on your own house rule interpretations of when to start moving the game board. The board is printed on thick stock and the colors are vibrant. The art is fun and the theme definitely caught their son's attention. I much prefer playing this one over candyland and chutes and ladders type games, but if you are looking for something that you would enjoy playing strictly as an adult, keep looking.

The only real gripe I have with the game is the rules are a bit ambiguous, especially when it comes to the board moving mechanic. We found it worked best to move the bottom piece up to the top *after* the first person took their turn. That will make more sense once you go through your first round. Family game night just got a bit more interesting. ;)

The game has a few rules to learn but once you get the hang of it, it was quite fun. Basically you need to get your ships to the end of the puzzle to get points, the first ship to reach gets the most points and each ship after gets 1 less. As roll your die and move your ships you can focus on 1 ship or all 3 ships. The board constantly shifts as the pieces slowly rotate, if you are caught at the bottom your ship is out of play and you cannot get any points for it.

I like this game because it allows different strategies of managing your ships, removing your opponent ships, and the order your ships reach the end.

"Rcae through Space" is a board game for kids, but rather than simply moving your playing pieces based on the number on your dice roll, there are a few other events that take place. This makes the game more interesting and gives the kids some strategies to think about. However, some of these strategies/events are not good for small kids (The game's recommended age is 6+).

The board consists of 10 galaxy pieces and one moon piece (target). Each player has 3 rockets and you start on the 4th galaxy piece (6 board pieces away from the moon) and move towards the moon based on your dice roll. There is an asteroid belt to cross through (You wait a turn - that's all). The dice has the numbers 1 - 5 and an arrow symbol. If you roll a number, you move one of your rockets that many spaces and with the arrow symbol, you can either move your rocket forward to join your other rocket closest to the moon or move your opponents rocket backwards to the farthest rocket. Similarly, at the end of each round (each player has rolled the dice once), you move the piece farthest from the moon and move it closest to the moon - all rocket pieces on the "new" farthest piece go out of the game. So these two new strategies make the game interesting - however, when my 9 yr old and his friends (ages: 6-9) played the game, moving the pieces around at the end of each round was a mess - rockets were disloadged from the game boards and they had to move things around the table etc. similarly, 6 yr olds couldn't take losing their rockets off the board completely and had trouble with their pieces being moved backwards by someone else.

In my opinion, the game could be improved with the following changes.

1. Using magnetic strips or velcro, the rocket pieces have to be "attached" to the board pieces so that they don't fall off when the board pieces are moved around.

2. The players should be allowed to move multiple rockets each round - splitting the dice roll number between different rockets (teaches addition and includes another level of strategy).

3. Moving opponents backwards could be eliminated since this seems to promote "negative" strategy - winning by messing with other players - not a good value to teach a 6 year old.

The board pieces (made with linen-cardboard pieces) and other game components are of very high quality e.g. nice wooden dice. So the game would last a long time and no more bent corners on these pieces.

This game is a lot of fun. It really isn't that confusing to figure out (as I have noticed some reviewers have said). The object is to try and get all your rockets to the moon, and to NOT fall into the black hole. After each round (after each player takes a turn), the board piece at the end is removed and placed at the top, by the moon. The board is moving throughout the whole game, and if your rockets don't move quick enough, they will fall off the board into the black hole and be out for the rest of the game!

This game is fun and imaginative with cute, colorful space pictures on each board piece. It is easy to play (hard floor or a tabletop is much easier than carpet to play on, since you will be sliding the board after each round), includes some chance (rolling the die) and some strategy. We really enjoyed this fun and original game. Will be a family favorite!

This game has way too many parts to it! Even the main boards are split so you have more than one board to try to keep together. My ten year-old grandson lost a few pieces the first time he attempted to play.

Be prepared to track the pieces when playing so they don't get lost and have plenty of table space to play it. More complicated than I originally thought and grandson lost interest quickly. If this had maybe been a computer game he would've been more interested.

This is a quick, fun board game that does require that players know and understand the rules before playing. While the rules are not complicated, they are not intuitive and the game isn't much fun unless it's played the way it was designed to be played.

The game board consists of several boards that shift as the game is played. This makes the game much more challenging as the pieces move up the board toward the finish. It is possible for none of the players to win if they all fall into the "black hole." The game board is made of sturdy cardboard with a colorful game surface. The playing pieces consist of colored plastic rockets and a set of two dice. The dice are specific to the game. The youngest player goes first and is in charge of shifting the game board at the start of each turn.

I first handed this game to a couple middle-school children and asked them to play it. They didn't bother to read the directions and played the game in about 3 minutes. They said it wasn't much fun. I then read the directions, explained the directions to them, and challenged them to play again. They were clearly enjoying this "new" version and, when finished with the first game, immediately played a second. Each round took less than 10 minutes which was well within their attention spans. It would be a good game for kids to play while waiting for dinner or in a classroom where there is limited time between lessons or activities.

This game is meant for children 7 & up. The plastic game pieces could pose a choking hazard for younger children. Also, the game surface is not waterproof so seating glasses and pop cans should be kept away from the game.

B006ZPO5AK.text: Rating this a four stars as it is costly and probably an appliance box would work better. However, I like the fact that it has windows and such already cut out and that you can color it. My grandson (4) loved it when I set it up with my son and spent hours (before coloring) playing the 'king'. Again, it is attractive looking, but is lightweight and will not probably hold up with multiple kids inside. But for one child playing alone (or with their parents), it's great. Good imaginative playing for hours and the coloring and personalizing make it worth the cost.

It is nice that it can be stored flat, compared to regular playhouses that take up a ton of room and there is no way to disassemble . The quality is fine. It is what it is - cardboard - so it is not going to be as strong as plastic of course. If you have kids who play very roughly, then it could be a problem for this castle. This was the only reason I took off a star. Still it is a great option for someone who wants a fun playhouse and doesn't want to spend $300.

We were very excited about this gift for our 4 year old who loves playing "castle" and loves to color/paint. It's easy to assemble and I think cardboard reinforcement is going to give a lot longer life. Unfortunately though,  ours arrived blank with no pictures to color in. Very disappointed.

Worst purchase ever!!! Not only did it not go together without bending and breaking, it is not sturdy at all. My kids would have had more fun with a plain old cardboard box. Hard to believe this can even be sold for more than a few bucks. So disappointed!

This is a very simple. . . very easy to put-together "castle". But I have to say. . . it's a bit on the expensive side, being that it's just cardboard.
