We would have been better off using appliance boxes, as they are more sturdy.  This cardboard is so thin and flimsy that I have had to bring in the duct tape to stabilize it, and that takes away from the area that children can decorate (and duct tape looks bad).  However, without my duct tape reinforcements, it wouldn't hold up.  I wouldn't recommend purchasing this, it's just not worth it.

I bought this on flash deal, buying it at just around 20 bucks. I would not recommend spending more on this - although I've noticed at times it’s $35 or more… so definitely wait until it is a flash deal or deal of the day!

My kids are all between the ages of four and eight and I was surprised that it mostly captured the attention of my five year olds. They wanted to play in it and hide in it and only colored on it the first five or 10 minutes. They lost interest in the coloring design and just wanted to play, which surprised me!

In terms of set up, it was very easy to put together and took less than five minutes. It was pretty durable and held up well during play. I could see this lasting a while, especially if kept indoors.

Truth be told, it’s really just a glamorous cardboard box. But the kids had fun so I’m happy we gave it a try! I’m including a photo just to provide a closer look at what to expect, hope that helps!

Comes in plain brown box - so not exciting to open for birthday boy. Unlike similar kits from Alex toys, this is just plain cardboard, no design printed on it to enhance play. Fun for a little while, but disposable.
Great fun! My Grandson absolutely loves it, and it is incredibly sturdy!

My daughter LOVES this and has covered every single inch in paint, drawings, stickers, glued gems, etc. I’m seriously considering buying the other cardboard structures, as this was her absolute favorite Christmas present that is now her favorite little spot to hang :)

My daughter LOVES this and has covered every single inch in paint, drawings, stickers, glued gems, etc. I’m seriously considering buying the other cardboard structures, as this was her absolute favorite Christmas present that is now her favorite little spot to hang :)

So far it’s survived a week with my two and six year old boys. They love it. I like that it doesn’t have a roof so they aren’t too tall to stand in it. The directions are worse then Ikea directions but we figured it out. We also used packing tape to reinforce the parts we had to fold on each other.
Grandchildren loved it. I would definitely buy it again.
One side wasn't aligned so it didn't go together very well. Unless I taped it I could see my son breaking it apart within minutes.

I bought this for my son for Christmas. He’s a rough three-year-old boy. I read the reviews about securing the inside seems with duct tape which really helped. Santa put all of his presence inside of his castle.The castle has been standing for two months now. Well worth the money if you make sure that you reinforce the inside with duct tape.

This was a big hit with the grandkids, ages 4 and 2 as well as with the parents who enjoyed how easy it was to set up! It lends itself to all kinds of imaginative play and is especially welcome now that the weather is wet and cold and outdoor play is not as attractive. A great buy.

This large cardboard playhouse is a great idea, and brings kids back to the days when a box and some markers are all it takes to be entertained for an afternoon. Assembly is simple, no tools required other than perhaps some packing tape to reinforce some parts.

Once assembled, the whole thing is rather flimsy. Its size makes it suitable for kids up to around 5 years old. Above that, and the castle is just too small.

That said, despite the fun concept and good design, there is no way I can give this product anything higher than 3 stars. It is essentially nothing more than a perforated and folded cardboard box - $2 in parts (at most), and retailing this at just under $40 is a major disappointment. With a couple of old boxes from things like a TV or washing machine, you'll have more fun as you can actually MAKE the caste instead of just assembling it. Alternatively, get some moving boxes at Home Depot for $3 each and you'll be able to create something far more entertaining (and much larger).

At $15 this would have been a 5 star product, but with its current price point and mediocre stability, it gets three stars.
I recommend getting some 1/2” strips of wood and glue them at the top walls, makes a big difference on sturdiness
Broke too easy
It's cardboard so don't expect much. My kids played with it for a bit and then got tired of it.

I found this castle flimsy when putting it together. I realize it is cardboard, but even after following the instructions of assembly, this product was wobbly and very unstable.  I would have been better off going to an appliance store and asking if they had a box they would be willing to give away.  I would not recommend this product.
Literally just a cardboard box cut into the shape of a castle. Super flimsy but kids don’t care so I don’t care. They have a blast playing in this thing.

Not well built. Buy the discovery brands in the store. The cottage we bought years ago was much better quality thicker cardboard. This fir $40 is very flimsy and cheap

Wish we had bought the discovery cottage Agsin
You may as well toss your money into the fire and watching it burn. After that, make a box fort in the traditional way.

My son was very excited to get inside once built, and he also absolutely loved drawing and coloring on the outside.  It was worth it for several hours over multiple days worth of entertainment.  It is VERY flimsy though once put together.  I’m saying this in comparison to a similar cardboard house that was much sturdier.  It got beat up and fell apart faster as well.  It was a bit of a pain to put together, only because the tabs don’t easily slide in place, but at least it was all one piece.  I may have cursed it out a few times during the assembly, but I would still buy the castle again for the amount of creative play my son was able to get out of it.
Bought it for my granddaughters for Christmas and they love coloring it and will love playing in it too. Great item
Great gift for young kids - can play in it, draw on it and its okay if it gets messed up bc its cardboard....nice filler for Christmas or "big" feeling gift for birthday

Update 9/14/15:

My 2 year old has played with this house almost every day. I find the doorways to be a little tiny, he has to duck down to enter, but he has loved this castle. It has dropped in price and I would probably invest in this price point ($30 versus the original $45). I did duct tape, but it still ended up a heap on the floor, literally flat on the floor. When my husband started saying it was time for it to go, I got out my thinking cap and reinforced the playhouse using scrap pieces of cardboard and my hot glue gun (please see the attached picture). Needless to say, it's better than new. When we first put it together the cardboard was flimsy in some places from being bent in shipping. Hopefully, we should get a little more play out of this cardboard box. I'm still leaving it at 3 stars because I had to modify and reinforce it. It's been a good play item and has gotten lots of use. Neither of my children have been interested in decorating it.

My two boys love cardboard playhouses. We recently moved and had to get rid of our Snoopy themed cardboard house, because it wasn't worth moving it. The boys were so upset. We had that house for well over a year. Yes, it had its fair share of duct tape, but it was well made, still standing, and played with everyday. And, that is my main issue with this castle. It is double the price I paid for the last cardboard house, and it's not the same quality. This castle will definitely not last a year. Yes, I know cardboard structured toys are not meant to last, but at this price point, it really should be better quality.
I'm on the fence about whether or not it should have pre-printed decorations to color. At least it can be decorated and tailored to your child's imagination for either a girl or a boy. However, my son, who is the oldest and was an only child for many years, has difficulty with using his imagination. He is very much a rule follower, doesn't like to make mistakes, and somewhat of a perfectionist. Therefore, coloring the castle was challenging for him. He would have rather had bricks to color or some type of print to follow the lines.
Overall, it's a great temporary playhouse, but flimsy and I wouldn't purchase again at this price point.

Love love love this play castle! We got this for my daughter's birthday party full of preschoolers and rougher cousins and it is still standing and looks great! So easy to assemble, the kids loved the working doors, and the parents loved joining in on the coloring too. Great interactive party activity and for afterward, too.

I gave this as a Christmas gift to 2 kids, 4 and 5. It was easy to assemble and gave a lot of space to color. Mom & Dad loved it too. Keeps them busy coloring inside and out....and what kids don't love a castle.
Instead of buying two lame gifts this was perfect!
We like it!!!

easy setup. good quality cardboard. my daughter loves that she can draw on it and stick all her stickers on it. we love it because she does not
need to instead draw on our furniture

I have 5 grandkids 6 and under, and I thought this would be great to have them color and play in. My 4 grandsons colored a bit, so my granddaughter and I more or less finished using markers to color most of the outside. It is really easy to color, and would be fun to do as a party activity for kids and assemble after it was done. I had bought two, thinking I could put them together to accommodate everyone, but decided in the end to just do one and have it join a pop up tent we had. It stayed inside since it is made of cardboard. Kids had a great time going in and out, and decorated it later on for St. Patrick's day as a leprechaun trap! I still have my second playhouse to use in a few years so the young grandkids can enjoy it again!

This is an awesome purchase fo little ones of all ages. My daughter happily spent a few weeks in one-hour sessions coloring the various features on the castle and currently her stuffed animals have taken up residence. It's also collapsible so you can always take it down to reclaim your living room, etc. Well worth the money and a great activity!
My niece love it! It’s bigger than I thought!
This was not worth the money in my opinion. I don’t know how you could draw on it bc it would fall over
This thing has been hours of fun for my daughter.  When the outside gets all colored in you can flip it inside out and start the process all over!

We used this at my daughter's birthday party! Entertainment for all ages!

First off, the girls loved the play castle.  They were so excited to get it.  They decorated it to look like the castle in Frozen (or so they say).  I knew it was cardboard, so I didn't expect it to be really sturdy and it's not.  If you have kids that play kind of rough, don't expect this to last long.  If you have a child that just wants to sit inside and play with dolls or action figures, this may last a bit.  Ours has already collapsed though and we've had it less than a month.
Came together in minutes. Fun canvas for the kids.
Great gift! Bought the castle for my five year old daughter and loved it so much I bought the garage as a birthday gift to my nephew!

Way too expensive for what it is! It doesn’t even stay up very well so as soon as kids try to color on it, it collapses! Got torn up when kids went in and out to play in it! Ended up in the trash! Don’t waste your money!
I bought it as a gift and both parents and child was happy with it.

I gave this to our niece for her 2 young kids... she said:

"Our two girls, ages five and three, had a lot of fun playing with this cardboard castle. They moved all their special toys in and played house for hours. It was easy for me to assemble. I thought the product was a little flimsy (a few of the corners didn't hold together well). The cardboard was thin and light weight. In my opinion, it should be a bit more sturdy for the price, given that it is designed for kids to go in and out of a lot.

My kids love to color and immediately wanted to decorate their castle. It would have enhanced the design if there had been decor on the outside for them to beautify. It was a lot of blank, white space for them to fill.

Overall, the castle is a fun concept but not a product on which I'd be willing to spend much money on."
My grandson loves it. Got it for his birthday and all the adults got in on coloring the great design. Easy to take apart and put back together. Highly recommend.

This cardboard is not sturdy. The connecting slots do not fit snuggly so it is constantly falling apart. As you can see the squares on top of the castle collapse instead of staying square. The picture on the card board is good quality and the idea is cute it just needs to be a made with better cardboard. My girls still like coloring it but it’s a hassle because every time I move it or it falls apart my girls ask me to put it together again. We were even more disappointed because the bankers box at play unicorn house we had as our first coloring house was such better quality and the same price. If you want to take the time to reinforce it could possibly last longer. It comes in a giant card board box I was originally going to cut into pieces to tape on to the weak folds in the castle but I never got around to it.
perfect!

I always assume melissa and doug products are aimed at children, but this may be for a slightly older child.  I could barely balance these thing myself. The kids love it when I mess up! Most of the kids really like it. I like the one reviewer's suggestion of add-on pieces and different bases.  I am convinced this was invented by a couple of guys with a 12 pack and a bunch of wire coat hangers.

I wanted this over Christmas last year but the only way to get it was online and everyone was out of stock it seemed like. This game is so much fun for 3 or more people. I did order 2 sets for when the holidays roll around.

My son has Nystagmus and only had a slight problem adjusting to play the game. Hey he adjusted so well he managed to win 2 games:)
Fun, I have been playing before I give away

Over a year ago I picked this up for my always-busy son who simply cannot stop moving and learning. I think we have played it the "right" way maybe five times but it's been pulled out and enjoyed a thousand times over. My son makes "lightning rods" and "electrical lines" with them and occasionally electrocutes nearby building block towers, completely demolishing them. (Boys!) It is a very unique game that catches the interest of just about everyone who sees it - adults and children alike - and I owe this game many thanks for letting me get dinner cooked or a phone call made in pure, blissful silence!

[[VIDEOID:1f2a3c880a660ba73bcdaf865374ae12]] How to set up your Syma X1 before first flight. I go through the following steps quickly in the video:

1) Place a charged LiPo battery into the slide rails on the bottom of the copter, but not all the way in.
2) Place the copter in normal top-side-up position on a flat surface.
3) THEN push in the copter battery completely. The red LED in the copter will flash (4 Hz). Do not move the copter from the flat surface.
4) The flashing stops for about 2 seconds. I believe at this point the initialization of gyroscopes, stabilization algorithms, etc. has completed. The copter has just learned where "level" is for this flight.
5) Next the red LED the copter will flash quickly. If you have not yet bound the copter to the transmitter, the following steps must be completed while the copter is flashing quickly to bind the copter and the transmitter. If binding has already been completed previously, timing is not important (transmitter can be turned on any time after the fast flashing starts) but the steps are the same to complete the connection between copter and transmitter:
a) Start with transmitter off and the throttle (left stick) all the way down.
b) If you want to switch from Mode 1 to Mode 2 (or from Mode 2 to Mode 1), push the fine tuning switch below the right joystick to the right as you turn on the transmitter.
c) Turn on power to the transmitter.
d) Push the throttle (left stick) all the way up then all the way down. You will hear a long beep from the transmitter.

The binding between the copter and the transmitter performed in step 5 seems to be persistent across copter and transmitter power cycles and battery changes. The transmitter also maintains Mode and Trim settings across power cycles and battery changes.

After step 5 you will know the copter and the transmitter are communicating correctly when lights are on steady (no flashing) on both the copter (red) and on the transmitter (blue).

Steps 1-4 must ALWAYS be done before each flight. If the copter darts off in random directions (especially after performing a level rotation-only maneuver), there's a good chance it's because the gyros weren't initialized properly. The key is to place the copter on a level surface BEFORE inserting the battery.

I've given the Syma X1 4 stars because it's a lot of fun, but 1 star deducted because the instructions are unclear, and in the case of how to set up the copter preflight, just plain wrong.

So, this is the second one of these that I've ordered; the first was for my nephew. After flying it a bit with him, I decided to give it a try on my own. This is probably the best quadcopter value out there, though I do say this based on other reviews and not my own experience with multiple makes and models. For about $40, you get a very capable quad-copter that you can fly left/right, forward/reverse, up/down, as well as rotate it 360 to keep the "front" of the copter oriented properly, so you're not pushing the controller left and having the unit bank right. It also has a "eversion" mode that basically flips the copter 360 degrees in a loop automatically. This function works left/right and forward/backward, and is very cool,primarily because it's so easy to execute the maneuver.

The unit has a Low and High setting, which trims the controls a bit on the Low setting, and makes for a very good indoor mode while the High setting is best for outdoors and stunt moves. There are trim controls for the throttle, rotation, left/right and forward/back. I've found that the trim does work, and is best adjusted when the copter is outside and has some height off the ground...essentially, you try to hover it and see how best to adjust the controls. Ideally, if you let off the controls, the unit should hover fairly well. The system has no "auto" hover mode that'll auto-adjust the trims to hover, so getting it dialed in is still a manual affair. The controls work well, and I've flown this for maybe an hours indoors and 30 minutes outside, and feel as if I have good control of the thing.

I've found this to be a very sturdy unit, having crashed it numerous times in just about every orientation. It does come with a set of spare rotors, which is nice, however even after using this in a parking lot, I've not yet broken anything. The body of the unit, which offers some protection to the electronics (which then have another plastic dome atop them), comes in several types...bumble bee, UFO, spaceship, etc. Ideally, you might be able to fly w/o it, shaving off some weight and possibly some air resistance, though the fairing does offer some protection and probably shouldn't be removed until you're past the beginner stages.

The battery lasts 8-10 minutes, depending upon how you're flying it. I've found they last more outdoors, probably because you're not making so many direction adjustments. You can get extra batteries and chargers, and I'd recommend it, as 10 minutes isn't enough...you're going to want more. The batteries charge off a USB cable, whether plugged into a computer or using a USB/wall adapter. Charge time is about an hour, give or take.

The directions are just OK, and you'll have to experiment to really get a feel for things. The most important thing to remember is when starting off, you want to try and be on as level a surface as possible, as each time you insert the battery, the thing will auto-level and find it's artificial horizon. If you start off on a slope, you may find the unit won't fly very well, or you'll need to make significant trim adjustments.

The process to start the unit is as follows:

1. Ensure battery for the copter is out, and the remote is off.
2. Insert the battery and immediately place the copter on a flat surface. You should see the slow blinking LED under the fairing
3. Turn the remote on.
4. Move the throttle/rotate lever (on the left of the remote) up once (you'll hear a beep) and then down once (you'll hear a beep).
5. The copter LED should then stop blinking and remain steady RED. You're ready to go...
6. If the copter doesn't start, turn the remote off, then on, and repeat the process w/ the throttle (you shouldn't need to remove the battery). I find I need to do this process twice each time the batter is replaced.

If you crash the copter, you just need to right it, and start flying again...it will automatically reset, and there's nothing you need to do with the remote or unit to get things going again. The only exception to this is if the batter flies out when the crash occurs...then start from step 1 above.

The two things I'd probably change about this unit are to have some LED lights that show the "front" of the copter; as it is, the rotors are white in the front and black in the back...this does help. Secondly, the batter insert/removal is somewhat clunky, but it does work. I'd like to see something a little easier to work with, as getting the batter in and out can be a little difficult sometimes.

So...this is a great copter, and the perfect unit for a child, or an adult (I'm 39) to start off with quad-coptering. Enjoy.

-J

This is my first quadcopter, with limited previous RC helo experience on 2 and 3.5 channel micro and mini helicopters, both single rotor and co-axial. The instructions weren't great. Here's the simplified version: Charge the battery and insert, immediately after place the copter on a flat surface and turn on the controller with the throttle at half. Once the beeping goes from low pitch to a single high pitched beep and stops flashing blue, move the throttle to full and then to zero. You are now ready to fly. Trim it and you should be golden. I've crashed this thing many times and have found that by cutting the throttle whenever you lose control, damage is minimized. I've yet to actually break it and have had at least 20 flights (each time I get better.) It flies well indoors, and outdoors, even in light wind. Every part on here is replaceable. I recommend extra batteries. The battery is protected, but the charger is not, so make sure you have a safe battery/charger combo when selecting spares.

This is one little tough unit.
It is just unbelievable that this copter costs only $40. I bought a set of 600 mAh batteries that I keep charged to extend my flying experience.
A word of advise in case your gyro seems to be out of calibration. Make sure you set the copter on leveled ground immediately after you plug in the battery as the system goes through a boot sequence. I'm not 100% positive, but I believe the gyro goes into self-calibration during this process.

This is way boat-ier than the Ladybird micros. It's like driving an 80s Cadillac. The big draw for this item is the auto-flip button. Once you get it to bind correctly and hover straight, immediately start hitting the right button, using the right stick to telegraph which axis to turn on. I can flip this thing in four directions right in the middle of my small living room which is awesome. Great fun once you get the feel for it.

If you have yaw issues, most likely you didn't bind correctly. For me, I pop in the battery, toss it on the floor, turn on the TX, wait for the beeps and we're good. If I need to trim more than a click or two on any of the rotors, it didn't bind right and I start over. The bigger batteries are no problem--the binding process takes care of all that. I'd get some of those too.

This is a good model to learn on because it takes a huge beating without having to spend a lot on extra motors and props like the Ladybird. It's definitely able to take some abuse--which it's going to get if you're new to this! Also, despite being bigger than the micros, because the motors are somewhat underpowered for the weight, it probably won't do any damage.

This copter is AWESOME, but it may be a little too difficult for some beginners to fly. I'd go with one of the Syma S107 copters for beginners. I've had both, and while both are fun to fly, the X1 is more exciting, but also more difficult to fly. I imagine some beginners may get frustrated not being able to properly control the X1, especially in closed areas.

Tips:
#1 - When you're about to run into something or crash, cut power to the props and just let the copter fall. This will preserve your X1 far longer than if you keep spinning while running into something.

#2 - I found that following the instructions didn't work for me to sync the X1 with the remote control. I turn the remote on first, then put the battery in the X1. From there, I do the up/down on the remote, and sometimes have to turn the remote off then on again with the up/down. Doing it exactly as the instructions say, however, wasn't working for me.

#3 - Learn how to do the barrel roll (see instructions). It's AWESOME!

I've flown many quadcopters, including micro ones that cost $30 and worked better than this one.
First, the init is non obvious and doesn't self reset, next, asking me to put power up and down to init is the stupidest thing. If I do it twice by mistake, the quad will takeoff straight up and potentially hit something.

Flying in easy mode is so slow to respond to controls that's it's only for very beginners. It will not let you fly against a light breeze (i.e. you'll lose the quad as it flies farther from you unless you switch to B quickly).
The more responsive B mode isn't great either. It's very slow to respond and doesn't self level quickly when you let go of the input. If you go straight left and then straight right, it takes multiple seconds before it goes from left to level and then level to right and finally stops flying right. This makes aggressive left/right flying mostly not possible.
Worse, if I fly up, cut the power, and resume power, it could resume flying sideways even though I have no left/right/fwd/back input.
Basically the control logic is just not good and totally beaten by a $30 micro quad copter I bought on amazon
Copter seems OK, but the instructions are really poorly written, and appear to be for a slightly different model of copter.  Seems to have a problem with the controls that I'm still working out.

This Quad Copter isn't easy to control, but that's just because "it takes a steady hand".  I have gotten better each time I fly it, and have had consistently longer flights that the first few times that were only seconds long!  You DEFINITELY don't want to be flying this on a breezy/windy day.  The calmer, the better!  That being said, this little thing is FUN!

I've used these twice, once for a 1000 piece puzzle and once with a 750 piece puzzle. The 1000 piece I had already started, but it was helpful to contain different colors in each tray so I could work out of one tray and not worry about the space for the rest of the pieces. By the time I got down to the last 100 pieces or so, I could sort the pieces by shape into each tray.

The 750 piece puzzle I used the trays right from the start. I sorted all the edge pieces into one tray and then by color the rest. You couldn't have a single layer, but the trays did contain all the pieces and still stacked when I was not working on the puzzle. I really was able to work out of each tray quite easily.

The final reason I really like these trays is that they stack on top of one another and can even store with the pieces in the box if I needed to. I have a cat. The 1000 piece puzzle half ended on the floor one evening due to the cat jumping on the table and knocking it all over. I lost several pieces for about 3-4 days before I eventually found them all. That is when I purchased this. For this reason alone, I really recommend these trays.

This kit comes with the dice and score sheets (naturally), the instructions, a shaker cup (metal, I'm guessing tin, and very cute) and Yahtzee bonus chips. I never knew there were bonus chips in Yahtzee, for if you roll a second Yahtzee, and none of my friends seemed to know it either. Or that Yahtzee could be used as a joker. In the 50's and 60's Board Games and Cards were very popular. I remember playing Yahtzee in the 60's mainly with older family than with friends. The older people in the 50's and 60's loved cards- my Mother's friends had Bridge Clubs and the men loved their Poker Nights. I always felt Yahtzee was a combination of a board type game using dice combined with the skill of cards.

The object of Yahtzee is to get the most points by figuring out the points the dice will give you with 3 of a kind, large straight, full house, aces and other card type combinations. You get three chances to roll the most points you can figure out. You really had to figure out which dice would get you more points on the upper section or the lower section of your score card to score high. They even included chips in the game, as you could get a chip for every 100 points you score.

When you roll the 5 dice all the same number, that was Yahtzee. It's nice to see Classic games coming around again to enjoy. For anyone who likes the strategy of playing cards, only with rolling 5 dice, Yahtzee brings that and more to this classic 50's game of both skill and chance.

Just the right size for her dresser. Glow in the dark paint must need a few coats to works. We love it though.
Thanks.

The kids love each having their own moon. Very bright, no dead bugs. I wish the moon would focus a little better without becoming super loose when you twist it, but the kids don't really notice that much. Overall, super cool.
Pretty cool! Was a stocking stuffer for my 6 y/o son.
A little too detailed for the 6 year old.  Likely very fun for a somewhat older child.

This product was a lot smaller than I imagined, I should’ve read the dimensions. I don’t mind the size but the picture isn’t clear at all, no matter how close or far away you are. The moon is blurry, my son is almost 3 and he broke it within an hour of having it. The button broke on it. It’s a neat toy for a child who loves the moon but honestly, I’d prefer to buy a more quality product next time.
My grandson loved it. Was the perfect gift
Fun great gift

Doesn’t work well.
Great purchase! My 2-year-old loves it.

It works well and is well put together. We have already had a few hours worth of play with it.

Bought this as a stocking stuffer and it stole the show on Christmas morning. Even adults thought it was "super cool". Came packaged on a cardboard peggable card, substantial enough for a stocking stuffer or grouped with other item(s) as a gift. Came with a beaded chain around the end of the flashlight to hook onto other items.
My nephew loved this!
I thought this would be a fun stocking stuffer and it was while it lasted. Only worked for 2 weeks and now every time we wind it up it just slides off the fridge.
4 year old loves it!  You do have to shine it on something pretty close up though, otherwise all the detail is lost
My daughter washed this accidentally, as it was left in a pocket. I had to order a second one as it was a hit! Great toy for little astronomers!
Fun tochky to have on the fridge.

This was a gift, and the child was excited and assembled it easily. She enjoys teaching and learning kits. She loves to learn about the moon and stars, so this was a great lead in for further learning.

The planet halves don’t fit together properly … the sandpaper is not the proper grit and is very ineffective for the large extra piece of plastic you’re supposed to sand. Some of the planets are the exact same size so if you’re trying to get specific with arrangement it’s a bit funky.

Overall okay.

The planets  are really really small but my girls loved painting them. They enjoyed the activity a lot and while they painted we reviewed what we had already learned about them (I homeschool). My girls are 5 and 6. I would definitely recommed.

So first off this thing is super tiny.  I was embarrassed for my kid when I got it in and we had to actually use it because it was a last minute thing. Also there is NO PLUTO.  And yes I know that it's up in the air and one day there's a planet name Pluto and the next day there's not. However with a fourth grader Pluto is to be included in their projects. There is no way to add a planet to this thing so you're kind of just up a creek if you need the planet Pluto. It's very flimsy and very very small, my daughter's teacher was not impressed at all.
The boys really like it
What a fun science expirament with magnets
This kit is great when you are just looking for a simple easy inexpensive solar system. My son is 11 and he was able to do all himself.
Very cheap and not big enough to use as a helpful teaching model
Super fun!! We have 2 of these on our fridge. Everyone who comes over always plays with these kids to adults!
I purchased 3 of these for Christmas gifts and they went nuts over them!!!

I like this gift set for its unique 3-D quality. It easy to do if given to an older kid. I gave it to a cute 4 year old girl but she has difficulty painting the teeny tiny planets. However, she got overjoyed when she put the assembled, painted solar system in the dark and found it glowing in the dark!
The 4M Solar System Planetarium was just what my grandson wanted, and it met his expectation.
The children have had fun with this toy,
kids loved this.  Bought 2 and had one stashed in the closet, perfect for the imprompteau birthday gift!

Still have not put this together (2/6/16, bought it for Christmas 2015) as it is more complicated than originally anticipated.  Definitely not for younger kids, lots of super small pieces, gluing and sanding involved--more like an actual model instead of snap-together kinds.  Older kids may enjoy it more as they have better ability to have the patience for it, and definitely something parents need to help with!
The children we gave it to loved it!

This is a fun product for a young child. It will stop at corners. I wish it was smarter and could turn and stay on the surface running longer. It only goes in a straight line. Still, for the price it's fun for a t least a short time.

So for the price (less than a ten-er) this is very nice.  I would have preferred something that didn't require so much effort on my part as this was intended for my 5 year old daughter.  The supplies provided though were sufficient and easy enough to use.  My only issue is that it's not clear which planet needs to join up with which size stand attachment (they are not all the same height). As such, the planets don't necessarily revolve around the sun so smoothly without bumping into each other.

B00BNWI4WA.text: part of a number of VTech smart wheels (5 in all.. planes, cars, cop cars, etc)  I purchased for my grandson's 3rd bday.  They are made of apparently tough plastic...the colors are bright and cheerful... fairly heavy for what they are... I think they will survive a few trips down the stairs... they are pretty loud... I was kind of surprised.  I mean, you won't need earplugs or anything.. but they do ramble on loudly a bit longer than I would like.  Ha.  But they live at Mommy and Daddy's house so that is ok.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.
Gift

My 20 month old loves these VTech cars.  I love that you can turn them on and off.  They are pretty loud..a lower volume would have been preferred, but the off switch works too when the noise is too much.
We love all of these cars! They make noise and light up and make playing with the track an even more interactive experience!
Another wonderful v tech purchase . All the sets go together and function well.
My son enjoys moving the cars on the roads and he likes that he can make them talk by pushing the button on the vehicle or by driving it around.  The only down side is they can't move on their own.
grandson loved it
not self propelled like some of their other products
Works well on the V tech train set we got our daughter for Christmas.  It goes around the track just as well as the car that came with the set.
This was brought for a two year old boy. Out of all the gifts he received he plays with this the most.
Great Grandson (!year) loves it
Product arrived in not working condition.  Possible quality issues?  There was no damage to the box.

This little car is the perfect size for little hands. I bought this for my grandson (15 months) and he has played with it more than
gifts that were very pricey. I love seeing him rolling this around on kitchen floor. This car plays a number of different songs as
it rolls. It features a off button on the bottom if you desire "quiet" play. The windsheild lights up and comes complete with batteries.
A happy feature for me :) This car is compatible with the VTech Go Track. The car is well built and free of defect. A great bargin
for the price of this toy. I am very happy with my purchase.
Gift
The songs get kinda annoying but I will deal since it is a small toy that both my 8m & 4yo like. They have a bunch & share them.

My son, 19 mos, likes to push the button because it makes car sounds. It also makes sounds when it goes over checkpoints on his actual VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels tracks (sold separately). Apparently there are these tiny protrusions on the bottom that push in when you roll the car over the checkponts which have slight elevations to them. Overall, we like this toy.
Came just as described.

Bought this car to add to the Vtech fast track launcher.  It is very cute and well made.  The voice is clear and the car is easy to handle.  Our one year old grandson enjoyed playing with this car.  Our son said that the racers are in sync because when one is talking, the others chime in.  That could be annoying.  Looking forward to adding to his collection for next year.  Fast shipping and SUPER price.

It fits the track perfectly. I was under the impression that these cars move on its on. Like the train that came with the train set. These additional cars are push yourself toys. My son plays with it without the track because easier on the floor than the track.
favorite toy!

My 16 month old son owns several of these, including a ambulance that sings in French (purchased in Quebec). He got his first at 10 months and several more for Christmas. He loves them all. Sometimes I turn them on, other times I do not. He doesn't care either way. He loves to drive them around the house, stare at them, spin the wheels, manipulate any other moving parts, or just press the windscreen to see what songs it might sing. I also love that they sing completely different things when on their tracks (there's at least dozen different sounds on all of them).

My only gripe and the reason I won't give five stars is the volume. We have around six of these and some of them are quiet whereas others are almost deafening. Now I don't mind noisy toys, but my son (like all small children) likes to hold his toys close to his face and sometimes chew on them. There is no way some of these meet the noise guidelines for hearing safety in children's toys. As a result some of them don't get turned on and that's a shame. I know V-Tech isn't great about adhering to volume restrictions but it's weird the problem only exists in some of his cars and not others. Seems like it might be more of a quality control issue as the batteries are fine on all of them.
My grandsons love this

I bought this for my great grandson who is 21/2 years old.  He has almost the entire set of VTech smart wheels and he LOVES them.  This is a gift I will give proudly.  This arrived packaged well and in a timely manner.

this thing is unbearably loud! It is far far louder than the train of the same series that we have. There is no volume switch. It's awful. Thankfully my 2-year-old is not terribly interested in it otherwise it would definitely top the "most annoying" list.
good toy
The merchandise arrived on time and in good condition, but I was expecting a bigger car.  Any way, it is a cute little car and the lights turn which entertains the kids very much.
A great addition to the VTech Go sets we have. My kids love them. Like others have said it doesn't move on its own - it has to be pushed. And it is loud but does have an off switch on the bottom.

Our son loves vehicles and this was part of his Christmas gift.  He loves it!  The sound is a bit loud for us so we added a piece of packaging tape over the speakers.  Still loud enough for him when playing, but doesn't overwhelm everything else in the room.
This was for a stocking stuffer.  I loved the lights and sounds that it made when it was turned on.
Just what I wanted & needed...

We have just about every vehicle and set from this line of toys (thanks to Christmas and birthdays for 2 boys being back to back).  My kids love these toys.  We don't leave them set up all the time because all of the sets together are huge, but when we do set them up, it's hours of playing at a time, which mommy and daddy love!
It's really loud
Great...
excellent product excellent service
My 2 year old son loves all these little cars/trains! And it's so easy to turn the sound off when needed!

Perfect for age 9mts - 1
I'd give these 5 stars except they're very hard. My son loves to shake them and hear the sounds they make, but occasionally he's hit himself with them and doesn't like when that happens!
My 8 month old enjoys playing with these. Even her 2 year old brother will play with them too. The balls fall into the holes when stacked, making it easy to stack them.
My 9 month old loves playing with these rattling blocks! My older son sometimes tags along and plays with him too.
Good size for under one.  They are plastic...not foamy or soft.
Keeps baby entertained. He's fascinated with them. Easy for baby to play with these  blocks.
granson loves this sturdy no breakable pretty colors he loves to shake them and listen to the bells inside of them
I bought my nephew these,  he and my infant daughter both loved these.  The noise they make and the ball on the inside provides minutes (they are babies) of entertainment over and over.
Fun, durable, easy to stack.
My 9 month old daughters loves these!

Purchased these as a gift for my grandchildren (9-12 months).  Both of the babies really liked these.  They are colorful as well as interesting.  Easy for them to hold as well.  I would recommend this product.

I actually got these from a friend for my baby when I was pregnant. My LO is 6.5 months old and these have been her FAVORITE toy for the last month or so. I love that there's 3. I keep one in her room, one in the living room, and one in the diaper bag. She loves to just shake them. They're easy for her to grab and shake, withstand chewing, and I pop them in the dishwasher to clean them. They're glorious!

I looked up on Fisher's site for their toy selection for 6 months old, and this was on there. Qaulity is great, no sharp edges or seams in the different plastics. Best of all every time I see my niece she seems to have one of these in her hand. She loves to shake it and push it because the little rattles in the balls. She seems to like it, so 5 stars it is.
GRANDSON LOVES THEM

My 6 month old son loves these!  They are easy for him to hold and he loves to shake them.  It's great that they make noise and are also easy to stack.  Great design and product.  I'm very happy with this purchase.
Nice for building and making noise.
My 6-month-old grandson loves these! Perfect for his little chubby hands.

I would have given 5 stars but we only received 2 blocks! Just arrived today before nap time but 7-mo old grandson put one in each hand and shook them and seemed to really enjoy them. These are fun and colorful blocks for babies that have learned to hold things. They are easy to grab with the cutout holes around them and will keep them thinking with the balls that are inside. My 7 month old grandson really likes them.
My little one LOVES these.  They are a nice size so he can handle them easily.
Cute blocks. Nice size for baby hands.
loved the blocks.
Baby loves shaking and throwing these. Overall it's a good buy!
Love it love it love it! Stable and fun sounds, little hidden pictures and all different colors. So educating and fun

These seemed like they would be a great toy, but my daughter was not too interested. They are well made and surely a toy some babies would find entertaining. I'm a huge fan of Fisher Price toys and equipment so far, these just didn't do the trick for my daughter.

I bought these for my son 2 months ago & they are still his favorite toy to play with. He crawls around carrying one, banging it on things or throwing it around the room. They are light enough to carry around, a nice size for little hands to grab onto & clean easy. I'm happy about getting them because my son crawls right to them every morning to play and picks them up throughout the day. The little ball inside moves around making noise too, which keeps my son wanting to bang them around to hear more noise!
They are super cute and pretty sturdy, but my baby gets frustrated trying to take out the balls out of the cubes.
Great toy for a great price. Good for kids learning to crawl or crawlers

Just opened the package today since my baby is about 4-1/2 months now.. He's playing with it and definitely seems to like the toy! He's able to grab it and move it around.. and apparently toss it to the ground (a new thing he's just learning). But he does love to reach for it and hold it!
My favorite baby toy
My 6 month old loved these because they fit into her little hand and she loves to rattle them they are a simple toy but really entertaining
My grandsons love this
My daughter loves loves loves it!

Quality wise these are okay, but these do not interest my child in the least. I think there are far better stacking blocks out there. The various textures are so small that a child really can't feel the difference. You can use them to teach about colors, but for the price I wouldn't purchase them for that. They are stackable blocks but they all sound so alike, which is kind of a waste if you ask me. I expected each block to represent different sounds.
Baby loves these

This is a cute toy I had purchased for my almost 8 month old, and he loves them! He can't stack them yet, but he can certainly knock them down when I stack them for him.

My son likes anything that makes a sound, plays music or that he can gnaw on. I try to make sure that I buy him toys that are good for his age now, but that will also help me reach milestones as he gets older. I'd say this is definitely a good developmental toy.

These stack very easily with the ball inside helping to lock in with the other blocks. This is very good feature, considering babies are not that coordinated yet.

These blocks were a great purchase for my 5 month old. She loves grabbing them and hearing the sounds, then knocking them over when we stack. We, the parents, love that they make simple rattling sounds and not annoying songs like almost every other toy does lately. We've been using these often for over three months and I expect them to be relevant for a while!

These cubes are absolutely fantastic.

Here are some key points :

1) My 7 month old immediately was able to grab them because they are cut out in the middle, her hands are not big enough yet to hold solid cubes.
2) The ball inside makes a nice pleasant sound
3) The balls also allow the three cubes to be interlocked
4) They are easy to clean
5) Unlike solid surface cubes, she has no problem grabbing them and tossing them around (apparently this is an important growing thing)
6) They are made of a hard plastic, resisting those little teeth from eating them

The only criticism I have is, why are there only three cubes... I suppose you can buy 2-3 sets, but that seems very expensive.

Nothing really wrong with it in terms of safety but our 6 month old baby had no interest with this toy. The ball inside just falls to the bottom while baby is naturally looking at the top. Doesn't even know the ball is really there until I hold it at the top. Preferred the squishy blocks or rattle. Will update review if anything changes.

Fisher-Price just knows babies. This is a rattle and an easy to grab toy for a 5 month old. I can see my baby using this toy for a while because it has that grow with the baby ability. At 5 months it's about grabbing and putting in the mouth. Now he's 6 months and it's about banging and putting in the mouth. Soon it'll be about stacking - probably putting in the mouth.

B00C2SJ7WU.text:
Grandson loved this plane. His parents not so much. The noise was being triggered continuously and now the battery is removed.
Definitely not the same as Bravo and Dusty but still fun for my Grandson. We weren't sure if the switch was sticking or the plane was suppose to be non-stop noise.
Something to think about when you purchase.
Christmas present for a Grandson..absolutely loved it…

It's a cute little plane, but the damn thing won't shut up! I pressed the button on the tail and it went through it's little recorded sequence. Unfortunately, the sequence just kept playing on repeat. Apparently it detects motion so the only way to shut it up is to shove it back into the packaging box where it's dark. I got this for a toy drive, but I don't want to put some poor little kid and his family through the annoyance of this stupid toy so back to amazon you go El Chupacabra.

My son likes the sounds, but this toy seems to be pretty behind on the sounds it makes vs. the movements that are made.

My Son still likes it, but becomes quickly bored with it.
Very cute and should be fun for a young child...... but the parents of the child I bought it for may kill me ,,, it's THAT loud!
Youngster sleeps with this FP Disney plane and plays with it constantly...very well made since he can tear up a rock!

I bought this more to aggravate my friends husband because its a little difficult to stop the recorded voice. But overall I'm pleased with the construction and quality. It does take some flying skill ;) to land the plane so he'll be quite. Overall a good deal.

I got it for my daughter on Christmas.
She really loves it.
We bough 20 pieces of toy and this one is her favorite.

Besides loving Cars, Trains, and Trucks, my grandson Landon loves the airplanes from Disney.  This one is really cute and comfortable.  I bought him some for his Birthday last August and he loved them so knew they would be a Christmas hit. I would highly recommend.

Got this on sale and gave it to my two-year-old grandson for Christmas. He loves it-  it's colorful and big enough to grasp easily. But for the adults involved, the sounds are ear-splitting, and go on and on without pause. This toy was so sensitive to touch that it went off when I was wrapping it and scared the bejesus out of me. So- this is a mixed review. If the child is crazy for Planes it's a good buy, IF you are ok with listening to yet another toy that screams for attention. Aye caramba!!!

I bought this as a Christmas present for 1.5 yr old nephew.  It makes noises for a decent amount of time and there is no on/off switch.  I think it will drive parents crazy.  Otherwise seems like a good toy, sound effects sound good just annoying.  He wasn't really interested in it. (There were a lot of other new toys)
My 18 mo old nephew was nuts about this.. It makes plane noises when you swoop it around and talks. Great colors, nice easy size for smaller kids hands
Fun toy!

I bought this for my 2 year old nephew as a replacement for a smaller one that my dog chewed on.  It is bigger than I imagined it would be.  He is able to carry it around with one hand (it's fairly light) and he LOVES the phrases it says.  It is your typical plastic but is pretty sturdy (it has gotten thrown around a bit and is still like new).  The colors are bright and the propeller spins.  I think it's a terrific purchase for any 2 or 3 year old boy.

This was the only toy from the Planes Movie that I could find for a 2 year old.  The other toys are more delicate and detailed, and I feared he was going to destroy it in seconds.  This one if very sturdy, says several different phrases, and my son loves it!

My 2yr old loves the movie Planes and loves all of the figures.  Seems to love Chupacabra especially!  Buyer beware that this thing responds to motion.  So once you push the button to hear him talk be ready to hear him until you put him down!  And with a 2yr old it may be a while!
If you like noisy toys you will like this toy. Good quality. Wish there was an off button to make it stop though...

Our son (2.5) looooves this toy and we haven't even seen the movie yet! Very durable he just loves flying him around. The plane reacts to motion which is good and bad. Good because our son loves it but it's hard to "turn off" the toy because it will still talk a bit even after being set down as it goes through the phrases. Will look into more characters from this model line though as they are perfect for a youngster that is rough with his toys and loves airplanes and Pixar stuff!
It's really load (no volume control), so we just took out the batteries after about a day of listening to it!
This toy seems much more worth the money than the Ninja Turtle Rat King I also ordered for about the same price. Highly recommend this toy.

This things doesn't shut up. My almost 3 year old loved it even without seeing the movie. But it takes awhile for it to stop making noise. DO NOT bump it in the middle of the night while checking on your kids!

Had problems with original item that was delivered but they made it right immediately and allowed me to donate the non-working item as it could still be played with and I thought that was really great!
Just what I wanted & needed...

We love the plane, very durable quality for children. However, wish it had an "on and off" button for the sound, which is fun, but very annoying after a few minutes for the adults. We just took the batteries out and the boys still play with it.

my three year old loves this toy.  it's has a lot of cool sayings from the movie Planes, and it is very easy to hear and understand.  one negative:  it doesn't turn off, it's motion activated, so if it moves, it talks.  tough toy to take to bed, cause any movement will make it talk.  otherwise, great product, good price.

That toy would not shut up!!!! I was trying to hide it from my kiddos but it kept on going and going and going and there was not turning it off, unless I took the battery out!  After it finally gave up, buried under pillows and blankets, I didn't give it to my own child! I'll let another mom suffer from it, yes, I'm that mean! However, it was a cute toy and it did what it was supposed too...a little too well!

This plane  is annoying! it never stops making loud sounds, I had to take the batteries out because was driving me crazy. There is a red bottom on the top but did not works, the toy just make sound with any touch or movement for endless minutes with no bottom to stop it. The material is not very good it scratches easily and the paint chips.

Cute toy but the sound effects drive us all nuts! Too loud and plays for too long with NO way to shut the thing off. Only solution....stuff it under some cushions and wait it out. Much better with batteries removed.
After just having been to see "Planes", my grandson wanted some of the characters from the movie.  The plane itself is well made and has held up over many take offs and "crash landings"
It doesnt seems what the description claims. I was disappointed with this toy when i received.i will not recommend it.
Love this toy! My daughter loves to play with it especially when she's watching the movie. Only this is, it doesn't have a off button. If anything hits the button to make it's noise it goes off.
All of the children we gave it to for Christmas were delighted with this one.  Still being used--didn't get put away after Christmas.
Smaller than I expected
The sound feature cannot be turned off and it is quite noisy after a while . I bought it for our grandson. Now it's sitting in a cupboard.

The plane would probably be more enjoyable if it was new.  I received it just in time for Christmas and hid it away immediately so wandering eyes wouldn't discover it.  When I brought it out to wrap it, I realized it was damaged in two areas and had been painted over.  Not great.  Also, I'm not sure if it is supposed to function this way, but once you turn it on to play with it....it is on for a while.  There is no off button.  I don't strongly dislike it, but I wouldn't purchase another.

In terms of value received by rating the enjoyment of my son, this is a five star item. My son loves playing around with the plane and its just about the right size for him.

The only problem would be that it does make a lot of noise, and it takes a long time to turn off. It was fun for the first little while, but when it says the same thing each time and it takes over a minute each time to turn off, it will start to get on your nerves. It gets really irritating when you just accidentally touch the plane and then it starts all over again.

So its great for kids, but awful for parents.

I'm sorry. I owe my friend an apology. I bought this for her soon-to-be two-year-old son. I figured the toy was chunky enough for small hands, uncomplicated, fun, and finally...it's El Chupacabra. If you haven't seen Planes, stop reading this review, buy it, then come back.

He is HILARIOUS in the movie. Yes, I'm a grown woman, but c'mon. If you can't laugh at him, you have no soul!

I digress. I purchased this toy and set it up on my desk while waiting to get a birthday bag. I had not yet made the HORRIBLE, DISASTROUS MISTAKE of trying it out yet. A couple days passed and I decided I'd see what he does.

I have not yet recovered from this.

Ok, really, down to the real review.

This toy is annoying. The idea is cute, but he makes this super loud noise. I've yet to figure out if you can turn him down, but I don't think you can. I didn't see anything indicating volume control. It's not deafeningly loud, but it's obnoxious.

Then, the noise doesn't stop. It goes on for awhile. Maybe 30 seconds straight (after I had set it down to make it go to "sleep"), or maybe longer. It felt like 5 minutes. It finally stopped and I was thankful.

I went back to work and then it came back on! It lasted maybe ten seconds, but I was ready to return it to Amazon. Unfortunately, I was pressed for time on a gift, so I kept it and gave it to my friend's son. Hence, my public apology.

As a side note, my 8 year-old daughter asked to see what it does and I screamed, "NO! Do NOT push it around me. Period. It's annoying." I had to go into the office the next day and told her once I'm gone, she could push it to see what it does. I received a phone call that morning from her and she said, "Umm...you're right...that thing IS annoying." From the mouth of babes!

***Disclaimer for all the crazies...she was not home alone.***

I'm giving this two stars because it is actually a cute toy. If the batteries were to die, it'd still be a cute toy, so there's that. It wouldn't be worthless, really. Just something to keep in mind if you like the idea of it minus the sound.
It doesn't stop making noises!#!

I bought this for my young nephew for Christmas, and would have returned it if I was sure I'd have another gift in time.

The plane itself is fine, though the plastic seems cheap compared to most young-kid toys I've encountered.

The noise, though, is heinous. I tested it out when it arrived, and it was loud and unpleasant. Once I set it down, it kept making noise for a very long time. I walked past it, which set it off again. A gentle breeze would set this thing off. We were all so annoyed with it on Christmas morning that we removed the batteries as soon as it came out of the package.
my son had a blast with this toy. I bought it for his Christmas gift and he was very excited. It says different phrases and the size was bigger than I had expected. I was pleased with this toy.
Sometimes the sounds goes off by itself! just a warning for parents out there.
Unless I remove the battery, I can't turn the plane off. Otherwise it seems just fine. If  there is a secret, let me know.

I love the original UNO so this seemed like it would have been a good fit. UNO Blast is fun but I would much rather play the regular UNO with the family.

Don't like that there is nowhere to keep the cards after you're done playing, except in the top where they can fall out.

Our family loves playing UNO, and I thought this version would be especially fun for my active 5yo son. Unfortunately, what I thought would be some fast-paced fun turned into an incredibly annoying experience! This game is SO LOUD. It's just too much. I searched in vain for a volume button, of course there isn't one. The game itself is also just unnecessarily complicated. I was really disappointed! The traditional UNO game is simple and fun, and about 1,000 times better than this "new and improved" version of it. Save your money, some batteries, and your sanity and stick with the regular deck of cards!

A fun variation on regular UNO. I would not recommend this as your only version of UNO in the house, as there are so many out now, and this is a great addition to the family. The blaster tickles younger kids pink, especially when my hands shake with trepidation as they approach the dreaded blasting machine. The blaster shoots one to five cards about a foot in any direction, so be careful if you have a glass of sodi-pop close by.
The only real negative is a lack of a carrying case once you have unpacked the original product. If you need UNO to go, the blaster and deck have nothing to go in, but a rubber band will suffice.

Batteries are NOT included in this game. You'll need 3 AA batteries.

It's always fun to occasionally throw a twist onto an old game. If you're in the mood for a little added noise and chaos during your game of Uno, this Blast game is a great addition to the game closet. Sometimes, you just can't beat a nice, "quiet", old fashioned game of Uno, though. At this stage in my life I prefer the quiet version, but it's nice to have this option around for when our children want to play.

Who knew they needed to redo the old UNO game?

This game is a lot more fun with a twist. It becomes loud, noisy, obnoxious, and a bit more fun with a few extra cards thrown in. It would be almost better to play with people who are unfamiliar with the old rules, so that one isn't comparing the old vs new game.

The game provides hours of entertainment, if not necessarily an educational value. For that the price tag is worth it, although one can always buy an UNO deck of cards and play peacefully with that instead.

Good game
A fun game.

Let's start out with the bad: the packaging is SO cheap. The game just comes in a cardboard wrap, not a real box. The problem with this? After unpackaging you're left with the blast unit and a stack of cards, with nowhere to securely store the cards. You can place them in the half-slot area on top of the blaster, but they're not actually secured there. The instructions say to "place it on the shelf". I don't know about you, but I don't have a lot of extra, open shelf space in which to store an oddly-shaped precariously packaged card game.

Now the good: Besides the storage issues we had a great time playing the game as a family. We played this game with our two kids, and even though they're under the age of 7 we all still had a "blast!" It's easy to play, even if you've never played Uno before. The cards blasting out provide lots of surprising fun. The kids can grow into this game and play it for years to come.

The idea is simple- when you have to draw a card because you can't play any that round, the card you draw goes into a slot on the side instead of into your hand. Once you put a card in a slot, you will hear a tone indicating whether you are "safe," or if the cards in the slots are all going to be popped out onto the table.

Kudos to the inventors of the packaging for this device- it was MUCH easier to unpack than most things. Three simple knobs you turn on the bottom of the holder and it's out.

Batteries not included. Takes 3 AA's.

I don't particularly like the "discard into the UNO blaster" rules for the game. Somehow that just seems wrong. Part of the fun of the game was watching someone's hand get larger as they had to keep drawing cards when they couldn't play. But, this is ok.

It says to put only one card into a slot.Since there are 5 slots, I wondered "what do you do if there are more than 5 discards?" The answer: Don't worry. The machine pops out cards often enough it will never get to more than 5 discards.

The timing of the "blaster" is random enough that there is no detectable pattern. The item is well made.

UNO BLAST is a blast!!! Okay, so that's cheesy, but this game really is a lot of fun. All three of my kids enjoyed playing this game (and one of them is a teenager!!!). This is a great renovation of a classic game that the entire family can enjoy. It's a blast!!!

* Important: Make certain to put the batteries in correctly. If the game does not make a sound when you put the batteries in and turn it on, you did it wrong. You will need a Phillips head screwdriver to install the batteries *

Uno Blast is a fun game. If you like Uno, I promise you will enjoy this version of the game. One of the best elements of Uno Blast is that the games go more quickly than in standard Uno. I do not like long games with the exception of strategy games (I'm an old Avalon Hill grognard from when war games had cardboard counters rather than plastic figures). We played three games in less than 45 minutes.

In part this is because with Uno Blast you can never get more than 5 cards added to your hand at a time. However, fortunes can change very quickly. You can say Uno! one minute and two rounds later you have a dozen cards in your hand. At one point, I said Uno and suddenly held 13 cards!

The blast part of the game is fun. When you put a card in a slot the machine makes a sound. The first time the machine shoots cards into the air you'll jump out of your seat and the sense of anticipation is ever present. If you are forced to draw a card, rather than adding it to your hand, you must place it in the machine. One of the five slots will cause the card to shoot out. Any cards that shoot out go into your hand.

Uno Blast uses several new cards, including an Wild Card Blast card, which requires the next player to draw cards until the machine shoots them out, giving him up to 5 additional cards.

The interesting part is that everyone can see the cards being placed into the machine. This has advantages and disadvantages and, I think, this adds to the strategy and challenge of the game. There are times you put a card (or cards) you want into the machine and you kind of hope they will shoot out so you can get them (like the above-mentioned Wild Card Blast card). But you also know what cards your opponent suddenly has and vice versa.

We had a great time and look forward to playing it again. It's a bit pricey at $27 but based on other games I've bought, I think it's worth the investment.

When you are done, the cards fit into a slot on the top of the machine. We folded our instructions in half and stuck them in there as well, so it stores very compactly.

We love Uno in this house so we were very excited to get the chance to check out the UNO Blast Card Game. The game changes up some of the rules of UNO while keeping the basic premise the same - but is it really a fun game?

PROS:

-A new way to play! It's always fun to have a little change when you have a classic game, and the UNO Blast definitely changes up the rules, requiring that you put any card you have to draw into the Blast unit, and adding a few new cards that definitely make the game different.

-Blast unit is fun! The unit is actually really fun, even when you're not playing! My kids spent a half an hour (or more!) putting cards in and watching them pop out, as well as trying to guess which slot was the one that triggered the pop up!

CONS:

-Fast game - all of the Blast games we've played so far went much faster than the regular UNO games, taking 10 minutes (or even less in one occasion!) to finish the game. Good if you want to do a number of games, bad if you want to have a longer, more involved game.

-Missing old UNO - While we liked playing the new game, we did admit to missing some of the facets of the old game. Not having to draw until you get a card that you can play is likely the biggest reason why the game goes so fast.

VERDICT:

While UNO Blast is fun, I don't think it's going to be replacing our regular UNO anytime soon. It's definitely fun for a little bit, and I have a feeling it'd be a blast during a party, but it's not something that we'll be playing all the time.

I remember many, many decades ago when my older sister saw this walking doll on TV. This was back when TV's were actually furniture themselves and you had to walk up to the TV to change the channel believe it or not. ;)

I remember her disappointment when she got the doll and it didn't really walk. Years later when I would actually read commercials, there's this fine-print at the bottom of the commercial that says, "Demonstration only - toy does not walk" for a similar product.

Since then I think I've always been a careful and over analytical consumer and when I had the opportunity to try out this toy, I really wanted to put it through its paces and see the joy in my daughter's eyes.

First, the toy works as advertised, it truly makes klippity-klop noises and the horses really do "gallop" down the ramps. I have to admit, it's pretty clever!

There's also a really slick "motion" detector for when the horse enters the carousel area that lights up the entry area.

If I could I'd give it 4.5 stars I would, but I reserve 5-stars for truly perfect items. I take off half-star because the top "flag" for the castle doesn't really snap into place and easily falls off. I suppose that might have been on purpose for safety reasons if your kid falls on the castle, who knows. Also, this is 5 stars for fun, but 3 stars for educational value and durability. It's really just plastic that snaps-together. Some toys are 5-stars for fun and 5-stars for educational, but the delight on our daughter's face is worth it. She loves putting the horses in their stable, putting them on the carousel and then making them go klip-klop down the ramps. Also her other Little People figurines can hang out in this Princess castle too. ;)

Although this Disney princess toy set takes up a lot of space, it's very cute. This set comes with Aurora and Rapunzel figures, which is a good introduction of these princesses to my 23 month old daughter, who is most familiar with Ariel and Belle. She loves the horse trot sound effects and the music. The only cons are that the slides don't connect to each other and sometimes the horses don't slide as smoothly as you would expect. This may or may not be a problem for your child, depending on their personality. My daughter doesn't seem to get frustrated with it. She really enjoys this toy it keeps her entertained for extended periods of time.
My little one loved this. She likes the clopping sounds the horses make when going down the ramps.

Toy is well made, easy to set up. The longest time is spent putting the stickers on (but I'm picky about getting them on perfect).

The plastic feels of good/sturdy quality. Came with two horses. We bought another horse since (Mike the Knight).

The horses do "Klip-Klop" down the TWO ramps. One ramp turns into a slide (which is kinda cool). There is a ramp/slide on the lower other side which has a permanent wall on it - making it Completely Useless. I read some older reviews where some said that slide did not work properly, so it appears Fisher-Price put the wall up so it cannot be used at all (boo!). Why not just fix it!!

My kids find this fun in short doses, but it does not have much depth to it. The horses move slowly and only for a few seconds on their own. The two ramps are not connected, so you have to move the horse from one to the other. If it had that other (now blocked) slide it would have been more fun. My son tends to run cars down the two ramps more than my daughter does horses since he can make the cars go faster.

Overall, I give the toy 4 stars. BUT, I removed a star because Fisher-Price blocked off the fast/fun slide and made that into a completely useless ramp.

[[VIDEOID:mo2GFGB9EYT3GUB]]Our 3 year old daughter has had the Little People Disney Princess Castle for nearly a year, an it is still one of her favorite toys. It is cute, fun, full of Disney Princesses, and interactive and has helped keep her attention for 10 to 15 minutes at a time. The Little People Disney Princess Klip Klop Princess Stables has already passed the castle in her eyes... because it matches her favorite Disney princesses with HORSES, better yet, as the horses strut down the ramp they make a klip klop sound that really sounds like a horse!

Notes

- The horses make a Klip Klop sound as the go down each of the ramps

- The ramps are not connected, which is a bit unfortunate since it would be nice if the princess and horse could start at the top and Klip Klop all the way donw to the bottom

- The horses can be placed on the small turntable and be spun (while playing music)

- As the horses go down the small ramp leading out of the castle horse sounds plays

- Two volume settings

- Comes with Aurora (Sleeping Beauty) and Rapunzel - but additional princesses can be purchased (Belle, Ariel, and Cinderella)

- The castle and stables feature many pictures of favorite princess firends (Pascal, Mrs. Potts, Chip, and etc)

- It is a bit tricky to get the horses to Klip Klop down the ramps without tipping over - younger children may struggle a bit, but ultimately it will likely help them with their motor skills.

- Requires 3 AA batteries which are not included

- This playset takes up quite a bit of room - it can not be fold or unassembled

- Assembly takes about 5 minutes - but adding the stickers will require another 5-10 minutes

Final Verdict - While the Little People Disney Princess Castle may have more staying power the Little People Disney Princess Klip Klop Stable offers a fun way to watch your child's favorite princess on a horse! Recommended for any Disney Princess fan!

This Gigantic Geode was about the size of a softball. I could feel some powder-like material shifting inside when I shook it, which only added to the mystery. I used a hammer, screwdriver, and a chisel to open it. My goal was to try and break it in two nice halves, so I tried to be precise in my brute smashing. It was surprisingly brittle in places. My first tap on the screwdriver went right through the shell. Other parts of the shell were, strangely, as hard as stone, and my chisel hardly made an impression until about 1/3 of the geode suddenly cracked free in my hand.

Inside, we could see white crystals had formed all over the interior and a number of them, about two tablespoons' worth, had ended up deposited loose inside. I emphasized how special this moment was, explaining that we were the first people to ever see what was inside that particular rock since it had formed deep inside the Earth untold millions of years before. My child was thrilled and excited to hold the geode, as well as the crystalline sand that was inside it. Later, we broke out a microscope to look at the tiny crystal bits, which was interesting for all of us.

Personally, I really hoped we would be fortunate to have a rock full of beautiful purple crystals, but I know these things are a gamble and you never know what you're going to see when you finally manage to crack them open. My child was excited and continued to be excited about it all weekend. I'll probably get a few more in the future for the educational, as well as the entertainment, aspects. I might even try to drive up the suspense before I open it; leave it out for a couple days where it's easily visible and make references to how mysterious it is before I actually open it to let the anticipation build like it was Capone's Bank Vault. I love doing this stuff with my child because they get so enthusiastic about it and it's more interesting than anything on TV. And we're both learning in the process, which is fun for both of us. Finally, we have a cool little thing to stick on the shelf and return to whenever we want.

If you have a child and you're trying to interest them in science and find cool things to do with them away from the idiot box, I think this is a terrific addition to your edu-tainment arsenal. If you're into homeschooling (as I hope to be one day), this would probably be a great tool for that, as well. At $12 a pop, it would probably be a good go-to gift for the other kids in your life (I know a couple I might get one for). Finally, even if your kid isn't that excited about it, you might enjoy it, too. So get crackin'.
