You know what to expect from LEGO: a high-quality product that leaves no room for complaint. The instructions are clear and easy to follow, and the cloud car shoots its tiny circles with an impressive amount of force. (Which might make me reluctant to give this product to a child on the younger end of the recommended 5-12 age range; I’m not quite convinced that the pictures showing not to shoot at someone’s eye will be persuasive to a five-year-old caught up in the fun of the moment).

I’m also impressed by the generous quantity of extra pieces that are provided here: there’s a duplicate of every tiny piece, for a total of 17 extra pieces on top of the base number of 126. There are extras for purely superficial pieces like the pig’s cookies, whose absence wouldn’t really make a big difference to the overall construction, and also for standard pieces like the flat white square. This is one case where you really do get more than you pay for.  

On top of the overall quality of the product, this particular set is just plain cute—but you can see that for yourself. I had no prior familiarity with UniKitty, but I don’t think you need any familiarity with it in order to appreciate this set. I particularly enjoy the faces on the UniKitty and the pig and the bee, and it looks like the other sets in this line will be fun too.

Much better than the smaller, non-extending sonic screwdriver (a colleague had one for his Halloween costume). That being said, I had a few issues:

Pros:
1) It's a solid toy, with good heft. It does not feel as though it would shatter if dropped, etc. I'm sure I will be proven wrong.
2) The extension feature is satisfying on the level that only a 32 year-old man ordering a Dr. Who toy could appreciate. Not flimsy, and I honestly feel like I could mess some Soltarans or Daleks up with it if push came to shove.
3) The extension feature drives my Boston terrier apesh*t, so bonus...he makes a crazy chortling bark noise every time. I haven't told him yet but he's going as K-9 for Halloween next year (shhh! It's a surprise!).

Cons:
1) It was missing a battery when it showed up. This was not a merchant issue, as the package was still sealed. I just was stuck with 2 of the 3 requisite batteries.
2) Installing batteries in this thing practically requires a real sonic screwdriver. It was a giant PITA, with the constant threat of stripping screws hovering over my head.
3) When extended, none of the buttons activate the light and sound effects. Supposedly the button on the rear of the handle is supposed to work in this scenario. It doesn't, and hasn't, yet.
4) Batteries for this thing are expensive, as in $12.99 for 3 of them at RadioShack on a Wednesday afternoon following a hurricane expensive. I guess I could have just bought one (since I had 2/3), but nearly every page in the manual and every website I viewed regarding the batteries indicates that the ones that come with it will most likely die mere moments after you install them, so I bought 3 new ones. At $12.99.

I hope this helps. Overall not a bad purchase, but not the most stellar piece of Dr. Who gear I've seen.

I like the idea of this toy/project more than I enjoyed the toy/project itself. It might provide an hour of entertainment to someone who liked to build models or tinker, and it is mildly educational, but it wasn't that much fun to put together, it was VERY SMALL, and it took a few tries to get it to work well. I would like to give it more stars because it's such a neat idea, but somehow it did not live up to expectations.

WHAT I LIKED: Learning about Archimedes screws and how they are used to move sewage and water. The project comes with a booklet that includes instructions and a comic showing how the device works and how it is used in application. I wish there were more explanation of the principles involved. It would have been nice to have a little bit more information about the function of various parts and pieces when putting things together.

I DISLIKED: It's small. Some of the parts are really small and difficult to handle. It requires white glue and ideally, a piece of waxed paper to use as a work surface. Would have been nice if those items were included. It really didn't work so well. On of the pieces of wood in the model I made was insufficiently sloped so the ball bearing wouldn't roll off properly. It worked okay with a little cajoling -- but who wants to cajole?

I did this project with another person. It was fun to work together, but I think this is probably better suited to a solo effort, as the parts are small and you really do need to look at the instruction book closely to figure out what goes where. Also, the project suggests that you purchase a motor -- why not just include the motor in the kit?

Overall, this provided a half hour or so of amusement and I learned something. But it wasn't as much fun as it looked like it might be. Perhaps if I were a twelve-year-old who liked to tinker, I might have a more positive review.

Marbleocity Archimedes Screw is small and do require adult supervision to assemble.  This is one of those hands on projects with a fun assembly booklet. These Marbleocity toys are a good choice for curious kids. We own three, and the kids have enjoyed building them and playing with them. The materials are good quality, and there haven't been any issues with pieces fitting poorly or flimsy construction, as can be the case with cheaply made imitations.

The best thing about these is the ability to combine them with other sets. This addresses the biggest problem with this kind of toy: namely, that once their built, kids can lose interest in them. Adding the ability to combine sets should help get more play and build time out of these.

B07FDMRRBC.text: My 8 year old nephew mastered the original Rubik's Cube very quickly. We thought it would be fun to make it more challenging on his next visit. He was here last weekend and loved the new challenge! He wore a blindfold and went to work at it. While he was visiting us, he did not complete the puzzle. He came close a few times, but in the end he ran out of time during his visit. He's already excited about coming back next month to try again! I feel confident that he will be able to get it next time. The cube is sturdy and very similar to what I remember as a child. It rotates easily. It's a well thought out version of the classic Rubik"s Cube!

This Rubik's cube is great. It is a 3x3 cube (not quite the challenge of a 4x4, but still plenty difficult). Each color has a different easily distinguished shape so that the color blind and people with visual impairments  can easily distinguish the colors. The tactile colors are nice for children as well. The cubes are not stickered which makes this very durable and child friendly. I am no speed Rubik's solver, but the turning feels smooth to me. My children and I are greatly enjoying this cube. It is priced similarly to regular Rubik's cube of this size.

Like the addition of the tactile sides to help figure out a rubiks cube with touch. Great for those that are visually impaired or for those wanting an extra challenge. Really cool addition to make the Rubiks cube even better.

Gift for a blind child, was great. He could feel the shapes

I've loved Rubik's famous cube since I got my first one back in the 80s craze, and although I didn't figure out how to solve it until years later, it still managed to inspire a lot of thought from me. I'm sure I spent hours back then trying to solve the cube, and despite being too young to have any real hope of solving the puzzle, I still kept at it. The cube has stood the test of time since then as a toy for the ages. This cube finally gives the classic a new spin!

This new version of the cube has textured patterns embossed onto the face of each colored square, so one may feel each side, making this the first cube which may be solved without the benefit of sight! While your average cube enthusiast may not find this to be significant, I'm sure that this will inspire a whole new "blind" solving practice, and best of all, those without sight can actually participate! This allows truly anyone to try to solve the famous cube!

While this may just be a cube for collectors (like me) who just love adding a new cube to the mix, I see a lot of potential to add to the speed solving practice through this cube. And on top of being more inclusive, being able to solve it without looking would be a whole new level of challenge to everyone!

For me, this little doll sort of breaks the cuteness meter—a bit too cute. But, then again, I’m not a 5-year old and my (almost) resident 5-year old granddaughter thinks this is the most adorable doll in the world.

While I’m not a great fan of high-pitched giggling and chatter, she is absolutely charmed. The doll, being so small and portable, goes with her everywhere (but I make her leave it in the car to prevent loss). She watches TV with it, talks to it and with it, and the sound effects never seem to stop and she never tires of the interaction which is not always predictable. Thankfully, it has an off button. It uses and comes with four LR 44 button batteries. They are relatively inexpensive and easy to find. I’ve already ordered a pack from Amazon because, with the use she’s getting, she’s bound to run out of battery at some point soon.

What absolutely impresses me is how well this compact little doll delivers in all the activities she’s capable of. It’s a very well made and a very consistent performer. All the contact points (places you touch to get a reaction) continue to work and react immediately. Considering how many hours she’s been chattering and moving, she just keeps on coming. It’s, obviously, a very well made toy that will last and last.

Another thing I like is that this is a doll that could have wide appeal, age wise. I know that a precocious 5-year old loves it; her 7-year old cousin loves it; and I think it would probably appeal to as old as 9 and as young as 4. It’s too bad that, at this price point (which given the quality is reasonable) it’s too expensive to buy several to have them to take to birthday party. Our usual budget for friend’s birthday is around $15 and this is considerably above that. But if you have a special little girl who needs a special little gift, this is a good bet.

B07GW29P8J.text: This is a darling Lego set! I keep a bunch of Legos around for my nieces and nephew to play with when they're visiting. This a perfect set for my 5 year old niece. It's something that my own children will take the time to play with their young cousins. This is an age appropriate set. It's not too challenging. It's been a bit hit!

This is an adorable Disney Cinderella set, but small..
Although for the price it is fun for the girls to put together, and play make believe with this set.
The coach and all the 3 yr. and the 5 yr love.
There is cute detail with the coach, and all the parts to this set.
This is a fun Lego set. It is a super simple build and very basic. Great for a kid just learning to follow directions for Lego builds.

My four-year-old daughter really enjoyed assembling this kit with some help from mommy and big brother. She had previously gotten a similar one in the Duplo line, but this is obviously scaled differently for normal brick people, and has a lot more detail and interest not only in the build process itself but also in the final product.

The details are really fun in this. I love the scrolls on the carriage, the beautiful wheels, the grouchy looking Kitty and the Kitty insignia on the building, and the fun Cinderella toy mini fig.

The instructions were clear and easy to follow as usual for Lego. It took my daughter some doing because she is newer to doing bricks, but she was very pleased to finally accomplish this with some support.

This is a perfect addition to your LEGO Disney Castle, or just a nice little playset. It's really got some adorable details that LEGO always gets perfect! Lots of specialty pieces make this a must-have.

My daughter enjoys LEGO, but isn't always attracted to the same sorts of Star Wars or hero sets my son enjoys. We pulled this out during a play date while a friend of hers was over. Her friend, btw, loves Disney princesses. As such, this set was a huge hit. The playability rating on this is high - apart from my three year old son working to destroy it (as he does all things), this was a great element to use imagination around as my daughter and her friend became lost together in their playtime. It kept them engaged beyond just the build, which is a huge deal with LEGO sets. If you have a child who is into Disney princesses, then this is a solid bet. It's also affordable and appropriate as a gift.
Gorgeous and sweet, exactly what Disney aims for.  Details on the product are always amazing with Disney. Granddaughter loved it!
Our daughter just loves it. The cat and Cinderella are too darn cute!

My daughter loves this Lego set. She is enjoyed putting it together, and enjoys playing with it still. It went together very easily, with no missing pieces. As all Lego sets they're a little more expensive than they should be, yet it's a quality set that she's going to play with for a long time.

Anyone older than three should be able to handle it. There are a lot of fiddly small pieces but it ends up with a nice detail set. The bit gold feather type pieces don't stay on very well but the overall set is designed well. The table of food seems a little out of place and just adds a bunch of small pieces but our daughter loves it so that's a good vote.
Love that this comes with a carriage! My daughter plays with this all the time!

After graduating from the larger Duplos my young daughter is just getting into smaller Legos and wants to play with everything princess.

She absolutely loves that the main mini-figure is Cinderella. To sweeten the pot, though, the set also comes with a white horse, and a cat, and a mouse, and my daughter plays with all of them.

The highlight of the set is the carriage, which can be ridden in, and which is drawn by the horse.

The final part of the set is a small princess castle (with a magic wand included).

The fact that the set has all these different aspects makes it very playable… and the fact that the set is under $20 makes it a wonderful value -and a great low priced gift perfect for the Disney lover.
This set is small, fewer parts and a good beginner set. While I received this as a Vine Reviewer, the price point on it seems a little high to me for the size of the set. Lego quality as always.

While the carriage and Cinderella are nice, this is a very small set for the price. The Cinderella minifig and the horse minifig are in the style of the Lego Friends minifigs (why are the minifigs in the sets geared towards girls different than the minifigs in the sets geared towards boys?). The castle is tiny. My 5 year old daughter easily built this set by herself in under half an hour. The carriage works well and she has been playing with it non stop since building it, but be aware that you are really just buying this set for a carriage and a minifig. Gus is adorable, as is the cat. The horse doesn't have any moving parts, which is typical of the "girl" Lego horses but I still find it annoying.
Very tiny pieces. I actually superglued a few pieces because they would come off too easily.

The horse and carriage and the castle are all very cute and once assembled it's a nice size for her. My only complaint--and this is from the grumpy parent perspective--is that some of these pieces are mighty small and could easily be lost or stepped on. B07GZ4FNB4.text: My kids used to play Minecraft all the time. My 17 year old still plays it now and then. She had fun putting this Steve set together. My six-year-old son enjoyed this fast, easy build and got a kick out of the big figure and the parrot sculpture he built.

The instructions were extremely clear and there was nothing complicated or unexpected about this.

Obviously, this would mostly be rewarding and fun for somebody who is a fan of mine craft, because the actual build would look very clunky if you didn't have that reference. In our household, my son was not only inspired by the character, but also by the fact that he could build his own figures from his own bricks, so it was inspiring for some continued play.

Really cool Lego building set. Lego,s are the best building blocks. They have easy to follow instructions. The blocks go together and stay together. I like the different set that are available. Would make a great gift for fans of Minecraft.
Product as expected

Minecraft is such a popular video game and now kids can put together their very own real-life model of Steve BigFig.  This 159 piece set creates a 5.3 inch figure complete with a moving arm that swings an axe.  An added bonus is the accompanying parrot that also has wings that 'flap.'  Lego has done a great job with the details of this set and it looks like Steve has walked straight out of the video game.

Sooo...parents with young kids, you will be building this toy for about 45 mins and then rebuilding it each time it falls apart. That being said, it’s kind of a cool LEGO toy that my 6 yr olds loved and still play with.  It was worth the money. I wish the parts stayed together a tad better

LEGO calls this a "bigfig," apparently to differentiate from the standard minifigs. It is definitely not a challenging build, but I was surprised by the bonus play feature of a lever to make Steve's arm move in a chopping motion with his pickaxe. It's a cute set, but I'm guessing it will really only appeal to fans of Minecraft. It's not really going to be winning over anyone who isn't already a fan.

The parts are not very noteworthy, except that there are a bunch of parts introduced in new colors. Dark Azure parts are always nice to get, as are the Dark Brown and Dark Purple. This set is full of "Dark" colors! It's a great display piece for fans of the game, or a great figure for a kid to play with, but I don't think anyone will be surprised when these end up discounted, so if you're interested, it may be worth a little wait.

We're not a Minecraft household, so I was unsure if my 4 and 7 year old sons would like this LEGO.  I need not have worried!  This is an unusual set, in that what you're building is an axe-holding character and his parrot.  Even without familiarity of the character, my sons really enjoyed putting this set together.  It's well priced for the number of pieces in the set and took my sons under an hour.  That said, I felt it had more after building play possible, since it is a character they can then use for imaginative play.  Overall, another LEGO hit.

My son received this as a gift and he loves it.  The figure itself is a good size.  The arm holding the ax actually moves.  There are some other characters from the Minecraft series available and we expect to buy them as well.

B07H3GMZQK.text: My daughters love these automated toys. They know more about them I do. Basically they are like a little toy pet. They react to you plying with them. It's fun to watch them play with them an treat them like a real pet.

The baby giraffe is adorable. Meadow responds to tickles and other cues. If you blow her a kiss, she blows one back to you. Meadow responds to sounds, movements and more. I was wondering what the big deal was about the Fingerlings, now I know.

[[VIDEOID:7eb09b0713c53a21d98668a7a0370615]] This was our first fingerling. Meadow is her name. It comes ready to play with, simple turn on. It fits snug around all my kids fingers ages 6-12. Right away she’s making googly noises and moving. Our daughters favorite feature was that it farts, of course. She sleeps if you lay her sideways. You can blow her kisses and she will respond. Also learn the spots based on the visual directions provided to see her do other tricks and responses. It’s a slightly annoying toy to me, but my daughter loves it and plays with it like it’s real. Very cute!
I love this little fingerling for my grandchildren.  The way you can hold it and play with it is important.

This is a very novel, cute toy that can be used in so many different ways. The overall size of this Fingerling is 5". It is constructed of all plastic, except for the adorable tuft of hair located on top of its head. There are 40 different sounds this toy makes along with performing various actions, including blinking and shaking its head. With some imagination, this toy can easily provide hours of entertainment for any child. They can even rock it to sleep. An added bonus is that the batteries are included.

My daughter had her birthday in quarantine this year. This is the one thing she has been wanting. We ordered it a few weeks ago and it finally came. The batteries are run down and it only talked for five minutes before it died. So disappointed and my daughter is heart broken.

I got this because I wanted a finger puppet to entertain my fifteen month old daughter. She is fascinated by this little thing’s noises and movements. It is too complicated for her to play with herself but she points to it and asks for me to play with it.

I am not sure how interested she may be in playing with it herself but it is a fun toy for me to play with her with.

This is a set of 3 finger painting pads, each one has 25 pages. While they are hardly "giant" that are16" x 12", or about the size of 2 regular pieces of paper. (Too small for an easel). The paper is coated with a slick glossy surface, that should in theory stop paint from seeping through. In reality some paint still gets on the surface below it. The coating also means that it is only suitable for paint, crayons, markers, pencils, or chalk don't work on it. Paint doesn't cover as well as it does on normal paper, and it takes longer to dry. The paper wrinkles when you put  paint on it. The paper is easy to remove from the pad, which is a good thing because the cardboard backing is too thin to hold it stiff and with paint seeping through the paper you would ruin other sheets in the pad if you used them still attached. Butcher paper is better.

It is nice because they can spend the time doing it and then they have something special to keep. They are excited when they make something themselves.

I would recommend it.

This is a fun little craft kit and comes packaged in a small box that is just big enough for the jewelry box itself, and the clay and implements are stored on the inside.

I brought this out for my daughter, but also brought out a variety of other colors of clay and another box for my son to play with at the same time, and they both enjoyed this unique style of crafting a lot.

Overall this is a really fun idea and I'm really excited about finding more fun wooden containers or boxes to decorate.

B07T57YSB7.text: Who doesn't love the element of surprise? I think this is a fun idea. You don't know what career path your Barbie has taken until you open the little boxes. There are 2 different careers in each doll set so you can still have a little bit of choice in the process. My Barbie's career options were Vet and Artist, both vastly different. The doll itself is pretty basic. The doll comes with job appropriate clothing and accessories.

this doll is great. It has the feel of a LOL doll with you not knowing what you will be getting… which my 4 year old LOVED! She was so excited to get the chance to open this doll. Our doll came with two outfits, the one in the picture and her “surprise” career was a soccer player. It’s a great doll and would make a great gift!

This Barbie doll was the center of attention for a while. There is absolutely nothing special about this particular doll - limbs don't bend, we all know what Barbie hair looks like. But my girls loved her. It comes with small amount of extras for imaginary or pretend play, and they had a blast playing with them all. The extra clothes were a little tricky to put on. The secret was to start with straight arm first then contort the bent arm to make it possible to get it into the second sleeve. See, total fun even for me. It would also make a wonderful gift for girls of various ages.

With the craze of "surprise" toys for kids, it was only a matter of time that Barbie joined the game. I received the Pop Star and Chemist careers Barbie.

The included Barbie is a basic Barbie in that she has a limited range of motion with her legs and arms. Included are three different outfits and accessories to match the career. The first is the Spice Girls inspired Girl Power t-shirt and candy land skirt. The skirt for mine was stained on the front and back by a dark brown dotting that did not seem to be apart of the design.

The two careers come with a lab coat and chem lab materials for the chemist and a microphone, floral print dress and guitar for the pop star. I love the fact that the Barbie is allowed to be two vastly different career paths within the same packaging and sends a positive message of "you can be anything you want".

Overall, I would recommend this Barbie package for anyone out there looking for a creative Barbie!

B07TR4N59X.text: This is the second pack I have had of these (the first I bought last June). My grandchildren loved these when they came to visit me in Central Florida in July). First, they feel like snowballs (minus the temperature. Second, they are totally harmless when it comes to things they come in contact with (no damage to lamps, tables etc). Third, they look like real snowballs. I had to get another pack for them to have at their home since they had so much fun with these. These would be great in your home for fun and play where no one gets hurt and everyone has a great time. Highly recommend!

I purchased 2 sets of these for my grandsons (8 and 11yrs) - and they are surprisingly fun!  They have a really interesting 'feel' to them.  They are very light, but fly amazingly well - but harmlessly.  My daughter loves that you can store them in the tub they came in (with handle).  They live in lower Arizona, but love snow.  This isn't a new idea, but it was met with laughs and joy.  Having said all of that, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

I like a good snowball fight, though I am not a fan of getting cold and wet. The closest I have come to an indoor battle with snowballs was with Nerf balls, and while fun it isn’t the same. These artificial snowballs come a lot closer.

These are plush balls, about the size of a snowball you would pack with actual snow, maybe the size of a small apple. They look like they’d be lightweight and airy which would make them too hard to throw any distance, but these are surprisingly dense and have a little heft to them (though still less than a regular snowball). So, they can be thrown a reasonable distance.

Some thought went into these. When they are squeezed they make that familiar scrunching sound you hear when packing wet snow, which is probably the most interesting aspect of these. They are very densely packed and they do not lose material even when played with a lot which is surprising. They’re heavy enough to travel a fair distance but light enough that even if you get nailed in the face they won’t hurt you.

I really can’t find too much wrong with these. They’re somewhat realistic, they’re fun, and they’re inexpensive. They are a good option for having a snowball fight without making a wet mess. And, unlike real snowballs, these can be picked up and thrown right back...

It's August, but I'm thinking Christmas. As in: the grandkids on school vacation, stuck inside because the weather is SO bad, with too much ice/sleet/hail/freezing rain to go out and play in the snow.

So I'm giving them a couple sets of these snowballs, along with some brightly colored mittens (adds even more fun), so they can have that snowball fight INSIDE the house. That should make for a few hours of fun, especially if they add an ambush/hide-and-seek bit to the fight (and they will)!

This pack of 12 "snowballs" are soft enough to throw at each other without anyone getting hurt. They are light enough that even if they hit you in the head, there's no danger of injury (Okay, please use some common sense don't deliberately aim for someone's eye!)

These are inexpensive enough to give as a little "extra" Christmas gift, and I'm pretty sure kids of ALL ages will enjoy them.

B07V2R6S83.text: I got these for when I am substitute teaching as a time filler. The girls absolutely loved these. Easy to use, colorful, hundreds of combinations, these will keep your kids busy for hours. These 'pop' together easily and even the kindergartners I used these with made some really cute bracelets. I have recently purchased another package as I have given away most of the first package of snap beads. Highly recommend these as a great rainy day activity or any time you want kids (girls or boys) to have fun!

My 6 y.o. has had more fun with these snap beads than with any other singular toy this year. They are colorful,  all different shapes and sizes and super easy for her little hands to use. She's made long necklaces to small bracelets. Plus, there are tons of beads, so you get a really good value with this product. I feel like any child from about 4-8 would be pretty stoked about these beads.

This container has 325 pieces of different sized recyclable beads, findings and ideas in this bucket. This has a booklet attached that shows some of the different creative ideas that can be used to make necklaces, bracelets, rings and more. They pop together easily enough. You will want to make sure that small children who put things in their mouth do not play with these, as some are small.

Our 6 year old daughter and her friends really like these beads. They are super easy to use, easy to snap together but they still have enough staying power to hold together and you can create lots of interesting combinations beyond the standard necklace/bracelet.

The only complaint we have about these is that the assortment of colors/shapes included seems pretty random. We got way more of certain colors/shapes than others. My daughter would probably be happy if we had an abundance of purple or pink pieces but instead we got a ton of yellow and orange pieces and far fewer of some of the other colors.
These are adorable. They are very easy to use and easy to come apart. The designs are able to easily be changed and creates endless time of play and creativity.

So many jewelry kits my 4 year old needs assistance with. She (and I) was so excited to be able to use this kit without help. She’s been playing with it since it arrived and she’s loved showing off her creations. Hours of joy and fun!

This pop art kit is so cute and fun to use.  It comes with 325 different pieces to make all kinds of jewelry.  The pieces snap together easily and are easy to pop back off again to start a new project.  There are small parts and it has the recommendation for this to be for kids 3+ years.  It comes with a tiny little "booklet" that shows different things to make.  It comes in a container with a handle for cute storage when not in use.  The tag states made in China.

320 piece set that your child can make bracelets or whatever their imagination comes up with. Well made set comes in reusable storage container that is cute in itself. Not for smaller children as could easily be swallowed but my 7 year old has a blast with these.

This came in a very damaged box from the manufacturer.  The colorful cardboard on he outside of the container was curled up so easily fixed with some glue.  All the internal pieces look great because the container is still sealed.  I got this for my 8 year old GDaughter so she could make matching jewelry for all of her AG dolls.  She's going to love them.  So many colors and so many possibilities.

This is a fun toy for kids to practice their fine motor skills and it’s also great for hand/finger strengthening. I’m a pediatric PT so I brought this to work for myself and the OT to use as a therapeutic tool.

There’s tons of colors of beads that can be snapped to each other to make jewelry, and there’s also some small bracelets that the beads can be snapped to. It’s a great toy, and the kids always enjoy playing with it!

My seven year old loves to create, so this was the perfect toy to try out for her. She loves to draw and make jewelry, so the snap pop beads help with her imagination and creativity. The container that it comes with allows us to keep everything in one place and organized, so we don't have the beads all around the house. My 7-year-old has already created several pieces from the beads, and even my teenager has created some pieces too.

Fair warning though that this toy has small pieces with it and I would not recommend it for a younger child/toddler. Also, if you have a cat as we do in our house and one of the beads ends up falling from the table, our cat will play with it like it's a soccer ball. She's our hyperactive kitty who loves small items to bat around the house.

All little girls want play jewelry, but a lot of the times it gets lost and even ruined. So it can be a waste of money. But this is a creative alternative! Your child(ren) can create and wear their own jewelry! When they’re done playing, they just take it all apart and put it back into the container; giving them endless ideas/possibilities for their jewelry.

My daughter is about to turn 6, and she had a blast playing with these. She can easily put together and take apart all the beads and bracelets. There were some that she needed me to help with, but I think once they’re broken in, it won’t be an issue. This entertained her and I for a good 45 minutes or more. We were able to make several different pieces of jewelry before we ran out of beads.

This kit came with many different style of beads and charms and there were also several different colors of bangle bracelets. The beads and charms are all decently sized, so they’re perfect for little hands to control. They come in all sorts of colors. The one thing I did notice is the picture shows rings, but there weren’t any rings in our container. But thats okay. My daughter was perfectly happy with it as it came. I think a child age 3 and up would enjoy this kit!

We were very excited to get these beads! The beads come in a cute container with a twist top lid. That's such a great design because we can put the set back in that container when we are done playing. The beads are very colorful and range in different sizes. I liked that because you can create all different sized jewelry. And once we got tired of what we created, we took it all apart and created new things. It's a fun little set to have around on those rainy days.

B07VKQ2HDY.text: My nieces (5 & 10)  and nephew (8) spend a lot of time at our house. I like to have unique toys that they don't have at home to keep them entertained. This magnetic play set by Melissa & Doug has been perfect! It easily accommodates all of their ages. This set comes with a pirate ship, building, characters and lots of magnetic props. It's a modern twist to the old school paper dolls that I grew up with. The subject appeals to both boys and girls. The play set is sturdy and should last. I am very impressed with it!

This play set comes with panels that you attach to make a pirate ship. They are magnetic. When you get the ship together, then you push out all the other pieces so you can man your ship. One thing to watch for: pay attention when younger children play with this set because you don't want them swallowing magnets. The magnets in this toy is not like the earth magnets, but, still good to not let them swallow them.

What a great fun toy for preschoolers. I love the creative aspect that this toy provides. These am work with all the other sets. The playtime and ways to put these together are endless. The these are magnetic and stick together in all kinds of ways. Each set comes with a sheet of characters and accessories. Very well made and the large pieces are good for toddlers to school age children.

I gave this toy to my four year old to try out, and she really enjoyed it. The magnets make it easy to snap figures to different parts of the pirate ship or playset. Melissa and Doug make terrific toys, and this one is no exception. It has the durability and great quality that they are known for. These toys last forever and are lots of fun!

This is a precious magnetic play set.  The images on the pieces are very cute and detailed just enough to be appealing to kids.  The magnets are strong and allow your child to use their imagination to create stories and scenes to their liking.  The set comes with figures and accessories that can be added to the scenes.  It's a good sized play set but small enough to require supervision for smaller kids.  Wouldn't want anyone to choke.  The downside to this set is the price.  Yet again, Melissa & Doug has overpriced one of their toys.  This should be around $20, in my opinion.  However, it's cute enough that I would repurchase it should the need arise.
Lots if fun with this magnet set, it’s  easy for my three year old and my 12 year old both to manipulate these magnets into their creative masterpiece. Recommended

I got this for my 5-year-old son who loves pirates.  He was very excited to find it when it came in the mail and immediately opened it up and played with it for a while.  I have never seen magnet sets like this before, and it's such a great idea!  It gives kids the opportunity to build a scene in thousands of different ways from making different building shapes to adding in characters, costumes, and props easily with them all being magnets.  There are tons of different items that can be placed throughout the backgrounds or on the 2 pirate characters.  The only thing I would say is some of the parts are very small, so this is not suitable to have around younger children, and the pieces can be easily lost.  I would suggest this for slightly older children (maybe at least 7) or children who really love to do imaginative play with scenes.  My son really enjoyed it, but I believe if he was a little older he would get more out of it and it would entertain him for longer.

These miss the mark in so many ways. I have two boys, almost 4 and 6. Both like building, legos, magnatiles, Lincoln logs and both love boats so I expected this to be a home run.  The sail magnets don’t stay up if they want to “play pirate ship” so they’re constantly getting frustrated or needing help fixing it, also there are too many tiny magnets that are “insignificant”.  I would not purchase again. Overpriced and barely getting played with. Regret.

This toy is great for promoting a child’s imagination. The panels can click together in many different ways to create different things. What I didn't really like was that the magnets had a strong chemical odor to them. We have another Melissa and Doug magnetic playset similar to this that doesn't smell so I'm not sure what's going on. B07VQHTGBJ.text: This magnetic play set is like a new take on paper dolls. Everything stays in place way much better than they did with paper dolls. These don't have all the clothing that paper dolls had, but there are accessories. There are a few people and they have stands to keep them upright. There's a scene set of the castle. This toy set is well made, has several figurines and parts to build a castle as well as many outfits and little odds to create wonderful playful moments. It promotes imagination, role play and creativity. Kids love it, can create whatever they want and play for hours! I recommend it.

The 14 double-sided panels with artwork on both sides magnetically attach in different combinations, so kids can build new designs for their castle every time they play. Magnetic tiles meet paper dolls in this cool new toy. It comes with panels that are magnetic and stick together like larger versions of the ever popular magnetic tiles. Now don’t mistake this for a building toy as that’s not really what I’m saying, more a designer toy. Building the castle yourself makes you the designer, lets you make the choices of what the rooms look like and where they go. There aren’t really a lot of building options though my kids have tried to get creative.

But as a designing toy it is awesome, after you arrange your castle there are magnetic pieces that stick directly onto the tiles to decorate each room. It comes with 2 people that you can dress as prince, princess, knight, etc to go with your castle. That would be my 1 complaint, that it only comes with 2 people. The castle, once built, is only really big enough for 2 kids to play but they’ve gotten bored and had to bring in other figures because 2 people can only do so much. Kids have 2 hands so 3-4 figures may have been better.

The figures are basically like wooden paper dolls but the clothes magnet on, making it way easier than paper dolls. It comes with many different outfits, which is nice because I know my kids are going to lose some pieces, but it will still be playable because there are a good many choices.

My biggest draw to this toy was that it is an open ended, imagination encouraging toy that looks small enough to travel with. We travel a good bit and if you don’t bring good, open ended toys they get bored of them quickly so you need to bring a ton. This does not disappoint, the pieces fit into the box which has a handle and is smaller than a book bag. My kids even play with it in the box on their lap.

Such an adorable set! It requires no batteries, makes no sounds, ie very easy to set up and use, it has the "S.T.E.M." stamp on it, and my kiddos love it!  It's a great way for kiddos to use their imagination and creativity. 5 stars!!!!

CASTLE PIECES:
In this Medievil castle kit there are a total of 8 square tiles. On one side of each of these tiles, there is an inside castle scene (one has a working door). On the reverse side, six of these tiles have outside scenes. On the remaining two tiles one has a dungeon scene and the other has stones in cement. There are two half tiles that have castle scenes too. There are two triangle roof tiles that have thatched grass on one side and shingles on the other. Finally there are two half-square triangles with a checkerboard on one side and cobblestones on the other side.

There is a bedroom, entryway with a working door, sitting room, hearth. dungeon, etc. and they are all very colorful, well-designed and perfect for imaginative ole play.

DOLLS/FIGURES:
Included with all the castle-building pieces are 5 stand-up "dolls" (2 males and 3 females) with stands. The dolls are magnetic and there is a sheet of magnetic clothing and accessories. This set really needs a plain magnetic sheet to use for storage of all these magnetic pieces when a child is done using them.

The castle pieces go together rather easily and stick together magnetically in such a way that the pieces always line up at the corners. Truthfully, there isn't a whole lot of different ways that this castle pieces can go together. That won't stop little girls from really enjoy playing "Medieval Paper Dolls" with this set. I did this myself a lot as a kid and always thought it was a lot of fun. As a young girl, my sister and I played with paper dolls like this literally for hours. This set takes it a step further with castle pieces and having a "house for the magnetic dolls to live and play in.

One of the very best things about this set is that there is a molded tray inside the box that can safely hold all the castle and doll pieces. There literally is a place for everything with one exception. There is no good way to store the magnetic clothing/accessory pieces. It would be nice if a plain magnetic sheet were included for storage of these pieces.

The molded form with all the pieces stores nicely in the box it came in. This box, very conveniently, has a handle at the top of the box that allows it to be transported easily for a visit with grandparents, a play date, or a sleepover.

All-in-all, this is an excellent set for role play and I highly recommend it.

The 14  Double Sided Panels with artwork on both sides are  beautiful and you can build your Castle in so many variations.  You then have 2 people you can dress up 2 live there. B07WP8FTKV.text:
If you're looking for a wonderful thinking game, this is an excellent purchase to get started. It comes with a Go instruction booklet as well, which hits all the high points of gameplay without being too long or boring. If you read your way through the entire book (about 20 illustrated pages) you will be well on your way to understanding most aspects of the game.

Several tips to note about this board:

It has 9x9 grid on one side and 13x13 on the other, which makes it the perfect board for beginners or those learning Go. These smaller sizes are normally used by less experienced players to learn the basics of the game, without being overwhelmed by the length of a full 19x19 match. A 9x9 game, depending on how long the players take to think about their moves, will take about 10 to 20 minutes, and a 13x13 game takes about 20 to 40 minutes.

The wood is spruce and is very good quality for a beginner's board. I have not used it for very long so I don't know how long it would take the lines on the board to wear off or show signs of use. However, it's still in pristine quality from when I bought it, and I've used it quite thoroughly. Any dust or dirt can be easily wiped off with a dry or slightly damp cloth (it comes with instructions on how to care for the board).

Of primary consideration is the quality of the Go stones that come with this board. If you don't have any stones, this is also a great purchase because the stones are rust-proof and will never crack, break, or corrode. They are nice and big, so they are easy to hold and become used to playing Go with. Another plus is that it comes with enough stones for a 19x19 game, so if you later choose to purchase a full sized board, you'll have enough stones to play with.

Overall, a great purchase if you want to jump into learning how to play Go.
Beautiful board but ours came with a crack :( Ordered a replacement, hopefully this one will be fine.
I like this set alot but I really wish it had a box or carrying case for all the parts.  I can't set it on our game shelf and keep it all together as it is now.

It's a beginner's go board. It is made well out of real wood (I have no idea whether it's actually shin kaya, but it looks nice and appears it won't warp). Everything about the boards is the right size, unlike the smaller boards in the lower-price tier.

The stones are light, slippery plastic. Disappointing. But your money is paying for that board.

If you are a go learner or looking to get back into it (like me), this is what to get. While it is cheap for a go set, it's obviously very expensive for a board game.

That's go. That's the way it is. The West received this game from Japan and with it the (expensive) Japanese aesthetic.

There is a similar board on here, bamboo I think, for $30. Don't get that one. Get this one. It is nice and nice to play on. Even if you only play a handful of times before putting it away in a dusty drawer, you'll only be spending a couple bucks extra on each game. If you play a lot, it will simply be worth every penny.

Thank you, Yellow Mountain! I can’t believe how nice this kit is, especially at this price. I own one of your full size wooden boards with glass pieces and beautiful wooden bowls, and it’s gorgeous, but I really wanted a small reversible board, mainly for the 13x13 side. It arrived today, and it is great. Thank you!

Four extra black pieces, and two extra white pieces (which is way better than being short a few, even though I’ll never use all of them on a 13x13 board). Nice painted lines (which I think are way better than attempting to carve lines in—that would just scratch the pieces and make the board fragile anyway. And I imagine painted lines are traditional anyway?) Oh, and the grid is perfectly “slightly foreshortened” so it is slightly longer in the direction between players, making it appear satisfyingly square from the player’s seat, as is appropriate.

The board is flat. No cracks. The grain is pretty.

Some people complain about the plastic bowls, but they actually seem reasonably solid to me! The lids snap on with a reassuring *snap*, and don’t just pop off. If I travel with it to the pub (which I intend to do) I might pour the pieces in a ziplock. But it doesn’t seem absolutely necessary.

Anyway, thank you for the nice board. It will get years of use.

The shell is three pieces so if you want, you can put it back together and hatch the thing again and again, or fill the egg with other things, like use it as an Easter basket later or something. Plus you don't have to have the vacuum ready for the bits and pieces.

It has two layers of plastic on the outside to peel off. The kid may need help with this because you might need scissors or a box cutter. There's a tab to pull on the outer layer but those things don't always work. The second layer doesn't have a tab and I had to cut it. There's a little preview card on the outside saying what the Rainbocorn likes-- That will end up in the trash.

It's not immediately obvious how to open the egg. If you give it a light squeeze in the center that will save you some struggling. Watch the heart in the center because that's part of the Rainbocorn as well. You can push the sequins backwards on them and they will show a new pattern. You can snap them onto the Rainbocorn or clip them onto something of yours like your backpack or something in your room like a curtain or bed.

The Rainbowcorns themselves are these hopelessly ugly little stuffed animals that kids love. They are scented with some ambiguous fruit-- I can't place it, but I don't think it matters. You can pick which one you want here on Amazon. There's probably a way to tell by the color of the sequined hearts and the plastic horns on the eggs in person, but I don't know it. I think the blind box part comes in when you open the mini egg inside and of course the idea is to get you to puy tons of these to get the rare golden mini toy.

There's the mini PVC figure in an egg, a bracelet with the Rainbocorn on it, a sticker sheet, Rainbocorn "poop" which is really just play-doh, and a collector's guide. So it's more than one toy and the unboxing experience is more than just sitting there and watching. They can take the stuffed animal to bed, wear the bracelet to a lot of different places, put the stickers on notebooks, play with the "poop" in the kitchen, and kind of have this everywhere.

So we have a winning toy here that was a hit with the kid and and the adults as well. Five stars and I may just buy one for myself as well.

B07WV5CF89.text: These seem like good quality and the colors are nice and seem accurate.  I was concerned that the horns of the moose might be sharp and could hurt a child if they fell on the toy, but no worries here; the horns are soft and bendable.  If you tried to bend them much, they might break off though.  The price seems reasonable.  If you buy them to teach your children about these animals, there is one problem.  The racoon and fox are over half the size of the moose, so the proportions are all wrong.  The fox and racoon are about the right size in relation to each other, but next to the moose, the grouping looks strange.  Looks like we an have incredibly large mutant fox and racoon or incredibly small mutant moose.  I noticed there are other groupings available in this brand and I would have paired the moose with maybe a bear and a deer.  Then put the fox and racoon with another animal about their size.  The package contains only one small paragraph about the 3 animals, so this is not an educational toy by any stretch of the imagination.  Smaller, younger kids probably won't care about any educational benefit anyway or the size proportions of the animals, so this may not be a big deal.  As a kid, I would have loved a set like this.  I suppose a smart kid would pick up on the size discrepancy if they have ever been to a zoo and seen some of these animals or seen a TV program that showed the sizes.

My kids liked these little animals. They were very realistic. They played with them for a while. The detail was great. They were cute.

We have a lot of these sets from this company. We have been very happy with them. They are made very well. We have never had a single one break, even with rough play. They can also be displayed. I would very much recommend them.

I actually gasped when I pulled these animals out of the box. They are beautiful. Bigger than I expected,  super sturdy and so much detail. The colors and textures really do a lot too to make these figures feel really special.

These are really good animal figures - lots of detail and sturdy enough for rough play.  My grandchildren have fun playing with them outside, building corrals for them - pretending they’re real.  I’m always on the lookout for things of interest that lures them away from the TV and tablets, and these do the trick.  When they’re older, these will be collectibles.

What a fun set! I've been trying very hard in educating my kids to emphasize the importance of ecology and to talk about how the animals that live in an area interact and work together in the environment so that everything functions well. I really like that these fun sets have been geared towards different areas of the world.

I think the Bears are my absolute favorite, with the one bear standing up on its hind legs to see what's going on and the other one walking in a more normal stance. The Moose is also pretty special, with its fancy antlers. I really love the level of quality on these. The deer looks a little spindly and is perhaps out of scale with the Bears, and the Buffalo. That would be my only complaint. Other than that this is a nice quality set and very sturdy and durable.
This is a nice set of animal figures.  They are fun and durable enough for kids to play with, but also look nice as part of a collection or up on a shelf on display.  The quality is good, too.

This is a nice set of wild animals. A hard plastic wolf, bald eagle and grizzly bear are presented in a forest scene. The bear and eagle are realistic. The wolf's body is perfect with the bushy tail bit the face with the squinty eyes looks more like a coyote. The white color, though not unheard of, is not common eithrt. The back of the box has few facts about the animals. Pretty spare. Still a nice set that should foster an interest in wildlife.

These are just so finely detailed, and so realistic looking. They're a lot of fun for a 4-year-old who loves animals. Super sturdy, will last for handing down to future generations. These are made with quality workmanship.

These heavy plastic animals are detailed and very nice, especially for the price. They are a wonderful value. The plastic is solid; it's a shinier type of plastic than the matte and almost slightly rubberized plastic of Schleich animals. The painting is detailed and accurate. There is no weird odor. They look highly durable and get wet with no issues whatsoever. The Schleich brand has much finer detail in the molding process and the painting is more detailed. So for collectors, I would still suggest that brand, but for children having a blast, school applications, etc. these are great. One note: they are relatively well protected against damage, but it may be that some parts will break. The buffalo had lost one of its horns when I received the set. I superglued it back in. The Schleich animals are solid and I've never had any breakage no matter how hard they were used. But then again, they are much more expensive. For the price, these are a great value.
Great quality. I know it is kind of a waste to let a kid just play with them and throw it around but you know what, it still looks the same, the paint didn’t come off or anything. Easy to clean too

I love these Battat animals and have quite a few. They are attractive and large enough to be easily handled by little hands. My kids always enjoyed plastic animals, so I have getting a lot of these for my grandsons. (My all time favorites were the polar bears which were so gorgeous, I wanted to put them in the china cabinet.) These offer endless hours of imaginative and non-electronic play. They are not proportionally sized though, so a fox and a moose may be fairly close in size. In this set, the bear should probably be much bigger to be the right size in comparison to each other. That's just a limitation of the toy.

I do have two reservations for the youngest kids: note that these are for kids 3 and over. I don't know the reason for this rating, but these figures are not completely unbreakable--I have a cow with a missing ear. Also I don't know the kind of paint used to decorate these. Whatever the case, I don't consider these animals safe to chew on, hence the age restriction.

Nevertheless, I love these animals. They are fairly affordable and I expect them to be enjoyed for years.

I have a lot of Battat animals for my grandsons, but this is my first set of forest animals. The fox, moose and raccoon are painted with such detail--the eyes of the fox are impressive. My only complaint with this set are that the animals in this set are not proportionally sized the ears of the fox come halfway up the snout of the moose! Other than that, this is a spectacular moose. I am wondering, though, if he should be reserved for display, as his antlers may break with normal children play. I like this set very much.
Another fabulous set! This set is a little more unique, has animals you don't see in many play sets. Great for any little exotic animal lover :)

Such a nice change from movie-inspired figures, comics figures, fantasy and magical creatures, robots, aliens and all others of the non-natural type! Though natural, I suppose you could toss dinosaur figures into that group, too.

The assortment provided in this set is also nice. Aside from providing a better playing experience, they lend themselves to display in a child’s room. They’re durable, adaptable to indoor or outdoor use, car trips, etc. They need no special care.

From packaging to the quality of the toys, absolutely amazing. My expectations were very low because of it’s price. But these are heavy and strong toys that don’t seem broken easily.

These are cute toys, but they could be a far more accurate representation of the animals. These are not at all close to what the animals look like so this can't be considered an educational toy. The noses and eyes are distracting, the shapes of the animals are cartoon like, very pointy noses, definitely not proportional with respect to each other either. I understand there are packaging issues but if kids are going to think that a fox, raccoon and a moose are certain sizes, that's like pretending the USA is an island and Canada just isn't there. Remember that in school? I do. We can do better for educating kids, even with toys that we might take for granted as none essential or insignificant.  They are a bit pricey when compared to the actual animal replicas that are very well made. These are priced only about 5 dollars less than the high end brand I checked out for comparison before writing this review. It intrigued me. I had an extensive farm animal collection as a child and they were an official brand that really created a farm scene with all the animals the right scale, with respect to each other and they were exact breeds as well. Again, not much of a price difference. I ordered these for me because these just happen to be a trio of my favorite animals, Fox, Moose, and Raccoon.  I wanted more totems. I'm not  worried about breaking them, but for kids I am concerned. The animals seem flexible but I don't want to test them to much to see what happens. They are okay for display and they are stable and stand on their own.  I think the packaging is great, air holes on the side and once you liberate them from their wires, the box can  used their box as a display base.

We have two other sets like this one, and they all meet or exceed expectations. The detailing is fantastic, they're structurally sound, and they deal with a whole lot of play. These are sturdy and look just like the real animals. They are size proportional to each other. They're solid and sturdy but not overly heavy. They're great for play or displaying.
These animals look so real and at the same time friendly and non-threatening. They are sturdy and pretty enough to display, which I am doing.

My kid has been using these since before turning 2, and we have never had any issues with pieces chipping or getting torn off or any other thing that would make me worry about such a young child playing with them. They are very detailed and well made- though not without flaws though (our wolf has got a funky looking face NBD). Nothing major, still much nicer than a lot of similar toy animals for children.
At the time of writing this review, this set is priced at under $5 which is an absolute steal for the quality you are getting! Other sets of animals are priced up to $10 or more, which is still a fair price considering the quality.

Ok well, I haven't ordered all the plastic animal toys on Amazon but I've ordered a few. These are the ugliest most un-animal like I've seen. If your kid needs corrective glasses they might not notice. These animals make the case for a "no stars" review choice.

These Battat toys are a happy medium between low end hollow toys, and high ends highly detailed toys. Price is totally reasonable for what you get.

The look and feel of the Battat animals is great for play. Each one is solid, not hollow, so they can get wet and water does not get inside. And, I can wash them in a bucket without getting water inside of them. Great for kids and convenient for me! And will hold up over time. The level of detail on the animals is pretty good. Nicely moulded details like fur and feathers. The animals have painted details that look good from several feet away. The level of detail is not photo realistic and nothing like the high end Schleich animals, but fine for basic play and after a toy gets beat up a bit, the level of detail doesn't matter so much. (For price comparison, a Schleich set of 6 animals at a comparable price to the Battat 6 animal set would have significantly smaller animal figures - like babies next to the Battat ones.)

For some reason, the paint on the moose toy scratched off like crazy in just a few days of light play. The others all seem fine with kids playing with them, so I don't know whether that was a factory thing.

Selection of what animals are available from Battat is also mid-way between dollar store and Schleich. Dollar store has exactly 6 realistic dinosaurs available, and the selection will never rotate or change, and then has 12 realistic animals available and they don't look so good. Schleich has any animal, I'm pretty sure, and all are beautiful. It's a favorite of zoo and museum gift shops, because they can stock toy versions of the exact animals that live at the zoo. For Battat, I got the "North American Animals" collection specifically for the alligator, because I live in Florida, and also because the other animals are a little less common - in my random collection of figures, I have polar bears, but just about none of the other animals here are common in animal sets so didn't duplicate animals my kids already have.

Overall for the price point and the quality, these Battat toys are great. Especially being solid and not hollow is good for long term durability and for being easy to clean without water getting inside.

B07XB3J38K.text: My 22 year old son is STILL a big fan of Pokemon. He has shelves in his room full of Pokemon things. This little guy has a spot on one of those shelves. In my opinion, some Pokemon are better suited to brick form than others. I think Charmander looks … kind of silly. There’s something about his head that’s throwing me off and not in a good way. I think Charmander’s mouth looks more like a beak than a mouth.

Sure, it’s difficult to recreate a round shape with bricks, but Mega Construx has done it with other Pokemon, such as Ludicolo.

The set includes an instruction booklet and 6 unnumbered bags. Finding the pieces for each step is the longest part of the build.

The instructions are pretty clear, but I did have to fix a few steps because I used the wrong piece. Some of the pieces are so similar that it’s easy to pick the wrong one.

As with other Mega Construx sets, sometimes it can be very hard to get the pieces to snap together. My fingers usually hurt by the time I’m done building a set. So kids might need some help with that.

One of my pieces for Charmander’s mouth has a spot of errant black printing on it.

For adults like me who want to display Pokemon, Charmander does stand on his own. He doesn’t take up too much room, so he would be a good fit for a desk or shelf.

This isn't just an electronic version of the same "Life" game from years ago. In addition to making it electronic the game itself is different, but not necessarily better (no stock, auto insurance or life insurance to buy for example, and no wedding gifts or baby gifts etc).

Every player gets a card and one calculator-type device gets passed around. You put your card in it and record whatever money you received or paid during a turn. The device tallies all the money and tells you who won. If you prefer the original "Life" game but not the hassle of dealing with paper money on every turn just give every player a calculator and let them tally their individual money totals on their own devices. Then you don't have to pass around one device, you don't have any cards to keep track of, and you can play the original game but "electronically."

We wanted a new Life game because our old one's spinner was terrible. This one has a FANTASTIC spinner that can't jam, and the new electronic banking is really easy and fun to use. We were playing the original version once a week so I feel like I can speak from authority here - this one is loads better. It's really well-designed.

Top tip - have the banker hold onto all the credit cards. It makes no sense to keep giving them back to each player at the end of every turn.

It's a really fantastic way to update a game and they've changed so much, making it easy to play and lots of fun. My kids love it.

That's going to get ripped and the flap is going to get worn out quickly.

The game of Life is as fun as it's ever been but I think they could have put more thought into the game case design.

The Avengers movies may be coming to an end, but I think that everyone knows they'll be classics for years to come. And Iron Man is the one that started it all! His Hall of Armor is a central part of the character in the comics, and a large part of the movies, and it's finally gotten a proper LEGO treatment!

The Hall is a set that appeals to collectors is a really meta way. Not only will collectors of LEGO Avengers love it, Iron Man fans will really NEED this set, and then fans will want to collect all of the Iron Man suits to fill it up! And it gets you started in a big way with 4 (!) of Iron Man's suits, including the Mark 1 armor that started it all!

Representing the new movie, it includes two Outrider minifigures, and although I haven't seen the movie or know anything about these characters, I have the feeling that people will really just want this set for the Hall itself, not so much as an Endgame specific set. It's awesome, and it even would be nice to have a couple of them to really fill out your suits. The set it designed to be able to accommodate this as well, you can move the individual pods for each suit and attach them above or in line with each other to customize your own Hall!

This is not your usual LEGO set.  Usually 500+ piece sets like this one are more complex builds.  Because the Hall of Armor is relatively simple in design, this is relatively quick (it took my almost 5 year old about 2 hours).  That said, the beauty is not just in the building but in the playing that came afterwards.  Although my sons haven't seen the Avengers movies yet due to their age, there is plenty of secondary material that they are well familiar with.  They loved being able to stage Iron Man in the hall, which is a nice set piece, and play with the assortment of mini figures.  If you're an Iron Man or Avengers fan, this set is a must.

Overally, for $25 it's hard to nitpick too much considering how much you are getting in the box. The half dozen darts are enough for 2 full reloads on the internal magazine of the pistol, the gun is quite large and sturdy, with the removable "suppressor" extension tube out front, and you get a few little targets that are good fun to plink at.

A few problems I had were difficulties loading, darts jamming, and some things I would've liked added to this.

In terms of loading, I wish the slide came back even 1/2" or 1/4" further. The slide right now comes back juuuust barely enough that you can kinda cram the foam darts in, but it can be a bit tricky to do at times. A little more room would've been nice.

Jamming happens a lot, forcing the slide forward sometimes it will just pinch a dart instead of nicely stripping it from the feed.

And then a big thing I think would've been nice to include would be an illuminated sight. The fake red-dot at the rear is just a hollow arch of plastic. There's nothing inside it. There is an orange sight post in the front, but trying to figure out how to align it correctly takes a lot of trial and error. On my blaster, you kinda had to hold with the tip of the front sight about 2/3 up the window, otherwise you'd constantly hit low. Having a piece of etched acrylic in the back, either painted red or with a cheap LED to edge light it and make it look like a real red dot would've been super cool and super helpful for aiming.

All in all, this is pretty good, and would be the great basis for someone who likes to mod and upgrade nerf guns, but its a little fiddly to use and jams a lot if it was for a kid.

B07YD34XSL.text: My 3 year old and 1 year old granddaughters love playing with this phone. Even though they have a few other toy phones, they are still curious about what all the different buttons do and what songs it plays.

Let me first say I love this toy and think it is a great concept BUT it does not work well. When we received it new, it did work however the volume is VERY low and there are no volume adjustment options. You basically have to hold the phone up to your ear to hear it (which obviously isn't great for little ones who don't quite understand that concept yet). Despite it being low, we just kept it and dealt with it rather than the hassle of returning. However today the volume/sound stopped working altogether (after ~1 month of use). The buttons still light up but no sound comes out. I tried changing the batteries however it continues to not work. Of course it is past the return window. My advice to buyers is to maybe try it out in the store first before ordering here. I am not sure if I just got a defective one or if the volume is just designed low on this toy. B07YYMFQQQ.text: My 11 yr old loved the idea of experimenting with this small vacuum. He was able to set it up quickly and enjoyed doing the experiments. The boiling water experiment was pretty difficult and he needed my help. The balloon was fun and we also put in a bag of fruit snacks to inflate. It was entertaining for about an hour but that’s about it. Comes with everything shown. Probably pass it on to a friend to try out now that we’ve had our fun with it.

This toy vacuum chamber is a fun learning toy to teach kids basic chemistry and physics concepts.  The experiments are neat and did hold my kids attention for a while.. but they became frustrated because the vacuum chamber is a bit hard for them to operate by themselves.  Given that this is a toy and not an expensive labratory grade vacuum chamber, it does hold a surprisingly good vaccuum once you get it sealed.  The main problem with our set is that the included plunger doesn't seal super well so its hard to draw a good vaccuum, it worked much better once I hooked it up to my handheld vacuum pump.  Overall, its a fun toy that kids will enjoy playing with for a bit but it doesn't have a lot of replay value.. still, I think its a good idea for getting kids thinking about STEM concepts like temperature and pressure, thermodynamics, etc..
This is a neat kit to get your child interested in learning more about science and how stuff works. It's fun to play with the experiments and see how pressure effects things.

Fingerlings are too cute. They are interactive and make over 35 sounds. This Fingerling has a puff of hair on the head that changes color. The Fingerling also has kiss tech, which allows the Fingerling to mwaah kiss when near your cheek. They are able to sit on your index finger and interact with you. This Baby Tiger also comes with a mini. Too cute.

Our daughter has several fingerlings including the classic monkey and a dragon, so she was excited to try these new cat fingerlings. Tilly the tiger is cute and comes with a little cub also, the smaller cub isn't interactive but my daughter loves playing with it alongside its mama tiger. These fingerlings are slightly shorter than the other ones which all seemed to use the same form factor but the smaller form factor may be better for kids with smaller hands. The light up hair is a neat feature which I haven't seen on other toys of this type before.

Fingerlings are generally similar to other electronic character toys like hatchimals, pomsies, wrapples, etc.. but they seem to be a bit more robustly designed than the other mentioned toys. Both of our other fingerlings are over 2 years old and still work perfectly to this day, whereas most of the others only last a few months before they start glitching up or break entirely in our experience.

[[VIDEOID:b3da2be0818071390eed86854dc5e31d]] My daughter is a Fingerling fan plus a fan of any type of cat...so squealing was bound to happen when she saw this one. It's her first light-up Fingerling but most of it's movements/interactions are basically the same as her others, just sounds a little different (cat/panther sounds vs. monkeys, sloths, etc).

One thing different about her is that her paws hold differently and she is able to sit up on her own. She is still able to hold onto a finger and Fingerlings jungle gym. As well as fit on the Fingerlings carousel.

Allec is very cute! She comes with a mini Fingerling- her cub Ronni, which is solid plastic and does not interact in any type of way- but you can place it on a pencil or snuggle her between Allec's arms and tummy.

Allec automatically goes into sleep mode after about 5 minutes until you wake her- or she has a power switch behind her head.

The following are a few of the things Allec does that are the same interactions as our Fingerlings, however- with it being a light-up, the color of her hair reflects her mood with these interactions:

- She goes to sleep when cradled. Hair lights up blue colors and purple.

- "Kisses" (just sound) if you kiss or tap her mouth, some Fingerlings blow a kiss but she "licks" like a cat. Hair lights up red and pink.

- Passes gas and giggles when you hold her upright and press your palm down on her forehead for a few seconds. Hair lights up green and purple

- Burps and giggles when you hold her upside down and press your palm down her forehead for a few seconds. Hair lights up green and blue.

- Makes silly reactions when hanging upside down. Hair lights up red, yellow and blue

- She gets bored and makes sounds. Hair lights up blue, green, teal.

- Responds in different ways when you pet her head. Hair lights up all of the different colors.

A couple things to note: Her glitter doesn't shed. She doesn't require other separate accessories to enjoy.

[[VIDEOID:36b30626a3e7263836c748c9c3834146]] My 4-yr-old granddaughter LOVES Allec and Ronni. They are very interactive. Allec’s little tuft of hair lights up and changes color. [[VIDEOID:50defebd333a312e5a21746c698c54cc]] Super cute! My daughter really likes them and loves how the baby can hold on to mommy’s tail. Light up hair works fine. The only reason I deducted one star is because the “kiss tech” doesn’t always work. It’s supposed to detect you holding it up to your cheek and gives you a kiss but it doesn’t always do it but that’s not a deal breaker for my kid...she still likes playing with it.

My kids wanted to get a pet, but I’m not ready for that kind of commitment yet. My kids enjoy playing with this interactive lion figure set. B082D3QYP8.text: I used to make my own greeting cards with rubber stamps, so I was excited to share this craft with my 6 year old niece when she was visiting recently. This is a nice starter set for kids. The set includes pre-mounted wooden stamps, colored pencils, an 2 color ink pad and some outlined stickers of the same stamp images for coloring. The addition of the stickers was a little odd to me, because with the stamps and ink pad, you could basically make your own stickers. The stamps are a good quality. There is excess rubber around the images, so if you aren't careful when stamping, you may get the lines from the edges on your art work. I used to get stamps that had to be assembled, so I always trimmed the rubber around the edges to avoid that. The ink pad is a double one so you can carefully use just one side of the ink pad for a single color or put the rubber into the center and get both colors. There are no papers, cards, etc for stamping on to, so you need to get that. Otherwise, it's a fun activity for kids. My niece is 6 and she had a lot of fun with it.
This kit isn’t as nice as the Melissa and Doug stamp kits. It is fun. The stamp pad could be better. I ended up swapping it out for a nicer stamp pad. But the kids really enjoy the stamps.

This stamp set it very nice. It comes with so many stamps. They really like all the animals.

I would much prefer them doing something than watching something.

It is nice because they can spend the time doing it and then they have something special to keep. They are excited when they make something themselves.

This is a great activity for a rainy day or a day when your child is sick or when you are just stuck at home. It is a good way to keep a child busy.

I would recommend it.

My girls have loved these stamps! This set comes with so many options. The ink pad is great quality and does not dry out. Colored pencil in the sets are pretty cheapy but honestly the nice quality of the stamps make this set worth it

I found these to be really cute rubber stamps.  I know the product is marketed to kids but like most of the other things I order on here, I am an adult who also enjoys crafting with these kinds of things.  I like to write a lot of letters and as such I like to decorate my envelopes and stationery.  I am going to get a rainbow stamp pad with multiple ink colors for more variety but I especially loved the llama and sloth stamps that came with this as well as the colorable stickers as well. The stamps are cute and well made.  Even adults would like this set, especially if they are into fantasy critters.  Color in stickers are a nice bonus.

B082YJV68K.text: My parents had one of these in the house when I was a child. Sharing this with my own family brings back a lot of memories. This does require some assembly.
