The drop spots are named after various planets. It doesn't include all of them as there is not enough spots for them, however I found it interesting that Pluto was included. My kids are 22 and 19 and both of them found it addictive trying to get to Pluto! It was fun watching them have some non-digital time!

The game is great fun for older kids (my son is 10 and loves it) as well as adults. It is not easy to reach Saturn or Jupiter but does take practice and quite a bot of focus and precision. It is fun to play / compete along with others. Highly Recommend!

I'd originally got this for my husband's office, but it has remained at my home because my son and I love it!  It's very easy to put together and it's fun to try and beat one another, and see who can get farther.  My son is definitely the champion, as he can get to the last one, but even after getting it to the end, it's still a challenge for him every time he attempts to do it.  Eventually it will end up in my husband's office, but for now, we are all enjoying it here at home.

B083C2JBYH.text: We are a fan of the large, over sized games such as this one for outdoor parties. Friends of ours had a similar one that they took with them tailgating. These blocks are sturdy and strong. It comes with a wipe board so you can keep score and make up your own rules.  The storage bag is just okay. It's a bit thin and doesn't seem like it's going to last long. My husband has already transferred them to a plastic tub for storage. The game is a lot of fun. It needs a solid surface to play on. We've been using a wooden picnic table in our yard.
Sturdy blocks

While many games make the claim that they are suitable for the whole family - this one is actually FUN for the whole family!

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. The primary difference is the blocks are SUPERSIZED, measuring 7.1”(long) X 2.3”(wide) X 1.4”(tall). The blocks are the perfect size for little hands and kids get the hang of the game quickly and enjoy seeing the tower grow and eventually topple.

While the game’s tower begins at around 2’ it quickly grows to 4-5’+. The blocks are not only bigger but they are made of high grade pine, sanded smooth - 20 of the blocks are numbered (1-8, some numbers are duplicated while others are not) allowing players to develop a limitless number of custom games. Something we do is let the winner of each game write their name, or a short message on a block - it makes it fun to look back and remember the fun we have had during previews games.

In addition to the blocks this set comes complete with a wooden crate for storage and travel that easily doubles as a stable, flat playing surface when needed. In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. Due to the 8 block being a one of a kind, we call it the Magic 8 Block and use that as a wild card type block - the person who pulls and places it can name whatever rule they choose.

This is a game reminiscent of games of old - no batteries, nothing electronic, it will last forever, can go anywhere to be played inside or out and is loads of fun for everyone.

This is most definitely a game set I recommend. We have loved it!
So much FUN!!!

There is a number on each block should you want to play a different game with these blocks.  There is a nice laminated gameplay instruction page giving you some optional fun rules with these numbers.  This set of blocks comes in an excellent wood storage crate. Just the sheer size of the blocks causes for laughter for those familiar with the regular "jenga" brand. This served as a great get-together game night attraction. We have an amazing time playing this super sized version.

This is a super fun game for bigger kids and adults. The blocks are quite sturdy and come stored in a sturdy wooden crate. It comes complete with rules and alternative rule suggestions as well as a dry erase board to declare the rules for that game.

Now, these aren’t as big as some yard ones I’ve seen. At first that was disappointing, until we used them. The smaller kids want to play. But even at their size that starts the game off at only 2’ tall these are heavy when they fall, they’re a sturdy solid wood so of course they are. Now in the picture it says it grows to 5’...I want to see someone stack that perfectly, we don’t even come close. However, once we surpass 3’ these take quite a tumble when they come down, I don’t think I’d want to see 5’. This is definitely adult supervision if playing with the under 5 crowd. Even carrying the crate full of blocks is quite heavy so I figured they wouldn’t play it themselves anyway. Don’t underestimate small boys. They worked together to push it to the middle of the room and then dump it.

I am not saying being sturdy is a bad thing, just that kids need supervised so a block doesn’t fall on their head. With supervision though this game is fun for the WHOLE family.

We have tile floors in our house so it’s no biggie to whip this out & play. The larger size would probably allow you to play it on a lower pile rug or carpet but I don’t know. The bag it comes in is a nice touch. We’ve had a ton of fun with this already & can see it being used for years to come!

Of course we had to try it out and I have to say the quality of the blocks is great and they feel sturdy, each being made of pine wood. A few practice runs in the house and I'm confident that this set will hold together through many tumbles, even outside.

If you're looking for a jumbo sized lawn version, this may be more of the medium in-between size than that. However, this is a great sized up version from the general tumbling tower games. Overall this is a great buy for some family fun. B084K4J39K.text: My two grandkids ages 5 and 7 enjoy playing this classic game. Great game to play as a family and before bed. Great for preschoolers and learning to count. Also comes with instructions and a puzzle to play a cooperative version of the game which we haven't played yet.
Came on time just as described.
I purchased a number of games to occupy all the kids when they visit for family Saturdays.  This was a hit for the adults too.

You really can't go wrong with this game if you've got little ones around(unless, of course, they put things other than food in their mouth, and then I'd save this for later). It's a classic board game for a reason.

My husband has fond memories of playing this game with his grandmother, but about a month ago was the first time I'd ever played it. My children have fallen in love with the game, and I'm thrilled they've had the chance to experience it. It's cute and fun!

It's a really quick and simple game to play, and easy enough for very young players to be included, since counting only goes to 4 in the game. (Again, the fruit is very small, though, so don't have it around those that put things in their mouths.) It's actually just right for my 3 year old, and while it's technically too easy for my 5 and 8 year old children, they still love playing it.

Also, with small pieces, I appreciate that there are 4 extra pieces of fruit(one of each color) included in case one goes missing.

Overall, this is a perfect game for preschoolers to play, as long as they don't put things in their mouth.
This game is awesome! This has a cheap pricebtag and is cheaply made. You get what you pay for.

At first glance my daughter seemed quite intrigued by the little fruity pieces. In the meantime, I was just wondering silently how long it would take for us to lose a few of the tiny things, whereas if we did, we'd have to throw the whole game away. Anyway, that was our first impression.

As we started the game, I found it very annoying to have to load all the little fruit pieces onto the board, 40 in all. 40 pieces tinier than a marble. And if you take your basket out of the hole, the little fruit pieces will roll into the hole where the basket was and to retrieve it you have to disrupt the entire board and put back all 40 pieces again. That is of course worst case, but it did (and WILL) happen, and was annoying.

You spin the spinner and if it lands on a number, you take that many fruits off your tree. If the spinner lands on the dog or bird you give back 2, and if it lands on the spilled basket, you give back everything in your basket.

There is a little over a 40% chance that the spinner will land you on one of the spaces where you need to give back your fruits. My poor daughter, through hard luck, kept landing on either the number 1, the dog, or the bird. So whatever little she got, she would have to keep putting it back.

This game bored me to tears and worst of all it made my daughter very sad. She did not have a fit but she just had a really sad face every time the spinner landed on the dog or bird. This game is pure luck, so there was no way to exercise her mind except for counting up to 4 fruits or taking away 2 of them.

Would not recommend. NOT FUN AT ALL. Lots of better games out there.
Oh.....the fun these students will have.  All while learning, so it is a win win for all.  Fun to be had by all.

Cute! Orange (oranges), blue (blueberries), red (cherries) and green (apples) fruits all look like the original cherries in this updated version. Bird--turn over a puzzle piece of the included puzzle. Spilled barrel--give all your fruit back to the tree. If you put together the puzzle before all the fruit is in barrels, then you lose, in the Cooperative version. You can also play the original version and just not use the included puzzle. Good game, very similar to what I remember from my childhood, with the primary difference being that there are now four different fruit (blue berries, cherries, green apples, and oranges) rather than just all cherries, which can be somewhat of a pain since now you have to sort out the fruit when setting up. Not a big deal though.

The game came in quite the unassembled state, which while not a huge deal, I was a bit disappointed by the fact that even the game board required me to fold all four sides down and tape them (no tape was provided) to set the game board in its elevated state. I ended up actually using a hot glue gun rather than tape. I also used the hot glue gun to adhere the spinner base to the bottom of the spinner card, ensuring the spinner would operate more reliably.

I would like to have seen the game come with at least the board properly built, and I would also have liked to see the game built such that the spinner mounts in the middle of the main game board, rather than being its own separate entity that must be passed around. If memory serves, that was how the original game I played in my youth was designed.

Otherwise, the directions were clearly written, there was a new game play version focusing on cooperative play that employs the use of an included puzzle to provide the "competition", which may eventually be an enjoyable alternative version (we haven't played that version yet), and the graphics were decent and not overbearing like so many other of the modern remakes of classic kids' board games.

The final say on the game: my 3 year old daughter loves it.

B084L326V8.text: My 11 yr old son loves Uno and spongebob so this will make a great present or stocking stuffer for him.
Played a competitive game of uno Saturday night, truly fun game. The memes are a little funny too.

Uno has been a favorite of mine since I was a child, so when I saw this Spongebob version I had to have it. The cards all have game related memes with character illustrations from different show episodes. There is also the added twist of four “draw six”  wild cards that can quickly change the game. I’ve enjoyed playing this version of Uno with my family while we’re home so much. It’s been a nice distraction and who doesn’t love Spongebob?

The quality is the same as usual....recent years Uno decks. The colors are fine but arent the original primary colors....this one has a purple shade as red....which makes sense because there isnt a lot of red on the cartoon. These cards are easy to suffle.

With theme decks of Uno most people add to the collection because they simply like the characters. This game doesnt change up anything really other than a nasty draw six card we've seen before in different versions. To me CoCo was one of the best because the new rule for that involved being able to remember a previous color card played. That was great. Also, Uno Flip is a whole different dynamic that changes it up a bit.

If you like Spongebob but missed earlier editions that people now think are gold and are trying to sell for 35 and more a deck used...lol....just get these. The memes on them dont effect play whether you think they are cute or not. And if you miss out, dont worry....somebody will buy them all up and try to charge 15 dollars or more a deck by Christmas. :(

Its 6 bucks...if you like Spongebob or know someone who does, this is just fine.
Easy to play, fun to look at with all the colors. Enjoyed it.
My cousin was having a spongebob themed party so I bought these to play with. They were cute, durable and got the job done. They are normal playing cards so expect to get just that!

This is generally a cute Sponge Bob themed UNO set. The cards are bright and colorful with cute Sponge Bob pictures. My 5 year old loves it (both Sponge Bob and UNO). My big issue is that this set doesn't include the rules of UNO so I had to look them up (because I haven't played UNO in decades.) Also the set includes a new card I've never seen and I cannot figure out how to play it or use it. It is a special card that says "You didn't say UNO." Usually you just call out someone for not saying UNO and they have to pick up two cards. Not sure how to use these. Can you only call someone out for not saying UNO if you have this card? How can you go out if you are stuck with it? Really I have no idea and a rather extensive internet search has not explained what it's for, so we have just taken it out.

Generally, we like the set. It's a fun update, though plain old UNO cards would have been just fine. I honestly just wish it came with directions.
Good, the box was a little messed up but we had fun playing it. I was expecting spongebob memes but they were uno related memes I can’t complain tho

I’ve included photos of each of the cards. The game comes with a special rule, but you don’t have to play with the new rule. We didn’t bother with it.

My kids had fun with this version.  This would be a cute gift for the Sponebob loving uno fanatic.  This deck of cards is small enough to be a stocking stuffer or Easter basket filler.

B08575MSSN.text: This is an interesting game that works best for larger groups. You also need a plenty of space for the game play. Rather than guessing the actions of the players, you are trying to figure out the intensity levels of the performers. I found it helpful to watch the video that was on the game description before playing. There are 10 different intensity levels. I think it would be easier to play (especially with kids) if there were fewer levels. It can be difficult to determine the difference between an intensity level 5 and an intensity level 6. I guess that's a way to keep the tokens from being handed out too quickly. You don't take turns like many games, so it's engaging for all the players which is good when you have children playing. Overall, it's a fun, new game.

I like when my kids play games because it so much better than staring at a screen. This was a very fun game for my kids. They really enjoyed it. It kept their interest. I really like that it gets them playing with others. It is great for them to play with each other or with us. We like to have family game nights.

This game wasn’t too hard for them to learn. The quality was very good. It held together fine. I really think it’s a lot of fun for them. I also like to give games as gifts. I would recommend this one.

I bought this game because we're having a big family gathering and I wanted a game that my son on the autism spectrum could play.  Charades as a whole is extremely too abstract for him to develop the character he needs to emulate.  This game gives very specific instructions, that while still fun, is beneficial to him.
This is a fun game to play with our kids. They are 12, 9, and 6. It is fairly simple to understand.

This game was a hit from 6 years old all the way to 37. Our family had a blast laughing at each other. Super easy for everyone to catch on and a great time for all. Would reccomend to all my friends.

We absolutely are boardgame addicts and consistently look for something new and fun to play when our friends are over... This past weekend, we tried this game. On a Scale of One to T-Rex is a family-friendly movement-based game that kept us engaged for twenty minutes. Conceptually, my 7 year old had difficulty with this game and my teen thought this game was better for younger kids. My husband and I both agreed that either you have to have some very extroverted people or get drunk for this...

We love  playing this it’s a riot! And young kids can play too, we just modify for two players as it’s better played with several people. We also love and have  the other games from the same makers, exploding kittens, bears v babies, throw throw burrito.

We played "on a scale from 1 to t-rex" on New Year's eve with another couple. I wanted to like this game, it was even on my xmas list. But I just couldn't like it. We were even drinking enough to be loose and silly, but not enough to not comprehend the rules. We are a fairly with it bunch with 3 masters degrees spread across 4 people, who like The Oatmeal and have enjoyed playing Exploding Kittens. I say that because we basically are the target demo here and this was just a flop.

The intensity miming is very odd and the scoring is way too complex for the otherwise seemingly straightforward objectives. We were all frusterated and just did not enjoy ourselves.

Two stars tho for good packaging, production quality and design.

Busy out a video camera on this one. It takes a minute for everyone to understand the rules. I suggest playing a practice round first. Once everyone gets going it is absolutely hilarious!!! Be prepared, it can get loud. Watching my parents, sister, nieces, and my son with autism play this was the best thing ever. After reading rave reviews, I purchased Zingo for my three and five-year-olds. After three times playing it, though, we weren't having ANY fun. I didn't understand what we were missing from the game. My five-year-old is on the cusp of reading but without any pictures or anything, I just didn't get it. There are only so many M&M's I can bribe them with.

I just came back to Amazon to see what I was missing and realized I purchased Zingo SIGHT WORDS and not the original Zingo (which is also sight words). I have no idea how I did this or that there was a difference. I just ordered the original and I have high hopes my kids will enjoy seeing words with pictures a little bit more than they will enjoy learning words like "where" and "there."

If you purchase this for your beginning reader, please do yourself a favor and make sure you're getting Zingo in the red box.
very nice and loved by my nephew.

We have another Zingo game (the one with the pictures only) and my son loved it.  Now that he is getting closer to reading, I thought this might be a fun game to help build that skill. I was totally right.  He is early in his reading so he still needs a little help, but this is so fun and I can already see that he is getting better at recognizing words. I highly recommend this product!
This game is so much fun to play with my grandchildren. They had so much fun and we laughed and played it over and over again.

If you have a child like mine, taking turns is a challenge, the idea of losing is mind melting, and patience is not yet a virtue. Zingo is a great game to start using those skills at an early age. While this game is mostly touted for teaching pre-reading skills, I have found that it is a great game for learning to take turns. Learning to lose graciously is so not easy so this game is a great starter to ease into that. I've found that the sting of losing hurts a little less when you allow everyone to cover their board, but also state, "this person actually won the game since they covered the board first, but everyone finished."

In Zingo there are yellow chips with various pictures, smile, shoe, cat, dog with the word written on the bottom. There are 6 "bingo" cards with those various pictures on them as well. One person slides the red chip holder forward and two chips slide out. If you have one of those pictures on your board, shout out the word first and you get the chip to cover your board. The first person to cover every picture wins the game. The two sides are merely easy and more competitive. You can choose to do regular bingo rules like four corners or X marks the spot. Cleanup is easy because the chips all sit in the red holder. Kids love the game because of the red slider and ability to use their outside voice inside, and adults love it because surprise!, you're learning!
Great game to introduce letters, spelling & reading. Also built to last.
Great fun. Children love matching games. This one fills the bill!
This is great! My child is learning her sight words in a fun and easy way! I love this game. I am going to purchase more games from Zingo.
Gifted to grandson-great family activity

Zingo-Bingo is just like bingo.  .. but with pictures/words.  Great vocabulary builder.  Though it shows for ages 4 and up, it might also work for some slightly younger kids, as they can simply look at the pictures.  I think it’s nice to have an adult/parent play along, because then they can stress the reading / spelling of each word.  Otherwise most kids are just going to look at the pictures.  Though you can play with just two players, I think it’s a little more fun with three or more.  There are a few more versions of this game, including one with numbers, and one with words.  They are all great fun and very educational.

My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.

This game is absolutely great for children learning simple math. It is a a fun way for them to practice as well as learn the simple science for winning and losing with tantrums. I would totally by it again and recommend it to anyone who has or works with children.

My three year old son is obcessed with this game. My other kids will play but not with his enjoyment. I see how it helps his memory and focus. It's a great game to learn names of objects. I had this game for years and just got a new one because mine had missing pieces. I'm thrilled that the pieces are now two sided so they're easier to sort and put away. The slot idea is cute but in reality it doesn't work  because it needs to much force, so it's difficult for kids and if I'm sitting on the side of the board I need both hands to push it in. We end up opening the cover during play to pop the pieces back on top quickly.
Good game for kids to play with adults.  They learn many skills: taking turns, patience and excitement.

I got this for my daughter, who is in kindergarten, who is really struggling with learning her sight words and does not enjoy flash cards.  We are not to the point to play the game as instructed, instead we are just popping the plastic chips out of the word dispenser and reading them together and then trying to find the match on our cards.  My 4 year old is also joining in, once again more as a matching game as she can't read these words yet either.  They like sliding the word dispenser and popping the plastic chips back in if there's no match.  There are six cards and all are printed front and back for the choice of twelve cards (the game says the green side is less competitive and the red side is more competitive), and there are nine words on each card.  Here are my reasons for 4 stars:  The sight words that are reviewed are as follows: and, are, come, for, have, here, in, me, my, now, our, said, she, the, there, they, three, two, want, we, went, what, where, who.  Being there are only 24 words, and in kindergarten (at least at my daughter's school) she is learning 50, so I wish there were more words to learn in the game (like the word "she" is played but not the word "he")  Also the word "she" is only on one out of the twelve cards; it seems that some words are focused on more than others.  So while I still find this game is helpful, the girls find it fun, and it was very easy to set-up and learn, I do wish it was more in-depth.

B089LJ9148.text: This was a fun puzzle to complete. It brought back lots of memories from an old favorite TV show. The quality of the pieces is good. I didn't come across any that had the image separating from the rest of it. The image quality was okay. It was clear enough to differentiate, but could have been crisper. I do wish it came with a poster of the image. In my old age, I'm finding it really helpful to have a poster to work with so I don't have to rely on the box lid as much.

EDIT: initially I reviewed this before really getting into the puzzle. I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

The Friends 1000 piece jigsaw puzzle is an officially licensed puzzle depicting over 100 scenes from one of the most successful sitcoms in history.

From the central perk logo and Rachel entering in her wedding dress in the first episode to the Halloween party and Pheobe learning to ride a bike. It's all there along with some of the better known catch phrases such as Joey doesn't share food and you are my lobster.

I like doing jigsaws, especially in recent times with Covid 19 when you are better off staying in than going out and this is a good depiction of one of my favorite sitcoms. Given the variety of the scenes covered it was actually fairly easy to put together, no big swathes of blue sky where one tile looks exactly the same as the next.

If you like Friends and you're looking for something to while away a few hours then get this and start putting it together whilst watching re-runs.

I enjoy working jigsaw puzzles and thought this would be fun. It is an interesting puzzle, but two things made it frustrating to solve:

Many of the pieces are the same shape and they fit together even if they do not belong together. Sometimes you can figure that out because of the images, but other times....

It can be difficult to tell what pieces go together because the pictures are not sharply defined. I ended up putting things together only to have to take them apart later. I don't find that challenging, I find it frustrating.

The pieces themselves are made well. They are not thin or flimsy.

If you are a Friends fan you will probably enjoy putting this puzzle together. But it would have been more fun without the problems I mention here.

this is a big puzzle (on a card table for size)!  big puzzles are like the big books - looks of time spent on them makes them a little more personal.  this puzzle was no different and i spent a lot of time on it.  notable points - it does not come with a separate photo/poster of the puzzle.  you have to work off the small photo on the box.  there is no alpha map - which is 100% acceptable, i've just been noticing the map on the back of many puzzles lately so now I think it's important to note whether it's there or not.  the pieces are limited to rectangular two-outie/two-innie shapes - there are loads of variations within these, but there are no non-traditional shapes, so I put this together based on scene and color.  because of that you will come across some false positives - got tripped up on two sections of the edge and the title section in the middle.  lastly the entire puzzle is somewhat muted - meaning the colors are kind of flat vs some of the shinier puzzles.  I am not sure why i am noting this fact other than again - based on other puzzles.  if you were going to frame it - it might actually look better under glass - i am not framing it though.  This one is definitely for a Friends fan!  There are so many memorable scenes represented spanning the entire series and it's really focused on the core 6 - the only non-core in the puzzle is Mike and you don't even see his face, poor Mike. I love doing jigsaw puzzles, but I realize now that I have specific likes and dislikes about them. First of all, I prefer "easier" collage puzzles rather than very challenging jigsaw puzzles (like a photo of a black cat or a borderless puzzle with repeating images). I do jigsaw puzzles to relax but I don't want to stress about them or have to work too hard.

Initially I thought I would enjoy this puzzle as it is a collage. However, similar photos of the same characters was frustrating In addition, the photos aren't super sharp so the details that you need to find a piece can be difficult to locate. The other issue I had with this puzzle is that there only seem to be two types of shapes for the pieces, which can lead to issues when pieces kind of fit together but aren't a real fit. For these reasons, I didn't completely enjoy this puzzle, but if you enjoy Friends and enjoy jigsaw puzzles, this might be ideal for you. If nothing else, it reminds you of all the wonderful moments on this excellent TV show. I guess I just don't need to see 40 different Joey's and squint at the box to figure out which scene with Joey the piece I have goes with.

This is a nice flash card set, it is easy to use and feels pretty durable. Some of the words are a little bit more difficult but I think that’s good for exposure to bigger words for younger ages. My two-year-old is a fan of using these and I’m sure will get plenty more use out of them in the years to come. We don’t handle these gently and they’ve held up great so far. Like most other Melissa and Doug products we have we are pretty very happy with these for our kiddo.

My almost 14-month old son absolutely loves these cards.  He doesn't understand letters or really many words yet, but he loves the card with the cat (his favorite animal) and loves pushing in the dots to make them pop.  Unfortunately, five of the dots out of the package don't work - won't stay pushed through, so when you flip it over, it's already "popped".  He doesn't really care, but looks a little disappointed when he tries to pop a dot and it won't pop.  But it definitely bothers me.  Worse, all three of the dots on the S/T are broken, so this means that card gets the least "love" of the box.

I love these, the size, thickness, and style of them. However quite a few of the bubbles wont stay popped to one side. I thought it was just the one I ordered, so I returned and ordered another BUT the new one is the same way just with different cards. This is very frustrating to a child.

Very nice. Bigger than expected.

This is a nice set of letter cards - sturdy, nice colorful illustrations, etc.

But obviously what sets this apart is the "pop" dot thingy, which is a good idea, IMHO. It seems like the satisfying CLICK! of the pop dot would be a nice little bonus for getting a letter right. But, my daughter never really cared - she barely popped them while using the cards. Of course, your experience may be different!

So, overall, this is a nice set. Just don't be shocked if the "pop" dots aren't a huge draw...

There are letters on both sides of each card but most of the poke a dot only work on one side. If you poke they just pop right back or don’t stay at all. This makes much are the cards no fun and frustrating to my 3 year old. Maybe I got a bad batch.

I got this poke-a-dot jumbo alphabet learning cards for my 15 month old daughter because she’s about time to start learning alphabet. I have to say these learning cards are awesome for toddlers to learn as their first learning tool. The quality of the cards is perfect. These cards are way thicker than I expected, and they are perfect for those who still put everything into their mouth before doing anything. Like my daughter, who always tastes the things in her hands when she first gets. Also, I am pleased with the design. These cards are colorful, using bright color to attract toddlers eye balls. Pictures are cute and easy to recognize what they are.

I still have no idea what those popping dots are used for, but my daughter seems to enjoy popping them a lot. I guess it’s because it makes funny sounds when she pops. In overall, these learning cards are so great to keep a set at home. It’s also nice to gift since it comes with a box, can be used as storage purpose, with handles. Highly recommend this product.

My son loves the Poke-a-dot products unfortunately I had to take a star off, because the poke-a-dots on these cards are a little flimsy and some of them do not “pop” into place. The cards are heavy duty and not easily folded/bent so they should last us a long time. Shame some of the dots don’t work.

I love Melissa and Doug toys!  They are always hands on without electronics and durable learning toys.  This letter/word set is no different.  They are nice and durable and also have the perfect little popping circles in each card to keep the kids entertained!  They are also inexpensive like all of their toys.  Highly recommend!

I am always so impressed with the quality of products they make and this was no exception. Very durable and sturdy which is nice as you can give them to a younger child and they won't damage them.

Each card is double sided and has a reference letter and 3 words on each side accompanied by a Poke-A-Dot. Each little plastic dot "pops" when pressed and then you can flip it over and pop it back from the other side. The images that accompany the letters are commonly used words I would say, but they toss in a few over the course of the set that are a little less common (fine with me, the bigger the vocabulary, the better). Overall, I foresee these getting a lot of use and getting toted around a lot by our toddler.

When I purchased this product for my son for Christmas, I wasn't quite sure what it did, if he would like it, or if it would be worth the money. I took advantage of a lightning deal and I'm very glad I did! It was the surprise hit this Christmas and I was very impressed with its durability and the ease with which my son was able to use it. It does a great job of encouraging creativity and provides a lot of sensory input, whether you are listening to those rattling magnet sounds, erasing the magnet balls with your fingers, or experiencing the satisfaction of just filling in all the dots. This toy provides my son with a creative outlet that he finds satisfying while offering up great opportunities to improve his fine motor skills. We play with this together, taking turns drawing designs and erasing them, and he plays with it by himself, filling in the dots and making patterns with his finger.

I plan on purchasing the similar products using the alphabet and numbers. I would recommend this product for preschoolers and early elementary age children. Parents with children who deal with developmental disabilities or sensory integration disorders might want to give this a try as it seems to satisfy on many levels.

Please note that the magnets can be pretty loud when they roll around and click into place. Also, I wish that the magnet wand came attached to the pad. It clicks securely into the spot provided, but what kid always remembers to put it back? This is an excellent purchase! The educational and entertainment value make it well worth the price whether it's a lightning deal or not.

B08PTZ2VKX.text: This is a fun deck of cards. The card quality is very good and comparable to most decks of cards. The images are clear. It has a nice variety of characters from the show. This would make a great gift for Outlander fans.

I certainly love the intention and idea of these cards. However, I'm not 100% behind the execution.

The positives:
Cards are fairly high quality
Each card, except for the jokers, are different - the sam characters are on each card, but are shown in a different pose within each suit

The negatives:
These are standard size cards - which is not a negative - but the result is that the impact of the images when the cards are in your hand is not nearly as good as when you look at the images of the cards on your computer screen.

Would have liked more negative characters (or even locations) instead of all the positive characters with only Jonathan Randall as the jack card. Most noticeably absent are Dougal MacKenzie, Stephen Bonnet, and Geillis Duncan. Not sure how they would have included these characters (and others) as it would have meant different characters on the same valued cards between the suits. Still, having more of the negative characters would have contributed to some interesting thematic experiences and maybe even made it possible to create some new games. With only Jonathan Randall this is not really possible at all.

Neutral:
Themed decks like this always cost more than a normal deck. One reason is the licensing fees the publisher has to pay. Another reason is that these decks have far smaller print runs than generic decks which increases the cost to make each deck. In other words, the MSRP is within the typical parameters.

I do like this deck. However, as a fan of Outlander I do wish they'd gone further with more characters allowing for more thematic use of the cards. Still, it's also unusual that they used different images on all the cards (outside of the jokers) so that is a positive.

If you're a fan of the show and you play card games then this is definitely worth a look regardless of my criticisms. It's not like you have another Outlander theme deck of cards you can buy instead. This deck is it and it's pretty good.

B08Q8PLH1N.text: I’d prefer more simple ingredients and real sweetener to artificial sweeteners. If you are Leto or low carb these would be great for you.

I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Inside the sealed packet the frosting mix is in a pouch, but the donut mix is just loose in the pouch. Getting the frosting packet out was a very messy proposition.

Making the mix is simple (needs water and oil). The included silicone molds are very thin and flimsy, and need to be inserted into a muffin pan to minimize the chance of spilling. This is the step kids will need the most assistance with.

But even if the donuts bake properly, they are no treat to eat. The chocolate flavor is not pleasant, and is made even worse by the artificial sweetener aftertaste. The texture is not bad considering these are gluten-free, but the taste is not good to the point where these are barely (and I mean barely!) edible.

Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.

Review for: PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar

I found the finished product of these donuts to be mediocre. The taste of the donut itself was ok but they were a bit dry. The frosting has an obvious sugar substitute taste. Being vegan, I know there are ways to make delicious desserts.

The kit does include most of the things that are needed to make the donuts. It is a fun project for kids to do with an adult to supervise. I do think the kit is overpriced for what it is.

The pros are my kids enjoyed making these and the donuts taste really good. The con-and it's a big one-is that this is pretty pricey for what you get. If money isn't an issue then by all means go for this. However, if you want cheaper options please know they exist.

The packaging on this kit is ridiculous. I appreciate it is meant to be given as a gift, but there is so much extra in places and then where there needs to be more, everything is stuffed inside one bag.

The main mix had the coconut "sprinkles" and the glaze mixed stuffed inside and the glaze mix had a hole so part of the glaze had mixed in to the donut mix. There was absolutely no way to separate out the two powdered mixes, so I just carefully put the remaining glaze in a bowl and made the donut mix with the glaze mix inside.

We did not use the sprinkles.

This mix is considered to be keto and low carb, but if you follow total carbs, this is not for you. There are 26 grams of carbs with 18 grams of allulose. Even though allulose is considered by some to be ketogenic friendly, I count total carbs, so these donuts were a crazy splurge for me.

The directions for these donuts ask for water and avocado oil. I had this crazy feeling water and oil would leave this mix bland. I used one egg, heavy whipping cream and butter. I mixed the glaze as suggested with almond milk and my husband applied the coconut.

My husband really liked these. I thought they were just okay.

At $25 this kit is really expensive. You do get six donut molds that are extremely hard to clean (I have other silicone molds that easily wash with soap and water, but these took soaking) but easy to use, so there is a tradeoff. I think this kit could be made by buying the parts independently for less money.

Planet Bake needs to work on their packaging and maybe try out their mixes with different ingredients and offer alternative ingredient suggestions for people who want to add some fat and protein to their keto donuts.

This would make a wonderful gift! The mix is so easy to make. It just needs water and oil. It also has sprinkles, coconut shavings and icing, but I think they taste great plain! The kit being vegan is also a plus. The only downside is it’s a little pricey, but it’s a good activity to do with kids.

I got this for my 3 1/2 year-old that loves donuts and really likes to help in the kitchen. The directions were easy to follow and all of the ingredients were prepackaged so that made it very easy for her to do all of the pouring and mixing on her own. These donuts tasted good, but they were like chocolate cake in a donut shape. We have made both the vanilla and chocolate from this brand. Our family prefers the vanilla even though we are chocolate lovers. This was like a dense cake which we found kind of dry and the vanilla was more tender.
This set came with 6 silicone molds that you can reuse to make more donuts in the future. It also contains sugar sprinkles, coconut sprinkles (unsweetened coconut), frosting mix, and flour mix. All you really need is oil for the flour mix and water or milk for the frosting mix. The frosting mix directions stated to put 2 to 3 teaspoons of milk or water. At first, we used 2 teaspoons of almond milk and it wasn’t mixing everything. Then we upped it to 3 teaspoons which made it a thin frosting. The frosting tastes pretty terrible on its own but on the donut it’s just fine. The package states that the donuts cook in 15 minutes but mine will be done after 12. Be sure to keep an eye on them or you will have nothing to eat.
Some problems I found with this product were minor but still disappointing. First, the package of sugar sprinkles was very weakly sealed and opens way too easily. Second, the coconut shreds and the frosting mix were inside of the package with the flour mix. I wish that all four packages were separate because we got flour mix all over the place trying to remove these from the package while pouring everything into the bowl. Ultimately, I had to rinse them under the water because I needed to keep them on my countertop since we couldn’t make the frosting right away and the coconut shreds were for the topping after everything was done. Third, I did notice some discrepancies between the package directions and the directions that came on the card inside the box. The package called for 3.5 ounces of water whereas the card said 3 ounces. I opted for 3.5 ounces to make the donut more moist. But why is there this discrepancy? Also, the calories are different on the package mix compared to the back of the box. They really should get their information straight before they start printing it in multiple places.
* we used our own sprinkles on some of the donuts because not everyone in this house likes coconut or sugar sprinkles

The presentation is very nice, with the little pink ribbons and the cute pictures with Happy Easter greetings, but they may require more patience than a 4-year-old can muster. At what age do kids stop hunting for Easter eggs?

Again, these are cute, but they require a lot of effort.
