There is another set from Melissa & Doug that is five dollars less, but this one is worth the extra since most little boys are interested in fire trucks, police cars, etc. Also it gives an opportunity to teach the kinds of vehicles that can be recognized in real life versus a plain car.

These are super cute, made with the same high quality we have come to expect from Melissa and Doug. Our 1-1/2 year old grandson was more than pleased with both the stacking buildings and the vehicles. We combines this set with the "Kids Carpet Playmat Rug City Life Great for Playing with Cars and Toys - Play, Learn and Have Fun Safely" -- the road sizes are perfect for the vehicles and the buildings in this set go right along with what is on the playmat. We are very pleased with both purchases, and anticipate many hours of fun imaginative play to come.

The wooden cars with it are great quality, brightly colored, and very durable. The box buildings with it are, as other reviewers mentioned quite flimsy. I received two of the buildings crushed, but my two year old did sit on the Amazon box they were in so that didn't help. I did reinforce mine with clear duct tape and packaging tape. It helped but didn't look great. We put ours on a felt city rug we found for a 3d effect. My 2 year old loves the cars but didn't care much about the buildings honestly. But I wish the buildings were plastic so they'd hold up in case he does begin to take more interest in them.
My 3 year granddaughter loves this.
Great quality and price! Kids love it!

I bought this set for our grandson's first birthday. To me, Melissa and Doug have always equaled high quality. Not this set. The wooden cars are great and will last forever; however, the nesting squares that represent a garage for each corresponding vehicle (police car goes in the police garage) are made of cardboard with the design of each glued on.
In no time, the design on one garage was lifting at the corner and without gluing, would have soon ripped off. another took a glancing step from a toddler foot and bent. Don't waste your money as this toy won't last.
The vehicles are cute but I was very disappointed that the buildings are just cardboard boxes. I had the impression it was all wood.

The stackable boxes are a little bit too close in size to each other so for a two year old boy it’s not as easy to stack as it should be. Also I expected it to be made of some thing a little sturdier than cardboard. Otherwise the concept is adorable and the cars are really cute!

I did not realize that the garages were just made of cardboard, perhaps I did not read the description closely enough.  I love Melissa and Doug toys but had hoped this would be suitable for outdoor play and the cardboard garages are definitely not.

It probably says in the description but I was shopping quick. The buildings are all cardboard with large stickers covering them. Still fairly durable maybe but I was assuming that they would be wood like the cars that came with it. Melissa and Doug typically has better quality than cardboard items. :/ my kids are all a little older so more gentile.  They played with them for maybe an hour and you can see the corner is already pulling up from the fire station. If you want it to stay nice I would definitely not recommend this product for a child under four years old even the expect wear

This is a cute set, and the cars are wooden/good quality and what I would expect from Melissa and Doug…however, the garages are cardboard. Most of ours were smashed and broken within a few days of play.
Bought this for my grandson for Christmas. Loves it

I really like this for my 2 year old grandson he likes it we call it his town! It keeps him entertained and stored Nicky and little sister 8 months can play around with boxes and cars too because it is safe!!

B0912NYVDB.text: This is a really cute way to give children a headstart on learning to save. My 5 year old grandson just loves this and is always looking for spare change to add to the safe. I am deducting a star simply because I am not sure how long this may last. The door was not easy to unlock and, once it was, I was afraid that it would come of the hinges unless I took a lot of care to open and close it. I know that if my grandson was doing it, this would have been in the stash already. I think you should look for a sturdier device.

This is a fun robot piggy bank. It has large buttons on the front that are easy to operate. It is powered by 3 AA batteries (not included). It is a convenient size that is perfect for a desk, bookshelf, or under the bed. You can feed bills in through a slot on the front. This is an excellent item that will help your children learn how to responsibly handle their own money.

This is a fun, plastic pin protected bank for kids. My 4 year old daughter loves the pink color and fact she knows the code all by herself. I put tape over the speaker to make it quiet which helped with the volume. It is decently made and a good price point.

First know that this requires 3 AA batteries that are not included. My daughter loves this thing and it is actually pretty good quality. I say actually because I don't recall ever hearing of the brand and she's never had a toy like this one before. It makes different sounds and there's a an electronic slot to insert bills into- which according to my daughter is one of the best things about it. It also has a coin slot on-top though it doesn't make any sounds or anything when coins are inserted into it.

It comes with a PIN that can be changed. My daughter really likes that, as well.

It holds a pretty good amount of bills and coins but note that if the door is opened the money falls out. Though, it doesn't even have to be used as a piggy bank. It's fun to keep their prized possessions "safely" in it 😊

The coloring is really cute

I don't really have many complaints- it is a bit loud and the sounds can get obnoxious sometimes but that's many toys 😏 So I didn't hold off for that but figured it was worth noting about the sound
Easy for the kid to use, she set up the password. Puts money in and it feed in, lasting a long time.

We gave my daughter a bank like this when she turned 5.
My son has wanted one ever sense.
This bank does a good job at sucking in the bills -which is awesome.
If the door is left open for a long period of time a beep reminder is given.
There is no volume control - its just loud.
The voice messages are super hard to understand what they are saying.
It’s like they are slurring their “s” sounds or something.
We like to just leave it on the Beep setting which is actually the toggle turned to “voice” - so that’s confusing.
Overall a fun way to show kids how to save money!
3 AA batteries are required and not included.
A tiny screwdriver is needed to open the battery compartment.

This is a cute bank that looks like a safe.  The inside is hollow, so you can store cash or small precious items. Be aware to lay the bank on it's back when you open, because the items inside will spill out.  When you open the door it sounds like a squeaky door opening. The posting does state anything that is not true except the quality of the plastic.  I like this bank it's cute, and my little guy likes putting money in it, but eventually we had to financially cut him off. LOL
Great concept but even with directions on how to change password it didn’t work

I'm seriously kicking myself for letting my daughter have this before I tried it out myself. She got super excited and started putting her hard earned savings into the correct slots. The bills were no problem. They feed right into the bank with no problems at all. The coin slot doesn't make any fun noises or do anything fun, but oh well, you can't have everything, right? What I didn't notice until she had half of her coins in, was that the coins weren't falling into the body of the bank. There's a little hollowed out area in the top of the bank where the coins fall, and while there is a slot that the coins are SUPPOSED to drop through into the main body of the bank, the coins weren't dropping through and are now stuck in the top of the bank, with no opening to remove them, other than the tiny coin slot. After spending a good 30 minutes with a butter knife trying to help her fish her precious pennies out of the coin slot in the top and having little success we finally gave up. The only way they're coming out is if we smash the thing. Fantastic. The quality of the bank isn't great over all, and the coin debacle made me like it even less. Save yourself a lot of hassle and a sad kid and get something else.

I didn't really need a piggy bank, but it's a fun thing to keep money in.  Unlike the old style piggy bank, you can insert coins and dollars into it (the dollar bills go through a slot like a bill changer at a car wash or arcade) and then enter the code you set to remove them like a safe.  So no smashing it open when you want to take money out.  Of course it's not as sturdy as a real safe.

I like the concept of this little bank, especially for my youngest as he isn't as good at counting money yet and he has a large volume of pennies! The passcode set up is simple, but it will automatically reset when the batteries die. This is problematic if the toy/bank isn't used often. The other issue is that the directions for use are printed on the outside of the box, so you'll want to cut that part out and find a place to store it because it's not as intuitive to reset as you might expect.

Still, it overall works well and seems to register the money correctly. It's not as sturdy as I'd prefer, but it's not an expensive piece so that's to be expected. A good toy or gift for a young child, especially if they like to save up for larger items!

My almost 3 year-old granddaughter LOVES this bank! I took a photo to show you how easy it is for her to operate it and how much fun she has with it! She will play with it non stop for about an hour(!) dropping all the coins I can find into the slot, feeding in paper bills, and then opening the combination and doing it over and over. I left the default combination of 0000. She has no problem pressing the buttons to unlock it. She can turn the knob to open the safe, but then often has a bit of trouble pulling the door open. But she absolutely loves this. I just need more coins and paper money for her to feed to it!

I have two complaints/suggestions: (1) there ought to be a way to totally turn off the sound. You can change it between a computer voice, and beeps/ringer/slot machine sound—but no option for off. I also cannot figure out how to turn down the volume. (2) it would be great if this bank actually counted the money or had some way to help teach the children about money and counting. It just accepts the coins and “draws in” the bills, but that is all just mechanical and there is no math aspect to it.

This is truly a TOY as advertised—it is not a “bank” for storing your money. It is made of plastic and could be easily carried away or broken open if someone really wanted to get to the money inside without the combination code.

This would make a great gift for any child.

I write honest reviews to help others make informed purchases because I read reviews myself and appreciate how helpful they can be. I hope that my review helped you!
It’s really nice and my niece is learning how to save money. So far so good it’s able to hold what we have put in it so far.

[[VIDEOID:245e3431bb5f5fc7ae16715acc94dfea]] This is a great "toy" that can be an educational one if you make it so. This toy allows your children to learn about money, and possibly the value of a dollar. This gets them excited about saving that hard earned money! This money vault accepts bills and coins, separate slots for them. Don't try to put anything other than bills, such as a gift card, because it will get stuck. You can pull it out by opening the vault but that may break the rolling mechanism if misused. Once you start putting the bills the rolling mechanism in the machine gets going and will keep rolling for 10-15 seconds after you're done. I had a lot of fun with my little one putting in the bills and coins. We haven't changed the passcode and just used the factory set code. There are two different sound effects but no volume control - the switch button is inside the vault (watch the video I posted). I think this is a great toy, well made. No, it is not the highest quality for a piggy bank but it is meant to be more of a toy and for this price, I think it is on par with the quality. If you are looking for an actual piggy bank that has better quality it is most likely not going to be cute and fun like this one - probably a boring cash box - where's the fun in that? I'm an adult and even I had fun putting money in it while I was demonstrating to my little one. I highly recommend this fun little money vault.

This is such a nice piggy bank! It is big and I love how it looks. I am homeschooling my kids and this help me encourage them to do better. It also helps me educate them about savings, retirement and finance. I know it’s too early for that but I believe the sooner the better if they can learn and mindful now.
PROS
* BIG and made of quality material. I think for the price it is well worth it.
* Easy to set up! It is a little confusing in the first coz it didn’t say while you are holding the * you have to press the desired number as your passcode and the # key at the same time to change the passcode.
* I love that if my kids forget the passcode I can just remove the battery and it goes back to its factory passcode which is 0000
* my son enjoys the lights and how cool it opens as a safe. The turning part turns really good without issues.
* his favorite is when he can insert the bills. It is just like in the ATM and he finds it super cool. I suggets you try using a normal paper first to see if it works so you do t have to worry about ruining your dollar bills

CONS
* it doesn’t come with a battery nor a small screwdriver. Most toy for this price range comes with one or at least the screwdriver BUT this one doesn’t. You will need 3 AA battery to make this work.

Despite the CON I still think this deserves a 5 star coz of the quality and features.

This would be so cute and fun if I didn’t have to reset the code after every few days. I got my kids each one last Christmas & they LOVE them but I put their codes in very single and one we can remember & it constantly doesn’t work and I have to reset it, u. Screw the bottom take batteries out etc, anytime they want to open it, it works for a few days than Locks up again, if they don’t open it offer it locks up.

Honestly I got this for myself and I love it. It would be great for a kid. It's super cute and fun. I wish it was bigger and it would have been amazing if you could make withdrawals. Probably one of the best piggy banks I have ever seen.

When my husband and I were growing up in the late 70s we both had piggy banks. We were both savers. Today we have checking accounts, saving accounts, money market accounts and a financial planner. I miss the days of the piggy bank. We wanted to instill the values of a piggy bank on our nephew and decided to keep a piggy bank of his very own at our house where he can keep anything he wants - treasures.

This is a modern day piggy bank and it requires batteries (not included) and it even has a programmable pin. It has a slot for bills and coins and it makes noise. It is the bank I wish I had as a child.

There is a 'vault wheel' that opens the door even. There is one drawback and unless you open the door carefully, everything will fall out once you open the door.

The pin is easy to reset by simply taking the batteries out. The new pin is 0000.
Gave this to my son for his birthday. He loves it. The fact it has a slot that sucks in the bills makes it super fun. It’s kind of loud but it works really well

This is a cute bank that my grandson is enjoying. That said, however, it has some quirks. First, it doesn't seem very sturdy. It's semi-heavy plastic but I feel one good fall on the tile floor would end its life. There is a fairly large slot in the top into which you can drop any size coin or even folder bills into. The coins just chunk right in. The bills can also be fed into a front slot like a typical vending machine. The machine nicely rolls them into the bank. The default code of 0000 works just fine and then there are some fun noises and a green light that signals your ability to spin the dial and open the door. All of this is very fun. Inside the door there is a switch tahat says "voice" to one side and "beeps sound" to the other side. It comes set to the "beeps sound". I moved it to "voice", closed the door and tried the default code. With every push of the four "0s", an annoying voice says "enter passcode" which was, of course, what I was doing. Once all four "0s" had been entered, the same fin sounds occurred. When the door was again open, I turned the voice off. Overall, this is a fun bank for my grandson but the price is a little high for something that doesn't seem that well-made or to have many features (for example, no volume control).

This is surprisingly well made and my niece absolutely LOVES it! She keeps all her jewelry in it.
Highly recommend!

A beautiful present for my son, for Christmas but very disappointed as not working as it should. The slot money didn’t inhale automatically the money and even manually you couldn’t insert it. When you put in the code, the green light flashes for about 3 seconds which means you have to dash to try to get the door open or it locks again. Even then it won't open half the time. When you change the code, it works for one go and then reverts back to the original code.

Its a fun novelty bank for a young child. If you are looking for something that will be kept and cherished, look somewhere else. This is only a novelty toy-like bank that a young child will get some entertainment out of and be encouraged to save money. And for that purpose it is a good choice.
It would make a nice gift box for a child containing another gift inside of it.
Gave this as a Birthday Gift for my 6 year old Granddaughter. She was so excited

This is a wonderful bank for kids of all ages.  I have a similar one that I got when my ceramic piggy broke, and it not only comes with an ATM card but also counts (and keeps track) of the coins that you put in.  Let me tell you, putting in that card gets old after the first time, and it's a pain having to put in coins very slowly so that the machine will register the count.  I prefer this one because it's just one simple password and that's it.  You'll have to work a little bit at deciphering the instructions written in pidgin English but once it's set up, you won't need them anymore.  Plus, you can always look here at this webpage, since the instructions are clearer (but it doesn't explain here how to get out of "beep" or "voice" mode, or to at least turn it down).

This piggy bank is a bit different, it is fashioned after an ATM.  Except for the ability to open this bank using a hand scan! hahah  Our younger grandkids enjoy using it and we are trying to teach them the concept of saving money to purchase toys they would like.  We pay them for certain simple chores so they always have something to put in.  So far it's working very well and they like the keypad and hand scan feature.  A bit perturbed about putting money away but they are only 3 and 4 yrs old.
I gift this for my niece and she loves it. Easy to use and helps her to save money. Very happy with it and we like it. Thanks

My niece seems to like this SHOMOTE Kids Stuff Piggy Bank and has been using it and playing with it. Hopefully, it will help her to learn to save money! Otherwise she has been having fun with it as a toy too. I hope it will hold up for a few years. So, it can be fun and educational.
Good

This made a great gift for my nephew who’s 5. It’s a unique and different type of “piggy bank” that looks more like a vault or safe. The bank requires 3 AA batteries and uses a pin code to open. It’s fairly easy to operate with the default code being all zeros. My nephew liked the bank a lot because the gold and red colors reminded him of Iron Man. Made a great gift !

This is super cute and fun.  My son has been playing with it A LOT!!!  Which would be fine if wasn't so dang LOUD!!  I don't know if I just haven't found it, but there is no volume control.  Aside from that it's super easy, the preset code worked fine and changing it was very easy.

This bank is super cute for kids! It's not super sturdy (I mean, it's plastic), so I wouldn't recommend treating it like a safe, but it's cool for little kids. I like that it has a slot for bills because most piggy banks are designed only for coins. It's also cool because you can keep little trinkets and keepsakes in it. In the case of my kids, it's rocks, but they're special rocks to them!
Very sturdy, easy to use, and makes her happy to have her own little keep sakes box! It is a little smaller than expected, but works perfectly months after daily play!

Personally, I think it's way too simple for the price. BUT if it makes my kids happy and entertained it makes it worth it!! My 4 & 6 y/o love inserting $ bills into it!! It talks back to them and makes beeping sounds (which they find hilarious).

I think it should have a separate compartment for coins as when you insert them through the top slot, they just fall into the same area as the bills or other items you might've place inside the box & it can get messy, especially if you open the door after placing many coins.

This is a cute money safe and great for kids and to give as a gift. The front slot rolls in paper money whereas the smaller slot on the top os to drop coins. You can even put in a 4 digit passcode to keep it locked and secure. When you want to open the safe you put in the passcode, turn the wheel clockwise and pull the door open. It requires 3 AA batteries and makes sound effects whenever you put in the paper money, a creaking sound when you open the safe door and an "uh-oh" whenever you get the code wrong.

It kept my toddler entertained and she likes to open the safe and re-enter the coins and bills. Overall it's a better alternative to the typical piggy bank and a fun product to teach children how to save and store money.
Birthday gift and kids loved!

I got this for my daughter (who is a toddler) but loves pushing buttons (and it’s never to late to start saving up!). Although it can take dollar bills, this is perfect for us to stash all of our loose change in. You can key in your code to open to bank. Only takes a few AA batteries. Fun and cute way for your kids to save up some money and keep track of their birthday, holiday money.

so this is a cheap little bank but works for what it is needed for

and for my sons first electric "safe"/ piggy bank.. it is working okay.. can be pulled open without a password though and somehow the password keeps resetting to 0000 even after we have changed it per the instructions

Each of my son has one of these. They're pretty cute. The buttons do work and beep when pressed. When the vault unlocks, a little light lights up green and dings. When the passcode is entered incorrectly, the light glows red. The little wheel is cute and turns about 90 degrees to open. The dollar taker even works and when you gently put a dollar in (or any paper) it'll suck it into the safe. Also, it does hold a good amount of money.

These are really cute and a fun way to teach your child to save some money. I would pay about $20 for it. I don't think it's worth more than that but to be honest I don't like to pay much for toys since kids outgrow them anyways.

This is my second time ordering the kids piggy bank. I ordered this for my little sister. The piggy bank looks like a mini vault. It's super cute to have a mini vault in your house. It works like a real ATM. There is a slot on the top to deposit your money. It rolls in your cash and stores it in the ATM. The bottom part has the key pad for your passcode. The keypad lights up and beeps when pressed. There are instructions to set your 4 digit pin code. Default pin code is at '0000.' Once the code is set you press the number and end it with the # key. It will make a sound indicating the vault is now unlocked. Then you turn the vault knob to open the vault door so you can withdrawl money. It's such a clever way to store cash. My sister have so much fun using the vault and asking me for more cash to deposit into her account.

We have two children under the age of 10 and usually have some coins or change to encourage them to save. Since they have this piggy bank, they are more interested in saving money and hopefully they can learn to manage money better.

While my daughter really enjoys this bank, with the coin drop and 'bill feeding' mechanism, reprogramming the password is very hit or miss. There is a simple process for changing the password, but once it was changed it would not consistently accept the new password. Sometimes when it did accept the password, I would have to turn it upside down and hit the bottom to hear some sort of mechanism 'drop' allowing the door to open. We found it was a lot easier to just use the default password, although I don't really see how that would change the issue.

Also, if you forget the password, simply remove the batteries and reinstall them - the password changes back to its default settings. So you'll need to remember that default password even if you do reprogram it. The whole thing feels cheap, but it is a cute idea.

This bank is a nice large size, but the best thing is the automatic bill feed. My grandkids love it and it makes saving fun. I bought another one in red and black color for my grandson. They want to do chores to get bills to put in it! It is a great tool for teaching children the importance of saving for the things they want.

My son is of the age where he likes to play and keep his "most valuable" toys protected.  I got this item so he could have his very own little bank vault to do so.  He enjoys using it and pretending he is the richest man alive.  His little imagination comes to life when playing with this.  We don't really use it as a full on piggy bank as he already has one of those.  For us this is more for play fun which it does an incredible job with.  :)

I got this for my 6 and 4 yo and they love it! They love that they can put money in it and it’ll take the money and that they can use a secret passcode to access the money they put in. They’ll do this for a while too lol Honestly this is a great bank for entertainment and their security that it’s safe. It makes noises but there is an option to quiet it!
It is a great Piggy Bank. It is very sturdy and durable.
The only thing I’m having trouble with is not remembering how to change the password but thats my fault for not keeping the manual! Great product!
[[VIDEOID:a7dc14be4e822afbd7dbb59415169b5d]] 😡😡😡😡😡I bought two piggy banks, the blue one  broke, the pink one can't opened I need my money back or another one I can use for my kids
Beautiful and works great
This  be is a great gift for kids.

B092Z1TB99.text: This set contains a lot of art supplies! The quality of the items is decent. They're not professional grade by any means, but they're good and definitely acceptable. There's a nice variety of supplies. It comes with an activity book, but I think it would be nice to have an art pad of paper, too. Everything stores in a wooden storage unit. The whole thing is surprisingly heavy! It comes in a nice gift bag, ready to go!

B092ZYNY42.text: It was missing a couple pieces

2 boys live in this house that loves legos. 11yo and 13yo. The 13yo is more in love with Star Wats and The Mandalorian and Boba Fett, but everyone in our house loves Grogu (and IG-11 for mom).  So….before the opening began, I had them write the top 3 items they wanted for better sharing.  Fighting ensued. Some skin was lost. But in the end, most were happy.  Until my oldest decided to be cunning. Who knew that Grogu’s carrier was separate?!?  Ugh!!!  In the end, peace reigned it’s lovely head in our house once more (for about 2 minutes, or when one is sleeping)

My Grandsons loved their Lego Advent calendar last much and have been asking if they will get the same this year. Not sure who will be more excited - them or their Dad! LOL!!!

Great price & fast shipping!

My youngest is a Lego nut. This calendar is perfect. He gets a daily surprise and something fun to make every day. The items are like little maker kits with simple instructions and the box is designed to provide a diorama setting for your finished products. I love that he proudly shows me what’s happening every day with his characters as he completes each of the daily kits. Definitely worth it if you have a little builder and want something other than candy as a daily treat.

This is supposed to be a new advent calendar in a box. The box being intact is part of the product being usable. Half the windows are already perforated! It looks like an elephant sat on it. So disappointed.
This is such a great advent calander.  He loves opening them daily and putting them together.
I ended up buying two...one as a gift for my son...and one for when he gets older. I wish my parents did the same with all of my 1976-77 sets?
Love the new Lego Starwars Advent calendar! Must have for all Starwars enthusiastics.
The pieces came out of their bags! It’s just a jumble of random Lego bricks. My daughter is very disappointed and I am angry. Dear Lego, DO BETTER! Do not waste your money on this.

I've purchased these for a few years and recently noticed a downward trend in what you are receiving. Intially they included truly unique and special figures and builds but this year feels very lazy and recycled. There has never been an abundance of figures but Lego would make up for that with really unique or desirable mini figures. I suppose the Grogu is supposed to be wonderful but it's just a cheap repaint of the one already out there and honestly it's just lazy. The instructions for the mini builds also continue to be problematic and I wish they had included them somehow in the Lego app to access a better of idea how to assemble them. Also it's truly disappointing that one of the first couple of days don't include a mini figure! I recall previous ones having a mini figure on either the 1st or 2nd day but not this one and was an extreme disappointment to my child and frankly I was surprised as well. Mini build Razors Crest doesn't hit the same as having a mini figure to start the set off with a bang! I'm hoping for a better effort next year but it's honestly seemed that Lego has invested less and less time on this in the past few years. This might be good for the collector/completeist but it's a let down for a child.
great gift for kids.

This is so much fun for anyone who likes legos and Star Wars. Some of the pieces are tiny and some of the builds require a bit of skill. Definitely for bigger kids because of that but it’s a great value and fun for the family. Recommend it!
We can not wait to get one every year!
Very good
My husband and son both enjoy making and playing with this
So much fun to do everyday.
We like to get these advent calendars for our grandson …. They have really cool pieces that they enjoy with the rest of their legos!!!
Shame he couldn’t work out that the instructions were on each door!

We bought our first one last year and really enjoyed it.  They put a lot of thought into these sets and each little figure.  We're all adults and still love putting them together each day.  This has become an annual tradition.
Person loved them. No face on last character was disappointed in that.
My husband and I had a blast assembling these with our two kids! Will definitely buy next year and make it a tradition.
My 25 year old son love getting this.  He had a lot of fun putting them together. The hardest part was his wife only letting him do one day at a time.

It seems like every other year the Star Wars Advent calendar is very disappointing. There are a couple of neat builds in the set, but way too many of them are either variations or repeats from last year. There are also a ridiculous amount of non-vehicle or non-character builds in this set, does anyone like those at all? If you are buying this that you are probably only buying it for the unique Grogu; but to me, that doesn't justify the price tag.
Great gift and lots of excitement
It’s hilarious that most of these reviews were written in October/November considering the box shouldn’t even be opened until Dec 1-24. Very strange.  As of Day 1, so far so good.
Needed it

24 days of joy with this calendar! It was the daily highlight of our son's advent season and had some very cool miniature ships and characters to get him excited each day. Way better than the stale chocolate calendars I had as a kid.
My 25-year old and 28-year-old are having sooooo much fun with this Star Wars toy advent calendar!  I'm so glad I bought it!

Little background: this is our 10th year in a row with the Lego Star Wars Advent Calendar, one each year since our oldest was born. As last year wrapped up we feared the worst as we would have to add in the youngest of four to the mix this year, reducing all of the kids turns to 6 a piece.

Welp, after last year's review (https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R13E0LP7WBL25G?ref=pf_ov_at_pdctrvw_srp) the moment of truth came upon us. We spent months trying to figure out what to do, fearing the fight that may ensue after the kids picked sides. In April I discovered #2 was hoarding nerf bullets while #1 was stocking canned food. #3 had very curious maps of the neighborhood including tunnels I have yet to actually find. #'s 2 and 3 clearly had an alliance as we had predicted but #1 was keeping #4 at arms reach.

After meeting with local leaders and sitting down with HRT we reached the Feces Armistice of 2021 whereby it was agreed that since #4 was not yet potty trained only #'s 1-3 would participate in the Advent Calendar. In exchange for maintaining their eight turns each of #'s 1-3 would have to share two desserts over the 24 days. Each was a assigned a share day randomly to avoid further conflict. The kids made it clear that the armistice expired December 26.

I'm not sure what will happen in 2022. The conditions leading to the Feces Armistice have become null. Each is getting older, stronger, and smarter. I stupidly taught and encouraged them to play Risk so they have begun to learn more complex strategy than "nuh-uh" or "yuh-huh". I fear for my neighborhood and the collateral damage that could ensue, but we'll try our best to work it out.

However, last year’s advent calendar had fun ships and robots and characters that connected to the story/movies that folks recognized clearly (Millennium Falcom, etc.). This year was just random odd grouping of blocks to kind of look like something you might have seen in the background of the Mandalorian but beyond the final figure there was nothing iconic here and it lacked the fun of the previous sets. We got so bored we just opened them all up and dumped the pieces into a Lego container to use creatively in the future. So as I said, not like we got no value from it, but for the small array of tiny pieces you get, and no connection to the actual films/shows/stories definitely not worth the $30 asking price.

B093FFB1SK.text: This is a fun set. Perfect for at home or at a park, beach… makes a nice gift as well.

Ok, now this is a FUN toy! My family and I have been playing with this for a couple of weeks now and it has turned into a near-obsession.

This is a cross between badminton and ping pong. Players bat a koosh ball back and forth with two rubberized paddles that flex enough to give the ball some momentum and they make a satisfying sound when the ball is hit.

It's [relatively] safe to play in the house and it can be played in enclosed spaces as well as wide-open places too.

My kids enjoy a little badminton with mom and dad from time to time, but they love this Koosh version of badminton more! The only thing is, it is very difficult to keep track of the Koosh in your home. As I write this review, I don't know where it is, that's why it's not in the pictures. LOL! 5-Stars!

I am old enough to remember when Koosh Balls were all the rage in the 1990's. Such a simple concept but so much fun. A Koosh is a soft ball that is made up of rubber strands and usually made up of loud colours.

This kit comes with a ball and two paddles. For what you get, the pricepoint is pretty high and the value perhaps a bit low. However, I will say that for something so simple, its a heck of a lot of fun! The racquets are made of plastic and have what feels like balloon rubber stretched between forming a spring-like launching pad.

I can see this tearing if you treat it too roughly ... kids may have fun poking at it or hitting objects that are made of plastic and metal, which may rip the rubber. However, if used properly, you'd be surprised how well the Koosh ball can be launched off the racquet ... and how easily the ball is hit/returned.

This is safer for younger kids than playing with a tennis ball ... you would be hard pressed to be injured by a Koosh ball even when hit at full speed. This would be fun in the yard, at the beach, or even indoors, as the ball is soft and lightweight. The value is a bit off for what you get but this does feel like a quality toy. I would not leave these in the sun or salt water as that could affect the elasticity of the launching surface.

You'll have more fun and play with this longer than you thought you would.

I bought this for a family swap.. with the hopes I would get it. After pulling the best number in the swap I knew this was going home with me!

Things to know:
Pay attention to the instructions.. like which direction things should face, making sure pieces are seated completely before moving on.

THIS IS NOT A 30 MINUTE BUILD.. this is like a 3 hour, take your time, do it right build. Trust me, I ran into what I thought was a problem, so I walked away for a few hours and came back to it... Was able to figure out what I did wrong and correct it easily without getting frustrated.

LIGHTLY sand all the pieces when you take them out of the boards, just around where they were attached. It will help make them fit and look better.

Use both hands while popping pieces from the boards, don't rush it. The woods is strong, but don't be a bull in a china shop.

WAX when it says to wax. I actually used some butcher block wood conditioner/wax on the moving gears as the wax provided broke into little pieces with my aggressive waxing. *Note you can also use candle wax if you run out

I did end up using the tape strips on the globe part to secure them fully. *Tip* make sure to press down on the tape piece BEFORE trying to pull it off the page(before even placing it) .. that will ensure the tape part comes up with the strip. (This happens with many kinds of strip tapes) I cut the pieces smaller, just enough to cover the bottom inch of each tab and the top 1/2 inch to secure all in place. Tape goes on the wood part of one bone, then on the globe plastic of the piece that is already down.

I love this and will be buying more! So much better than watching TV, or playing on a phone, or doing dishes!!!

Love these wooden puzzles, bought a few different ones for Christmas gifts this year and got one for myself. This puzzle globe is a very good quality. It was easy to assemble. My husband loves it. It was a present for him.

This is my third ROKR puzzle and they are by far the highest quality brand. The instructions are very clear, even for the complicated parts, and they include links to video instructions as well. The kits have a lot of features, and every part and tool you need to build them. This globe has a lot of impressive bits like the gears to rotate it, and the moving magnifier, and of course the LEDs. All of it looks really good when it's assembled.

One word of caution on the LEDs: connect all of the parts before you assemble the globe so you can be sure which way the tiny connectors fit. It's possible to plug them in upside down, and once the globe is assembled, you can't get back in to correct them. If you plan ahead, it's no problem.

There is a large heavy battery pack on the bottom of scrat. Probably mostly to keep him in an upright position. I wish they could have put it more central. Will limit kids walking around with it more.

NOT a dog toy. However our dog loves to play with both. Doesn't destroy toys. The tail is fluffy and she loves to grab it. The noises make her brain work. The nut has to get really close to work but touching and pulling away causes desired reaction.

We're happy with this. Battery lasts longer than we thought it would, but we're a little worried about the actual longevity of the figure due to the animations. But it works well, and the kids like it and we're happy with it overall.

For a kid who loves this squirrel from ice age this is a perfect gift. It’s really big and well made.

B096LYV74X.text: I didn’t read carefully and thought these were for regular sized American Girl and Our Generation dolls. They are for smaller 14 inch dolls not 18in. However they do look really cute and my granddaughters really liked them.

So sparkly and fun! Came packaged so nicely and is so easy to put on your doll. Velcro on back of dress allows easy on and off. The style of this outfit matches my daughter’s style and she absolutely adores it!

Cons: The material is a little thin to me. The glitter on the shoes does rub off. There are A LOT of strings to cut to get these items out of the package.

B0978PKKWD.text: Wow.  This is a great set.  I purchased for my 7 and 10 year old grandsons - but my daughter (their mom) put it together so they could see the final result first.  Typically they put kits together and then dissasemble the pieces one by one to make other things - but they play with the completed kit first.  It's a big set with lots of unique pieces - basically a beachy/ocean theme.  I think they are going to love it.

This set is amazing! It's over 1,200 pieces and includes several different sets of instruction books. My boys are10 and 11. Usually they can put these sets together without any help from me as long as they are in the right mindset. This one required a bit more mental fortitude and time from them. Like, 5 hours. Once done though, it's pretty rad. So, as long as you have the space, this Lego set is a much, much better a way for them to spend their time than looking at a tablet.

[[VIDEOID:dcafed0c1764b40e8a192a2cd8171670]] I loved putting this LEGO set together, it was hours of fun. I think the best think about this set is that there are two full rides to build and each of them work, as in you can put the characters into the seats and then have them use the rides. There are also a couple of smaller buildings that you can build when you have less time.
This set is clearly more geared towards girls, which I liked, and the figures are different than the standard LEGO figures you might be used to.
I would recommend this set for older kids 7-10 because there are an extreme amount of very small pieces, if your child is younger than this I would recommend a lot of supervision.
I highly recommend this set and I hope to do more of them in the future.

Got this for my 11yr old Nephew; not enough kids signed up for Lego club and it was cancelled. So we decided to have our own!

This has been great. We're still working on it - typically takes 1 after school session per piece. We are going to debut the finished set to his parents at Christmas and he's very excited :)

If you're looking for a satisfying, fun project for older kids, I highly recommend this set!

This is a nice build, but a bit overpriced for only two rides.  As with most friends sets, there are a bit too many stickers rather than printed LEGO pieces.  There are many tiny pieces, so have a ziplock bag handy and build when LEGO stealing cats are sleeping.

Received this yesterday evening and my 7 year old daughter put together the first two bags with minimal help from me. (Goal was to do the project together.) so far I’m blown away by the design and we are a small fraction of the way done with the build.
If anything changes in my rating I’ll update but this is looking to he well worth the money. After the haunted castle this is quickly becoming my favorite LEGO set!
Update: we have completed bag 6. Set keeps getting more amazing. Quality time with my daughter building this set is priceless. We are both enjoying the set, and each others company very much :)

This set is absolutely adorable. Took my ten year old less than an hour to put it together. She luvs her Lego friends. We own most of them, this was one she didn’t have and it was on sale here at amazon for an okay price. Did not arrive on time, shipping was delayed with amazon which was the only disappointing part and why I didn’t give it a full 5 stars which is deserves.

This is a pretty amazing build. First off, you get 7 mini figures (to include 3 girls, one mermaid, one boy pirate, and two skeletons). Then you get a huge (and fully functional) haunted house (pirate themed) roller coaster ride, a tall spinning ride (which actually spins), a small carnival game with a spinner, a ticket taking booth/turnstile, and and an ice cream shop.

The last three items (the carnival game, the booth, and the shop) are pretty standard fare with nothing unusual -with the exception of a large, cool, spinning wheel for the carnival game, and a turnstile by the ticket booth. And, what a nice touch that all the pictures on the spinning wheel are actual prizes for the children to give out -and which are included as extra props for the game!

The highlights of the set, of course, are the two tremendously detailed rides. I initially thought that the rides were more for show -a look but don’t touch variety, but I was incorrect. They are fully playable, and supremely detailed (with lots of little decorative touches all around). This is almost like a doll set, it is so complete. You can take your friends to the park, ride the rides, play the carnival game, and get food.

It is a somewhat complicated build, and uses more than a normal amount of “technic” pieces for a non technic build, so it may take a little help with a younger child, but the finished product really is something to behold. The railway is fully functional, and though it doesn’t really glide super smoothly, you can very easily move it along with your hand. And, on the spinning sky ride you can actually spin the top of the ride causing the vehicles to flare out from the side, spinning out just like they do on a real ride.

If your little ones love amusement parks, and would like to play in one, then this might be a nice set for them. Recommended.

My girls have been huge Lego Friends fans but most of their sets have been houses, stores, and animals. This is fun for them but they’ve really enjoyed some of their brothers racing and more interactive sets. They were super excited to see that Lego Friends now has racing sets AND this amusement park.

I will say, this is a big set, it was basically a weekend project for 2 girls (9 and 11) but working together they figured it out on their own. With younger kids there will definitely be a good bit of help needed. My 11 year old is pretty good at problem solving and determined, otherwise I’m not even sure they would have been able to do this 100% in their own.

They were so excited with it they’ve done nothing but play with it. Even their brothers thought the set was cool and came to play.

It includes a roller coaster and a swing ride but it also includes working games (that even light up). This is the best set I’ve seen for girls.

My daughter and I spent hours putting this set together, only to find out the cart that is supposed to go around the track does not go. The previous LEGO amuse the park coaster had wheels ( which this set does not) in this set the cart is supposed to slide around the track like a monorail type ride. And it doesn’t work! . The hanging swing ride is well constructed and works great but my daughter was really looking forward to having a pirate theme coaster. Not worth the money at all!!
Ok
It's a pricey gift but my grandkids put it together and enjoyed it so much!! A great family gift !!

Got this for a 6 year old's birthday gift and she absolutely loved it! The piece that goes in for the light actually lights up. Kiddo spent hours quietly putting this together so it is as much as gift for parents as it is for kids.
This Lego set has lots of parts and characters to play with.  My grand daughter loves it.
Very expensive .....great gift challenging

Got this for my 8 yo niece. She built it without much trouble and has had fun playing with it. I guess we'll see how long it keeps her interest, but for now it looks like a great lego set. Lots of detail and interesting stuff to build.
Fun. As always
This is a very beautiful  Lego for girls. My daughter loves it very much

like all lego its great quality, but all the friends set are way easier to build and require significantly less building skills than the "boy" lego. Lego underestimates a girls' ability or desire to have a fun built verses just a fun to look at play set.

It was satisfyingly challenging for my 8 year-old. By that I mean that she wasn't bored at all, but it only took her a couple of hours to put it together. I wish they had more challenging sets for girls. My daughter isn't interested in Star Wars or some of the themes of the more challenging sets.
Nice set top keep kids company for a good hour
Coolest Lego set ever! My daughter loves it!!!

First of all, this is a great theme park. Lego has rolled out some fun coaster sets recently. This set pairs well with the Creator 3in1 Pirate Roller Coaster (31084). It also goes very well in any bigger theme park and/or boardwalk set you may have. It is, however, more than enough on its own. It has the roller coaster through the pirate ship, a snack stand with ice cream and waffles, the ticket booth, the carousel ride and the spin-the-wheel-to-win-prizes stand.

It has a lot.

The Lego designers continue to impress me with their creativity. Using the carrots stacked together is a wonderful coral technique. The jellyfish is maybe my favorite build in the entire set.

For food pieces you get popcorn, 2 cookies, 2 cupcakes, ice cream, a popsicle, two waffles (which are adorable) and a pizza box. You also get red light brick, a teddy bear, a green camera, a purse, a cell phone, two skeletons, two swords, a pirate hat, two yellow crabs, a dolphin, a ticket, two dollars, a 5 cent tile, a cauldron, a bone, a bluebird, a ton of heart tiles and a bag full of coral-colored underwater creatures (seahorses, shells, fish and octopus), and more. So much.

We really like the snack stand build. It looks like a giant cupcake. Love it.

You get 5 minidolls included in the set and one of them has the mermaid tail. This is a slightly different mermaid tail from the different Ariel minidolls we have, which is nice.

The set takes up a fair amount of space but it has a lot of playability.

I currently have the pirate ship repurposed for Halloween. I replaced the yellow and purple with black and brown, I took out the roller coaster and added a few more skeletons. It is a fun decoration.

B097XMKD6P.text: This is beautiful but comes with a million different pieces....definitely for the skilled builder who has a ton of patience

I got this item to make with my children and we've had a fun time with it so far. This is the first time we've built something like this so there is a lot to learn. All of the pieces are very small and it's easiest to assemble them with a tweezers. The pieces don't snap together, so we've been using small pieces of tape to hold the pieces together while the glue dries.

The kit helps develop an awareness for how furniture goes together. There is fabric to make bedding and even cushion stuffing to go inside chairs and give them form. The instructions are easy to follow and the pieces come in bags that are well-organized. I would compare this kit to putting together a 1000 piece jigsaw puzzle. It takes a lot of time and effort, but once you get into the flow it's relaxing. Please note that this isn't a kit that your kids can assemble and play with. It's more of a display model. The assembled pieces are very delicate.

This is the kind of kit that could help ignite an interest in architecture. It's fun, but it requires patience and precision work.

Easy to put together and fun for hours.  I love to decorate.  I also added my own special touches.  Sooooo many pieces.  I am already starting another.  The only issue I have are some of the pieces were warped but I was able to fix with glue to hold it together.  I was able to reference back to the pic for extra details the directions didnt cover.

Kit arrived quickly and as advertised.  We quickly gave up on using the white glue provided and used a hot glue gun for much of the construction.  Keep in mind that this is NOT a "some assembly required" child's dollhouse.  This is a time-intensive crafting project.  It will take you many, many hours/days and much patience to complete it.
My daughter has built many of these and loves doing it.

You will need to reference back to the picture to see how to proceed. She used super glue on certain pieces that have to stand up. The white glue just won't cut it. The result is stunning. She likes it a lot.

B09BQ429PZ.text: When I saw that there were light kits for some of the Lego kits,  I thought that was a neat idea. Most of the kits, however, were not for Lego sets that my family had. Then I saw the Boba Fett one that my 23 year old son had recently assembled, so I had to order it. It comes with an instruction booklet that shows you step by step with pictures. I assisted my husband with the task. You do have to take parts of the Lego masterpiece apart to do the job. The wires are very thin and once the job is finished, they're not very noticeable. They could have been completely hidden if we had run the first wire along the opposite side of the brick. Lesson learned. By the time we were finished, we were glad to be done and didn't want to go back and change it. The whole thing probably took less than 30 minutes. We were a little slow at times, trying to decipher the instructions to make sure that we were removing the correct piece and such. The actual lights have adhesive strips on them to keep them in place. You do have to plug the wire ends into a piece so everything is linked together. It requires 3 AAA batteries, not included. The end results are great! Our son was very pleased with how it looks.

B09HN8QMXK.text: This is a nice set of reference cards dor D&D. My 23 year old son is the D&D player in our family, though many years ago, my husband was one. My son likes them and finds them helpful during game play. I would have to agree with the other reviewer about the small print, but my son is young and doesn't seem to mind. Illustrations are good.

OK Just to start, that box is awful. It takes up SO much space! When you put the cards in it, it has so much empty space, that makes it take up room on my shelves, but then when you open it, it just has flaps that fall down everywhere for no reason, taking up a huge chunk of the table.

It's not 150 different cards, there are repeats of common items, which makes sense. The art is nice, but not great. Font is a little small. And lastly, they are just regular D and D items, nothing special, just items from the basic book. Not really complaints, more just pointing things out.

I would have said these were ok, but the official brand has a set here on Amazon that has way more cards, for way less money and they have much better art and better cardstock. So it's just a worse value.

Inventory management is a pain for anybody but kids in particular find it much easier to have a card representing each item in their pack. That's fundamentally what this vault does only with better art and in a nicer box. But unfortunately it has some major flaws that detract from the overall presentation.

First off is the design itself. There's a lot of unnecessary design elements that reduce the picture (not a big deal, we know what a sword looks like) and the text (HUGE deal, that's why we got these cards). The font is simply too small and there's no good reason for it. So that's one star off just because you can't read them.

The other thing, and I find this unforgivable, is that the cards have no encumbrance rating. There's no weight. There's nothing, except gold value. The whole point of keeping track of inventory like this is so you don't have to do the math of listing every item on your character sheet. These cards lack a simple, easy-to-include element. It blows my mind that weight is missing from these items. That's another star off.

Finally, there's the container itself. It's a vault, so it flops open. Fun right? And it sure is for someone giving this as a gift and someone else recording it on video. But then there's the actual use of it. Sliding it back in is challenging, and the box itself doesn't even have any art to make it look vault-like. That's another star off.

This vault is a nice gift for someone who hates keeping track of inventory, but it unfortunately won't solve that problem. I love this idea so much I made my own with my own limited resources and clip art. With more resources, this should be so much better than it is.

This is not a paid review. Yes, I bought the product.

1. Box Design
The very nice, rather large, sturdy box, is designed to store and allow you to easily flip through the cards during gameplay. The fall down sides aren't needed, and could be irritating when gaming real estate is limited, but it is a fun feature. Unlike some reviews, it's not hard to put the lid back on if you hold the sides in place. You can opt to have the box open without worrying about the sides by putting the main box inside the lid.

2. Card Quality
While these aren't the heaviest weight stock I've seen for cards, if you treat them well, or put them into card sleeves, they should last for many years to come. They have a matt finish and the print quality is vibrant.

3. Card Design
The set includes 7 category dividers: Weapons, Tools, Treasures, Proficiency, Armor, Potions, and Focus. I agree with other reviews - the text is much too small when in most cases it doesn't need to be but even with my bad eyesight, you can read them. Each card has a nice, watercolor like illustration along with the name, type, details, and worth.

Weapons Category Example:
WHIP - Martial Melee Weapon / 1d4 Slashing Dmg / Finese, Reach / 2gp

I highly recommend this wonderful set. While I feel there are improvements that could be made, I feel it's still worthy of the 5 stars I'm giving it. GM's will love the ease this tool chest of 150 cards gives.

I don't regret buying this set since I wanted visual representations of mundane items that my players could "buy" when they go into a shop (we use actual game coins). The art is good on all but about 6 cards that seem to have been drawn by a different artist. The cards are the same size as official D&D cards, so they will fit the same clear pockets. The deck covers a lot of mundane items that the official D&D decks don't include.

I may laminate the cards so I can write on them - most have little or no game mechanics info (such as the value of the treasure items). Laminating would allow me to write homebrew info on them, then wipe it away when I want to change it. It would be nice to have duplicates of things like rope and other items that multiple players will carry, but I will probably just make color copies of these cards.

The box, however, is idiotic. It's glossy, uses a lot of cardboard and full color print (despite lacking actual art), and clearly required gnomes to engineer it. For one, it's huge (and thus required a lot of glossy elaborate filler inserts so the cards would sit neatly.) In actuality, the cards tend to slip between the filler inserts and get stuck or sit awkwardly so you can't read the tab dividers. (But I do like having color-coded tab dividers for different categories of items.) Also, the box shape is an awkward size that won't accommodate additional card sets. The cube is about 1.75 card widths in all directions, including height.

The gimmick of the vault "opining" is really dumb - there are these flaps that flop down when you take off the lid, but they just glued a smaller box inside the flaps, so the flaps don't even open anything. I taped them so they wouldn't flop since it's annoying when trying to close the box. Also, they didn't bother to use any art to make it look like a vault. It's just a lot of wasted cardboard that adds to the price while reducing utility.

If they wanted to inflate the package size, why not make a box that could be used to store additional card sets? That would motivate me to buy more of their cards.

B09J21PCKB.text: My family enjoys playing games. We discovered cooperative ones a few years ago and those have become our favorite. We weren't sure what to expect with the 5 Minute Dungeon game, but we really had fun playing it. You can have up to 5 players. It was my husband and me, plus our two teenagers and one visiting teen. Each round takes up to 5 minutes and there are 5 rounds to the game. My 19 year old son was the one who read the directions and told us what to do. I had problems keeping it all straight, but everyone else seemed to understand. Once the game was underway, I quickly understood and was able to join in without any difficulties. Most of our rounds took about 4 minutes, though one round ended up with just fourteen seconds left when we were done. The game is really quick and slightly chaotic. It got a bit messy in between rounds because we were just throwing the cards down on the table when we played them, but it was pretty fast to sort them back in between rounds because they are color coded. After the first round, my 16 year old daughter was the first one to say how fun she thought it was. That was unexpected because she was the least excited about playing it in the first place. The family has already decided that this is a game we'll take with us on our next beach/cabin trip.
Easy to learn & super fun family game suitable for 8 and up (lots of action and it does not take forever to play)

This game is a BLAST! It’s a stand up, push your chair back, yell at each other kind of game. Even after my friends and I got the handle of playing and began winning every time is was STILL FUN. This game is worth the price. You should certainly get it if you’re looking for a fun game.
Awesomely fun party game, even for adults!!! I game with serious gamers and everyone and awhile we break out this to have some insane fun. Easy to learn for all ages and just around an awesome game.
Great game according to my dad

Best. Game. Ever.

Never the same twice. I bought this one to give as a gift after family played the one I own. Get the expansion set, too.
Very easy to learn and it’s a got nice quick rounds. Plus the characters/cards are super funny. Over all it’s a really great game to play with a few friends!
This was fun for the family game night. Age 8 to 60 enjoyed playing. Challenging for me, but very fun and fast paced.

This is a fun, fast paced game for the whole family. There are not a lot of games out there that are as much fun for me as they are for my 7 year old or vice versa, but this one is. Make sure to get the timer app for your phone to enhance the experience.

It's loved by my young daughter and her friends, as well as by my friends. The emphasis on fun rather than fighting makes it kind of a natural pair to 'No Thank You Evil' to break kids into the idea of fantasy gaming without the high pressure stakes of D&D or Pathfinder. It's also a good gateway for those friends who seem to think that only unwashed neckbeards can be interested in this kind of fun.

It's a bit misleading. Sure, a dungeon is 5 minutes, but a full game is 5 dungeons. So 25 minutes. And a few minutes to reset everything between dungeons. So maybe 35 minutes for a full game. But... it's a really fun 35 minutes. This is very much a real-time, cooperative game with everyone shouting their plans so the group can efficiently defeat enemies. Good fun.
Love this game! It takes teamwork and quick thinking and great for family game night or with friends!
Cute game. My family enjoys playing.
So much fun! Great (quick) family game. Definitely download the timer app for maximum fun!

This game is fantastic. My entire family (husband who never did anything like D&D, two tweens, and a seven year-old who thinks she's a Disney princess) LOVE playing this one. Takes just a few minutes to learn, and the replay value is amazing because you never play the same game twice.

HIGHLY recommend for anyone, kids or adults.

How quick this game is makes it perfect for groups that are hard to keep engaged in longer play games. The artwork is fun and the timer adds to the stress. It always seems when you hit that minuet and a half left the intensity hits. It’s can get really chaotic and if you play with people that don’t handle stress well this game can actually be amazing. It seriously takes maybe two minutes to learn the game and after the first play everyone pretty much understands the dynamics.

There is one problem. Two player seems broken. Yes you draw more cards and shuffle two decks together. But it doesn’t seem to work. I’m guessing it’s you are still down overall cards in play as well as you have less character effects available. Anytime we play just two it almost always ends in we re stuck without proper cards to play. If someone plays the theif to draw new cards it can work but typically they either run out their cards or you waste a lot of time with the redrawing so much the timer ends. Four players was the best so far.

I understand that this game is similar to a game that is played online as a video game.  As a "older" parent I don't know how it relates to the video game.  However, this is a fast paced game against time played as a team against the clock.  It is a bit tricky to play the first few times as there are many different cards and powers.  After a few rounds you begin to catch on.  You need to pay attention and be quick. Rounds are 5 min each and you advance to the next level by beating the "obstacles."  There are a total of five rounds so roughly 30 min to play.  You will need to sort and add cards each round.

My son is into any card game he can get his hands on.  Pokemon, Magic, etc so when we had the chance to get this for him, I jumped at it.  He and my daughter love it!  They play it for hours on end and take turns trying to cheat each other.  Haha.  Anyway, as an adult that doesn't play these games, they wipe the floor with me but we all laugh while they do it so I guess its okay.  The characters are fun and the game play is good too since games don't drag on.  I highly recommend this game to anyone, especially if you want something fun that limits screen time.
great for intro to people who've only played monopoly, when you don't feel like explaining a lot of directions, or when you have kids in the group. great fun with adults only too.

How does a Five Minute game last 3-4 hours, well because everyone wants to keep playing it, that's how!

So let's start with all the pluses and I'll mention a couple of minor negatives.

This game is easy to pick up, easy to play, and quite fast paced. There is some very minor set-up, everyone get's a clearly colored deck, picks a character with one ability they can use throughout the game and go.

Now my gaming group meets about once a month to play a ton of different games from Agricola, Pandemic, 7 Wonders and CodeNames. I love having a variety of games to play from but none of them are timed... because I find that gets in the way. We're a social group, we take our time, and sometimes it's been a month or longer since we've seen someone so being punished with a timer is just unappealing. But this is a fast paced and short game to play. So you can get everyone going AND focused for five minutes, discuss the results and play again either from the start or advancement.

Now I love the cards and the bases and the characters. The game is designed with humor and plays and puns on the genre. Despite how fast your throwing down cards, cards just wind up sticking out. Two Guys and One bow became a focus point for half the evening. Our 3 person team was always somewhat short one symbol so we began to recognize the cards that gave us trouble. Steve! The cards are colorful, and oddly memorable after a few rounds. I do not have a colorblind member in the group but the symbols on the cards are also clear, so I think if that is an added challenge it would be fine. For the most part, you're not reading the cards, so the 8+ is pretty spot on. If you have a kid that focuses and reads and picks up stuff faster, you might actually be able to go younger. I became a board gamer from an earlier age, and this I know I could do.

Variety, it's pretty easy to switch characters around. You don't have to study the decks or anything or the abilities. Because the games are so short, it's not a big deal at all to learn as you go, switch abilities, exchange decks... very versatile. Heck if you have another person walk in late, just throw them a deck when the next round is done, they'll be adding to the fun in literal minutes.

The App is awesome, we used Android. It's so great in fact I was disappointed I forgot to use it. So let me assure you, if for some reason you don't have a smartphone around, you can use another timer. The only challenge with that is pausing isn't always easy with the other timers. And let me tell you, the App has humor, music... really well done for something that some companies might call a throw away addition.

Okay, so I did mention some minor complaints and they're all based on the quality of components. After a single night of use, I have peeling on the angles of the box, basically surrounding the middle angle. I take pretty good care of my games and we're really only talking about taking it out and putt it back. I think the shape of the box is interesting too, but it's awkward and clearly created a stress point where the damage begins first.

The second is the cards. It's a hectic game, so the card get used and mixed a lot, after four hours, they're already showing wear that is rather noticeable.

Aside from some disappointment due to the quality of the components, I really enjoy this game. It will easily be a regular for game nights, especially since you can pull it out when there is some energy left in the group but maybe not enough time to do a full game of anything else. It really rounds out the collection
Was looking for something short and fun. A little easy with 5 players, but a lot of fun! Would love to see more levels!
I can see the appeal of the game but it lacked in-depth play and instead made rushing time the most important mechanic. I can see the appeal but I much prefer card games with thoughtful play.
great!
One of my favorite games! It’s easy for everyone to join in and I love the collaborative aspect.
The game is a blast. Great for teamwork and teaching kids strategy. I would totally recommend it. Both for adults and kids about 9 and up.

If you've rarely/never played D&D, this is a neat, fast, fun variant. Played with my wife and 2 of my kids and had a great time! First couple of attempts to clear the first level were a fail but as we got the hang of how to make good decisions at a FAST pace, we started to really enjoy it! Lots of laughs and fun!

The box depicts a family, and I'm sure its great in that scenario too.  But don't think that is the only time it shines, we've played a few times now with 100% adult groups and its been great fun every time. I only have 1 real complaint and one regret of sorts.  The complaint is that difficulty scaling at 4 players is a little off.  My regret is that its so fast paced, you can't enjoy the humor of the game during actual gameplay.  We've instead ended up reading over the cards after the battle is over.
Christmas gift and he was a  Happy camper.

There are three main pieces to this review, and I would encourage you to read them all. Start by knowing that I am a fairly avid board game player and a father. In this instance, I bought 5-Minute Dungeon ("5MD") in my "dad" capacity but have a pretty good idea of how it will play out with my game group.

Mechanics and families:
5MD is a real-time game that requires the players to complete the "door cards" (thematic monsters, people and obstacles that you draw each turn), until you have passed all the doors and can confront the boss. You complete these bosses and cards in three ways: by matching symbols from your hand of "character cards"; or, by using a "character card" that has a one-shot completion ability: or, by using your character's special abilities. You also have supporting cards and abilities like draw more or stop time. You do this in real-time by quickly laying your cards and moving them aside. For those who don't know, real-time board games operate continuously, on a real-world timer. It requires a balance of rapid inter-group communication and quick inter-personal thinking. That's a fancy way of saying there will be lots of shouting and quick thinking because you are on a timer! 5MD wound up being great, relatively complex tactics game for our 6 and 8 year old. I expected nothing out of this game in terms of educational value, but I am pleasantly surprised and happy to report that this should invariably help with rapid-fire critical thinking and communication.

For the most part, the mechanics of the game are clean and simple.

The one notable mechanical issue with 5MD that needs to be mentioned is setup and cleanup time. Yes, 5MD itself is exactly 5 minutes, because you have that long to complete the dungeon. However, sorting and cleaning up your cards takes another 5 minutes. Not the end of the world, but know that the kids might be squirming around a little during intermission.

Theme:
From a thematic point of view, this game is absolutely hilarious. The "door cards", character sheets and bosses all have amusing adventure tropes and names. The art is bright and colorful (I bought 5MD to wipe away the gloom of a cold Midwestern fall, and it didn't disappoint!). All of this will go largely unnoticed during your playthroughs due to the rapid-fire nature of the real-time game, UNLESS you read through the "door cards" ahead of time. Do yourself a favor and do just that. You will find yourself chuckling when you draw and recognize "Adorable Slime," or "Just Some More Stairs", or "Steve." [Yes, just "Steve." There has to be joke there that I'm missing.]

Importantly, the "character cards" that contain the symbols are starkly minimalistic. You know instantly what you have in hand at any time. A great move for the game.

But the real star of the show thematically is the free-to-download timer available for Android and iOS. Absolute, total hilarity. There are 6 narrators that leave you alone for the most part, but at the start, end, and every minute they will say something heroic, or dark, or snarky. My kids were in stitches when this cute, bubbly, imp-like voice started saying "You ready to start the dungeon? I can't WAIT to watch you fail miserably!" Such a great feature, and borderline a necessity.

Family Conclusion:
This will become a family staple during the cold winter months. Gets the brain juices flowing while laughing and enjoying colors besides white snow and gray nights...

Thoughts for game groups:
For game groups, this is a good 3-4 shot filler game. You'll enjoy it, on theme alone and probably based on mechanics. But, you're going to break the puzzle behind the game pretty quickly. Once you figure out the symbol makeup of each character's deck (as in, the Paladin has lots of shield symbols and the Warrior has lots of sword symbols), the "best" play becomes pretty obvious. And from there, you will either crack the dungeon or get frustrated because of bad draws. The character abilities provide a nice but limited way to mitigate bad draws, but they too are easily gamed; making a balanced party is a cakewalk.

Full stop: You should still get this game.

I mean, 5MD is $15 at time of review. You are going to jointly spend $60 on movies, so this is absolutely worth your time and money for a few rounds of narrated hilarity. If you go into 5MD expecting some simple strategy to fill an hour every once in a while, you'll enjoy it. Just don't expect this to be the next great dungeon-crawl-in-a-box.

This game is a great cooperative game that can be played very quickly. You do download an app with a timer for the game. The timer has different styles of voices for announcing the time left on the clock I.e. dramatic, suspenseful.
