I got this for to have something other than PC gaming friends who were coming in from out of town. You know have to find something to help with time and that can be over heard when kids are everywhere theirs and ours. It was great! We of course decided to not actually use the 5 minute timer because we didn't want to start over that much(Yes I know but it was still a difficult game). We played it for hours and had a great time learning the game. It is also great that there is expansion abilities for this game to extend/change up the bosses to keep things interesting. Loved the game!

Oh boy... This game had some real potential to be fun, but the game balance being out-of-whack and the vague rules really ruin a great thing.

Game consists of a party of adventurers, each with their own unique deck of actions, laying their cards down in real-time in order to defeat traps and monsters in order to take on the final boss; all in 5 minuets! The pitch sounds great, and certainly had me interested; unfortunately the execution is pretty terrible.

First problem is the rules. What cards can be played is really up in the air thanks to unclear rules; really inexcusable considering how critical this is to the game. Searching online reveals quite a few interpretations that change the way the game is played and won quite dramatically, with no feedback form the game's creator. Pretty frustrating.

Second major problem is balance. How many players there are and what classes are chosen can swing the game to unbeatable all too easy. Oddly enough, the German rule book had a system in place to help deal with this, but for some reason didn't make it into the English version. So if you do end up purchasing this game, do yourself a favor and track this down (and Google translate it) for a much better time.

Final problem is a personal one: how is there no solo rules for a game that practically screams for them!? By the way, if you are looking for a great, rules light dungeon crawl, check out One Deck Dungeon!

5-Minute Dungeon gets three stars because if one takes the time to iron out exactly how they want it to be played, downloads the German rules and incorporates the scaling aspect, and learns which classes work well together, you get a somewhat fun "filler" game to pass some time.
We love this game!!! So fast, so easy, and playable!

As a DM (Dungeon Master) myself in D&D (Dungeons and Dragons), this was a must buy for me. I was introduced into this tabletop game by an uncle of mines and I was totally hooked. It’s a great game for lifterally anyone, from kids to old folks. It’s a fast paced game, a teamwork game, and most importantl, it’s a dungeon tabletop game. Now it’s only a matter of one when the expansion comes out.

This game is so much fun. We played a couple untimed rounds to get the feel of it and get comfortable with the rules. I was worried about replayability at first...then we smacked headfirst into a steep difficulty curve.

I highly recommend just looking through all of the dungeon cards to read their names and enjoy their art. It's all bright and colourful and just a joy to look at. Easy and addictive, exactly what my household needed to have quick and simple entertainment. No long setups.

My family loves the fast-pace as well as the easy set up. Instructions may need a tad of polishing, but over all, excellent value.

Instructions: When dealing with cards, the cards used, all of them thrown on the pile are "consumed" and therefore out of play. This is different than discarding for abilities.

This is fun and I love the new packaging style, though the instructions are a bit confusing: not sure if it's 5 minutes to beat all the boss mats or if you reset each boss mat. Had to look up the youtube videos and it seems like the latter is true. It's a chaotic fun time, but it's best played with geeks and gamers, casual people may find it too chaotic.

[My standard disclaimer: I try to review games based on how good I think they are for their intended audience and less how much I personally like the game.]

5 Minute Dungeon is actually a bit more than 5 minutes, but that's okay because it's a really light hearted fun game for those who enjoy this type of game.

To understand this game in a nutshell there are three terms: Real time (you don't take turns, it's a free-for-all like the game of Pit), cooperative (you win or lose together as a team), and filler (it plays in under 45 minutes). A large percentage of serious gamers don't like games like this. Real time games are especially not well loved amongst those who prefer more serious war games or Euros. However, for non-gamers, families and anyone, including serious gamers, who want a silly good time this is a game to check out.

The goal of the game is to defeat a boss card (a single dungeon). Before you reach a boss card, however, you have to defeat a series of "door" cards. Each player has their own hero mat with a specific single special ability. The special ability varies from freezing time, to defeating specific door cards (obstacles, people, monsters), to giving extra cards to other players at the table. Each has their own hand of cards, 3 to 5 depending on how many players there are. As you play your cards you replenish back up to your max hand from your own personal deck that consists of cards with symbols or actions. You play the symbol cards to match the symbols on the door cards and when all the symbols are played the door card is removed. If time hasn't run out you and get through all the door cards you then take on the boss card in the same manner. If you defeat the boss card before time has run out you've won this round. The timer is reset and you start on the next dungeon/boss card. There are five boss cards in total so if you defeat all five you've won the game.

The energy of this game reminds most of Pit, the real time stock trading game that's loud and chaotic. If you like that game you might like this one. If you really loathe Pit then this one is probably not for you. If you don't like Pit because it involves back stabbing and the chaos is fine then this game might work because it's cooperative. If it's the chaos of Pit you don't like then stay away from 5 Minute Dungeon.

Based on what this game is I give it four stars. It's a very good real time cooperative filler game. I'm knocking off one star for a possible lack of replayability based on the 5 boss cards. Perhaps more will be available from the publisher, I don't know. However, for the audience of this type of game this might not matter. This isn't a game you're going to want to play several times in a week even if you really liked it.

I happen to like real time games as a concept. My issue is that I so rarely find people who want to play them. The problem for me is made worse in this game because of it being cooperative. Co-op games aren't that fun in my house. I can't explain why, but they just aren't. So for me this game isn't what I'm looking for only because of that one element. However, I know co-ops are great for others so I can't fault the game.

Overall I recommend this without hesitation to those who enjoy games like this.

We were originally concerned that people might get mad at each other for not playing certain cards, but we found that the gameplay is so fast, there is no time for that! Everyone just ends up laughing and having a great time. Good for families with kids.

I like that this game you are working together.  My 11 yr old and 14 yr old really enjoyed it.  They got really into moving fast and working together.  Good quality.  Takes a bit of reading to get the flow of play down (I think...if we have it right) and how each card can be different, etc. I think my kids got it much faster than I did!

This game is hysterical. Bought this as a little extra gift from Santa for my newly eight year old son and we played it for the first time tonight. We giggled a lot. Was very easy to figure out and we found ourselves screaming to get the adventure complete. The only hurdle was trying to finish while laughing. I highly recommend -- especially for the price.  One thing at first, we tried using our cell phone timers for the countdown but then we downloaded the app, just to see what it was like. Much more fun than using the straight countdown on the phone.
you will need to download the 5 minute dungeon app and once you have it downloaded. play away with your friends, it's so much fun and I hope they add new cards, classes and bosses in the future

Super fun game!  I especially like the fact that there is no waiting for one’s turn is this rapid pace game.  My kids (8 and 6 YO) both love it as well. I do recommend looking up play instructions on youtube to make the learning curve shorter.

Originally played the original Marvel 5 Minute dungeon, and I am surely a bit biased, but I definitely like this one better. Albeit, I am not a large marvel fan. The original version feels intentional and properly balanced. Will definitely be buying the expansion when it comes out.
Great game. My kids (6&13) love it as well. Easy to learn. Mastery takes some trial and error. Cooperative gameplay is wonderful.
Great game! Only thing that I'd like to change is a way to make it for more than 5 players. This is a favorite in our family.
Quick fun for groups to work together
I had fun
Fun for the whole family and only a 5 minute game! Love it!
It is a fun fast paced game. I like to bring this out whenever we are hanging out.

The weapons are really made out of metal and have immaculate detail. These would be a GREAT Christmas present for any League of Legends fan you know, or if you are a collector, get them for yourself! My husband is a long time LOL player so I got these as a "just because" gift for him. Being bad at gifts, I told him before they arrived and he kind of shrugged and thought whatever. B09LZ77874.text: I always get my girls a calico critter for Easter and this one will make the perfect gift.

Originally we got a couple of these Calico sets for my daughter but now my wife has started collecting them as well. This birthday set is very cute and there is a lot of attention to detail. My wife loves the birthday girl cat character in this set (she's a big cat lover) and was particularly impressed with the quality of the dress.

A nice thing about this series is that they use very small sets, so it doesn't take up a lot of space. In this set, for example, there are lots of small, detailed pieces like the cake, plate and tea sets, and birthday gifts. We usually have this set up as a decoration but sometimes our daughter plays with it. When she does, she can spend hours with this set, in particular. It also goes well with other Calico sets too.

My wife and daughter both love this and give it 5 stars!
Bought for a choreography gift for a holiday choreography my little and her dance mates did. They got first place, and this toy to take home afterwards!

My daughter has an ever-expanding empire of Calico Critters, and honestly I love them too. I love that when she and her brother play with them, it's always creative, imaginative play — making up stories, talking to each other, going on little adventures.

One thing that sets Calico Critters apart is how wholesome the play is, and I think that's in part because every box comes with a little story describing how the family relates to each other and to other people. It's nothing too elaborate, but it sparks some creativity and it sets the context for positive relationships between each of the critters.

Unfortunately, this little playlet does not come with a storybook, so I think it would work best if you already have the Tuxedo Cat family and perhaps already know who Lily is. My daughter did not have those, so she's missing some context of who Lily is and what kind of birthday she would want to have. It's not a big deal, really, but it's amazing how much those little story books add to a set!

The other watch out I want to mention is that this playset comes with a high number of tiny, tiny pieces. All the cake decorations are removable. That's great because it gives kids more to play with, but it also means you'll need to be extra careful not to lose those tiny pieces.

Overall, this set is definitely up to the high quality of durability and attention to detail that I expect from Calico Critters. Definitely a fun addition!

Ok, I have to pull a star for excluding Pluto, but it's obvious the puzzle's educational value is not in learning about the solar system as much as it is in learning to complete jigsaw puzzles. As such, the image has artistic and inspirational value, and not much educational value. I mean, besides missing Pluto, the planets are not drawn to relative scale, the orbit and scale of their moons are way off, the colors are excessively saturated and so on -- but this isn't about teaching the solar system. It's just a puzzle. As such, it's a very good one. The pieces are rigid, fit precisely for their size, appear to be durable, don't seem to easily warp, and those colors and object scales are off for a purpose -- to aide in one method of finding puzzle pieces that go together. My 4 year old independently noticed that the Moon and Earth were the largest and knew this wasn't correct. Because of that I was able to explain "perspective." Anyway, it's a good puzzle, well made, and the large size is fun. I just wish it had longer-lasting value. I think most children will pretty quickly outgrow 48 piece puzzles and this one will be of little remaining interest -- but of course it's impractical to start with 1000 piece puzzles, so we need beginning or intermediate puzzles like this for the short time that we're at this level.

Now, while I agree that the puzzle's instructional value is as a puzzle not as a solar system diagram, the correct response to Pluto reclassification is to INCLUDE Kuiper belt objects rather than delete/omit knowledge. Because the asteroid belt was included, and Pluto was previously included in basic solar system knowledge, it's reasonable to expect Pluto and Kuiper belt objects on this solar system puzzle. In essence, if we learned something more about Pluto, then TEACH it, don't omit it. Additional knowledge is not a good reason to fail to teach what was previously proven not to be too complicated to learn.

The 3Doodler pen is good. And my daughter loves it. It’s nice because it is rechargeable so wireless when using it. Also the plastic is safe to the touch and won’t burn kids.

These filaments are fine but I don’t like the false advertising in the descriptions. 3Doodler charges so much more for filaments than any of the other brands and doesn’t work any better.

This description says there are 8 packs of 24 strands. A total of 192 strands. It shows the strands are 6.7” long. Therefore, you are getting about 107ft of plastic for $30. Not 900ft like it says in the title. All other brands run about $10 for 320ft. So most filament cost about .03/ft and 3Doodler costs 30 cents/ft. That’s 10X more!!!

I have the Scib3d pen and the 3Doodler. I can tell you that there is no difference in the filament performance or quality. They both work equally as well.

If you plan on doing a lot of work with a 3D pen you might want to consider the ongoing cost factor. The initial cost difference on the pens is negligible.

I would like Amazon to make sure these descriptions are accurate as I was going to buy this thinking the cost/ft was comparable but it’s just even close.

If you've done more than a few puzzles, you start to get irritated by things like the packaging. Why all the cardboard dust? Why do I have to ruin the box to open it? Why is the picture on the cover slightly off from the actual puzzle? Why isn't the bag inside re-sealable? Why do the pieces bend/crease so easily? Why don't the pieces lock together comfortably? And so on.

I've never heard of this "Fred" brand, but we were really drawn to the quirky modern housecat-in-the-bushes artwork, and I was pleasantly surprised that none of the annoyances listed above are present here. There is also a full-size poster of the art, which you could certain put on the wall after you're done, if you like the art but aren't a 'frame, mount and hang your completed puzzle' person.

I like how most of the solid color areas have some variety to them, with light lines criss-crossing through them, and so on. Some people like the challenge of a, you know, rowboat in a storm surround by grey seas and grey skies kind of puzzle, and if you're that somebody, this puzzle will probably be way too easy.

But, for our gang, it's challenging but not overly tough, it's also not overly huge, and you never get tired of looking at that black cat!

It's perhaps a little pricier than some puzzles of similar quality, but I'd only deduct a half a star for that, I suppose. 4.5 stars and recommended.

We like to do a puzzle during the holidays, to sit together, chat, and do something relaxing.  This affordable puzzle was just the thing.  Great price. Fun art. It fit on the coffee table nicely while being assembled.  A couple of the pieces fit, even in the wrong place, so, be careful.  But, an affordable, fun puzzle, that made for a fun family experience.

QUALITY: Pieces are very high quality. Every piece locked in smoothly to its adjoining piece. They are thick, don't bend, and the printed coating on top is smooth. One of the most disappointing and frustrating aspects of a poorly-made puzzle is when certain pieces fit into multiple other pieces so you're left confused and irritated. This puzzle did NOT do that, and we are pleased as punch with the quality.

CHALLENGE: The challenge level was perfect. My boyfriend and I have gone through many puzzles during this quarantine, and this one was our favorite. We found ourselves challenged, but not stuck for weeks or frustrated as we experienced with 1,000+ piece puzzles or puzzles that have sections that are all the same color. We finished this in 1 night over the course of a few hours. It comes with a large print out of the design so you can reference that for help.

DESIGN: I was beyond thrilled when I found out Mary Kate McDevitt had come out with a puzzle. I took her Skillshare class on illustration several years ago and have been a fan ever since. She did not disappoint with the design of this puzzle and I'm pleased to have it in our collection. Now that we've completed it, we're passing it on to one of our friends who is a graphic designer and is sure to get a kick out of it!

I just love the new generation of Barbies. I love it!

Though I think of Barbies as being for slightly older children than my three-year-old daughter, she absolutely loved this set and knew exactly how she wanted to play with it. Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

As for the set, my only suggestion would be to make the eggs able to come out of the a container. Even if this means that most of the eggs immediately got lost, it would provide so much more opportunity for fun and creativity. In order to allow my daughter to collect eggs into the bucket, I made a few eggs out of oven baked clay so that she would have a little bit more opportunity for interactive play.

My complaints about this Barbie doll are my usual complaints, I wish that this Barbie was shaped a little bit more like Daisy, and I wish that this Barbie moved a little bit more like the sports Barbies. I wish that all Barbies off the shelf would come with more functional joints so that Barbie could do more interesting things. However! My three-year-old has noticed no lack, and I think the fact that Barbie is rather inflexible makes her somewhat easier to get dressed, which is fun. This Barbie has a very sweet, engaging face, and even though this toys for children, I'll be honest and say that I genuinely enjoy playing with this set with my daughter.

[[VIDEOID:3f39968e56dbff14af3d8dcf6e56c33c]] There is nothing wrong, per se, with this product--but there is a lot wrong with how it's marketed. I got this under the misunderstanding that it's a Transformer toy, but it's in no way a licensed Transformer product.

1. Manufacturer describes the toy as 3 to 7 year age range. I'll say that 3 years old is probably the limit with this. I have a 4 year old who likes to build with Legos and Duplos and has a few actual Transformers toys. This toy just moves in circles and on its own, so there's completely no intellectual engagement. A baby or very young toddler might enjoy watching it move, but for a kid in the 4 to 7 year old range, they might be briefly interested in it, but the interest won't last long. The box talks about it encouraging brain development. I can't see how given that you just watch the toy creep along the floor and veg out to it.

2. $15 is a high price point on this. It's mostly lightweight plastic. $10 is pushing it, especially considering that it does not come with batteries. (You have to get 3 of your own AAs.) This is the kind of toy you find in discount stores, drug stores or the small carts at the mall. (Target ain't gonna have this.)

3. It's not a licensed Transformers toy, though they market it as one.

4. The music it plays is cool (more cinematic and not cutesy chimey toy music), but it's LOUD. This is the first toy that has ever made my son want to cover his ears. "Momma, it's too loud!"

So, be aware of the true target age group for this. And be prepared for the decibel level. It's not a bad toy--it's just better for a younger and narrower age range, and also a little high on the price.

This is a pretty cool-looking and fun AE86 build for the Initial-D fan.  It's pretty much the size of legos as I was able to use the lego removal tool to help with the build.  Inside the box everything is well-wrapped even the display case has a plastic bag wrap to prevent it from getting scratched.  The build pieces comes in 6 bags similar to how legos are packaged.  At first I thought that each bag # gets built separately and then put together for an easy build process.  But as I followed the instructions that was not the case.  Seems like the the number on the bag is purely nothing but for the manufacturer packaging.  You have to open all the bags and search for each requested build piece from all bags and then build.  Not much of an organization process but was still easy to put together since the pieces aren't too many or small in size.  The instruction booklet was nicely design and provides good detail on putting the pieces together for an easy build.  Quality-wise, there were a few pieces that had poor manufacturing blemishes and finishing and just my luck they had to be on the ones that would be visible once completed.  The finishing stickers are good quality and well-done and isn't too sticky so that it makes it easy to reapply if you mess up.  Once put together it looks great and probably won't even be able to tell the difference if it's Legos or not.  Definitely a nice-looking AE86 build for the Initial D fan.  I had fun building it and likely only took a couple of hours to put it together.

this build is so cool. I love how it comes with its own container for displaying and I love how they tried to make such a detailed build in such a small sized model. It is about the size of other lego cars and the details on this are amazing. It was a tough choice between the skyline, the rx-7 and the trueno, but the skyline won with its build aesthetics for me. I loved the anime and games as a kid so I needed to add one of these iconic cars to my building block collection. Worth every penny in my opinion.

Early during COVID without having to drive back and forth to my business, I got pretty addicted to 1000 piece jigsaw puzzles, but I had put them aside lately as I got busier again. However, I felt that I deserved a break and maybe doing a puzzle would be a sort of meditation. I've been to Venice quite a few times, and this doesn't really remind me at all of Venice, one of my favorite cities, but the puzzle looked like the type I like -- lots of amusing images and not too much "blue sky" with no defining marks. The quality of the puzzle is good, with pieces that are relatively thick and cleanly cut. The colors in this particular painting are a little muted, but the print quality is, nevertheless, fine.

I started as I always do, by sifting through all 1000 pieces about five times to find all the edge pieces. I"m at the point where I'm missing only one edge piece, but it will probably crop up as I starting working from the outer edges inward. As a matter of fact, I've already made some headway there. So, why have I already given the puzzle 5 stars in difficulty on top of five stars in quality? There are many pieces that are shaped almost the same. For instance, I had pieces that fit perfectly on the edge where there was some blue sky, and later, I had to go back and change their positions in order to get other pieces to work with each other.

Ordinarily, I can, after getting the edges in place, sort out the puzzle pieces into dominant colors. However, other than the blue pieces for the sky, along with more blue for the water feature -- not sure whether it is supposed to be canal or maybe the sea itself -- the pieces are more pattern pieces than color pieces. Other than some prominent features it's going to be pretty difficult to find the pieces that belong together. So -- a very challenging puzzle, I believe.

I"ll mention one other feature that is a bit unusual. This puzzle is square, rather than the shape most puzzles seem to be, in landscape format. Consequently, I could not use the puzzle board I had left over from one of my finished puzzles. Fortunately, I had a box from Amazon I had not yet disposed of that was big enough in both dimensions to hold the puzzle. So, if you are planning on getting this puzzle, make sure you have a table or board that will work, probably at least 30 inches square. And then look forward to a pretty challenging puzzle.

Initial Review October 23, 2021

With the Covid Pandemic we've been staying home a lot for the past 18 months. I normally do about one 1,000 piece puzzle per year, usually in the rainy cold dark winter months. We must have done about a dozen puzzles in the past year. With that experience I've developed some rules for buying puzzles.

One thing I look for in a puzzle is an actual photographed picture. They aren't always easy to find.
Another thing is I don't want one color to dominate the puzzle which can tend to make the puzzle harder to do. After all I'm doing the puzzle for fun and if it becomes too difficult I get frustrated. So no large areas of blue sky, or no large areas of water for example. I also demand that there is a large paper print of the puzzle which I can use for reference. Having the boxtop with the photo is also a big benefit as my wife and I do enjoy doing them together. This puzzle ticked all the boxes.

I really didn't think I would enjoy this puzzle as it was a graphic drawing rather than a photo. In this case it turned out to be a positive part of the experience. There were so many different objects, and no large areas of the same color. The pieces were smaller than most of the other puzzles I've been doing, but I adjusted quickly so that wasn't a big problem. The "cut" of the puzzle is very precise. They locked together positively. It all sounds good so why not five stars?

Shiny puzzle pieces were the one issue, and why I wouldn't buy from this company again. It may not bother you depending on how your lighting is. Ours is a 7 bulb chandler directly over the center of the table. With the pieces being so shiny I had to constantly rock my head from side to side to shift the glare. My wife also commented on this feature. I hope the company reads this and considers it with other puzzle purchasers comments and they make an adjustment. I haven't had this problem before. Now I can appreciate that one other puzzle we purchased actually advertised that the pieces were not shiny.

So pretty much everything is good concerning this puzzle, except for the shiny surface.

Oh one other thing. When I completed the puzzle there was a piece left over. I wonder if there is some sorry person out there who bought one of these puzzles but finds, at the end of hours of puzzle making, their puzzle is missing a piece.
These pieces not well made. The cardboard on the puzzle peels off.

The image is bright and fun - eeBoo has several others in a similar style that suit us well too. We've done a few with images intended to challenge, but this is our preference.

NICE: It comes with 3 good versions of the assembled image. The top & bottom box pieces each have one and there's a separate sheet insert with an even larger one. My wife doesn't stare these down nearly as much as I do, but when there's only one on the box top, it does get in our way a bit. The color fidelity is also good across these 3 and the actual puzzle pieces.
Like the product description says, there is minimal dust with the pieces. Virtually none.

Not so nice: The cuts are below average. There are a lot of unseparated pairs, and some bigger 4, 6, and even a chunk of 12 as in my photo. Most separate cleanly and easily but I've had a few so far that started small tears (always on the bottom) as I carefully separated by hand.

The pieces are typical thickness, decent quality. The image face feels glossier than many. Shapes are uniform squares, but the combinations and sequences of tabs & slots varies. Their location & size vary a little bit - it's pretty easy to tell a proper match when you find it. But there are no extreme differences, so you won't spot the right fit from across the table. This also means the bag has a lot of false connections in the bag - pieces that obviously don't match (or aren't even facing the same way) that need gentle separation.

A lot to like overall, a shame there were so many incomplete cuts in the set we got.

FOLLOWUP: This puzzle finally reached the top of our stack and we finished it recently. There were still a few more uncut pairs, and a small bit of damage to a couple pieces as we separated those by hand.
But there were no missing pieces and the image and piece shapes were above average in our enjoyment of the puzzling.
We found this puzzle relatively easy - a nice break from our previous 2 that were also 1000 pieces and similar size, but just more challenging images. For this one, just about every part of the puzzle has distinctive color and content, so there really wasn't any area that lagged behind as we took care of the easier parts.

My family was recently reintroduced to the fun of picture puzzle solving by friends who are knowledgeable fans off the hobby. On their recommendation, we started off with a puzzle by one of their favorite puzzle makers, “eeBoo Piece and Love”. They recommended eeBoo puzzles to us based on their positive experience(s) with the company’s table top puzzles. What we were told boiled down to “eeBoo makes totally excellent, high quality puzzles that are fun to solve. They are reasonably priced (and) you can’t go wrong with any one from them. (Period).”

Hearing that, we were in.

Our first picture puzzle from eeBoo was titled “English Cottage” and it was a treat in every way, shape, and form. As much as we enjoyed the challenge of solving the puzzle we appreciated the effort that went into creating the namesake image. The “English Garden” puzzle was made with quality pieces that had clean edges and sharp, colorful, images. And, importantly, all the pieces fit together precisely and without fuss. That “English Cottage” experience led directly to our experience with the puzzle “Venice Open Market”.

Simply put, eeBoo’s “Venice Open Market” puzzle shares all of the same, high quality, features we liked about “English Cottage”. It is very well made, and the puzzle’s image is detailed with many built-in mini stories to discover. The puzzle’s image has a nice, warm, color palette that (the box states) was created with eco-friendly vegetable based inks on 90% recycled board. It’s a win-win.

The takeaway:
Our experience with eeBoo’s “Venice Open Market” shared all of the positive qualities we enjoyed when solving our first puzzle from the company. Working on this puzzle has been a treat that makes it very easy to recommend. Have fun.

B0BMTV3GNY.text: As a child of the 70's the Wham-O Air Blaster was one of my favorite toys.  It looked like a big cool ray gun and fired a precise focused ball of air. This air bazooka is no air blaster. This air bazooka is basically a collapsible bathroom trashcan with a hole in the bottom and a short plastic liner and rubber bands. What an innovative and inspired design.  Holding from the bottom while pulling back from above means it's hard to aim.  It's very loud and the plastic used in the liner is crinkly in both sound and appearance. With all the cracks forming in that plastic lining after minimal use, I don't expect it to last very long. This is a good idea from the past that's been implemented cheaply and poorly.

May not have been set up properly at the factory - weak puff of air; tension band had an inch or more of slack and may not be allowing the bladder to fully push the air out. NOT as powerful as the old Whammo Air Blasters at all. Near impossible for a hand to hold it halfway steady while pulling the mechanism back, let alone try to aim it and release the mechanism. Would be even more difficult for a kid, ... BUT you can kind of aim through the center hole through the semi-clear bladder, so that may work for most people. The concept works, and may work better on a hand made one.
Just not sure whether to recommend this device - it could be fun if it performed better.

B0BTDY19PT.text: Fun kit that comes with everything you need to make vegan vanilla donuts.

Some of my best memories from childhood revolve around baking with my mother. This kit streamlines the process. The kit is easy to use with vegan, low carb ingredients. It is easy to mix up , bake and decorate. The donuts are actually pretty tasty. The one problem was the sprinkles that escaped from the pack. They got everywhere.  Otherwise a fun project for parents and kids.

I also tried the chocolate version of this donut kit and was quite disappointed in the taste of the donuts. This vanilla option is much better. In anticipation of less than ideal taste I added some good quality vanilla extract which also helped boost the flavor.

Still, the issues I had with the chocolate version are also present in this version. The box it comes in is cheap and flimsy, and dented up quite a bit in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.
Easy to do. Fun activity to do with kids. The donuts taste ok but I seriously found it overly priced.

I got this for my 3 1/2 year-old that loves donuts and really likes to help in the kitchen. The directions were easy to follow and all of the ingredients were prepackaged so that made it very easy for her to do all of the pouring and mixing on her own. These donuts tasted good, but they were like cake in a donut shape.
This set came with 6 silicone molds that you can reuse to make more donuts in the future. It also contains sugar sprinkles, coconut sprinkles (unsweetened coconut), frosting mix, and flour mix. All you really need is oil for the flour mix and water or milk for the frosting mix. The frosting mix directions stated to put 2 to 3 teaspoons of milk or water. At first, we used 2 teaspoons of almond milk and it was really thick. Then we upped it to 3 teaspoons which made it more like a glaze than frosting. Next time I would only do 2 teaspoons.
Some problems I found with this product were minor but still disappointing. First, the package of sugar sprinkles was very weakly sealed and ended up exploding all over my countertop and floor when my child moved them around. We ended up having to use our own chocolate cookie crumbs on top of the donuts because we didn’t have enough sprinkles. Second, the coconut shreds and the frosting mix were inside of the package with the flour mix. I wish that all four packages were separate because we got flour mix all over the place trying to remove these from the package while pouring everything into the bowl. Ultimately, I had to rinse them under the water because I needed to keep them on my countertop since we couldn’t make the frosting right away and the coconut shreds were for the topping after everything was done. Third, I did notice some discrepancies between the package directions and the directions that came on the card inside the box. The package called for 3.5 ounces of water whereas the card said 3 ounces. I opted for 3.5 ounces to make the donut more moist. But why is there this discrepancy? Also, the calories are different on the package mix compared to the back of the box. They really should get their information straight before they start printing it in multiple places.

Our family had so much fun making these together and the adults had even more fun eating them as a guilt free indulgence! The taste is great compared to other vegan desserts we’ve had. Definitely will purchase again!

Love this baking kit! These are perfect for my 9 year old niece, as she is learning to cook and bake. This kit is very cool and fun, something to do together with your kids, niece, nephew or even grandchildren, etc. Will for sure try their choco collate flavor next!

B0BZTVR5SX.text: This set of Pokemon cards is as described. I gave this to my 24 year old son who is still a big Pokemon fan. He said the description was accurate as far as the rare and foil cards. He actually found a couple that he felt was worth keeping. The rest he will share with his younger cousins who are ages 8-13. They will be thrilled!  He says this set is good for beginners.

My 24 year old son has been collecting Pokemon cards for years. This set of 20 "rare" cards, according to him, may technically be better than average cards, but they're fairly common. Out of the 20, he kept 2 for himself. The rest he will divide between his younger cousins. If you're new to collecting, these will probably be pretty good.

This set of Pokemon cards is good for beginners. You get a lot of cards for the price. The cards are from smaller packages and I'm assuming that they have been picked over before repackaging them. This set does include 10 hologram cards. For the most part the cards were pretty basic, but if you're just starting out as a collector, it's a good way to grow your collection.

This is as advertised. You get the "random" Ultra Rares and Rares promised, but the rest appear to be random old Pokemon commons. I highly doubt you'll find anything great in these repacks.
I think your $$ are better spent getting 6 retail boosters. You will get almost as many cards, with many more rares/foils, and likely much better quality. But to each their own... my son still enjoyed them

There are tons of cards in this set. The variety is great.

I was really skeptical about this set but it's totally fantastic!!!

They are legit cards and there are a ton of really nice ones, not just trainers and energies!

Lots of hollows, reverse hollows, and some pretty rare ones. Tons of legendary pokemon so kids will love them.

Overall this is on of the best card values I've ever found online and is great.

First of all, this pack was a big hit with my kids. Sure it came with dupes but that's fine in my opinion because you can use more then 1 of the same type in a deck! Each card came in decent/great condition. The holos that were in this pack was from the 25th anniversary which was awesome since those are more of a collector set. Would totally order another set in the future.
We got 22 cards and the kids divided them evenly. There were no complaints and my oldest son confirms there are all “very cool”.

If you are looking for a wide variety of Pokemon cards for a casual player then you should consider this item. For an avid collector, I would not recommend this item.

It did contain 20 Holo/Shiny cards and 3 Holo Rares (seen to the left half of my picture).

The non-holo/shiny card duplicates are to the right side of my picture.

This item contained multiple duplicates. 13 cards had doubles. 3 cards had triplets. For a total of 19 duplicate cards. Of 70 overall cards, that is 27% of the deck that is repeated.

Many of the cards had minor scratches to the surface.

I imagine if you are an avid pokemon card collector, this would be a disappointment to receive for the price point (~$42 as of now). I personally know nothing about pokemon cards but my boyfriend does and he was not wowed with the set. I only wanted it because my daughter is newly fond of pokemon and so personally, I’m very happy with it. It makes for a great starter pack for a 4 year old who barely knows how to read yet for sure! Definitely a good variety of different pokemon. No Pikachu but many many others

I feel like if you’re a big fan you might expect better than what comes in this pack. Not sure why the cards were badly arranged in the box. Some were upside down or flipped. I also got a few duplicates which I was not expecting.

I didn't count to see if we actually received 100 cards, but there was a nice variety of cards with only a handful that were duplicates in the regular cards (a couple we got 3 cards of).

We got 11 holographic cards, but 3 were the same, another 2 were the same, and another 2 were the same. So that was a bit of a disappointment since I was hoping that the holographic cards would at least be all different since you only get 10 of them (we got 11), but my son's only 8 years old & the cards were a gift for him, so he didn't seem to mind a bunch lol. They're were so many cards that he was happy! :D

We also received in the set 5 of the trainer/supporter (people) cards (no duplicates) & about 10 of the trainer item cards (a couple of those were duplicates.)

They were all in new condition & are a great gift for someone who likes Pokemon if you aren't sure what cards they already have...this way, they're bound to get something new! Or they'd be great for a children's party or a picnic/holiday gathering where each kid can pick & choose some cards to take home with them & to play with while they're there.

I like that the packaging was minimal...all the cards fit into the small black box they came in which can be re-used. I can't say what generation these cards are all from since I don't play Pokemon so I'm not familiar with it at all lol, & my son's just starting out collecting the cards himself. But it's a great price for so many cards & it was a good way for my son to enhance his small collection!! :D

I would echo what some other have said regarding packaging. Since the seller is essentially repacking Pokémon cards, they come in a cheap little box that’s not even sealed. As such, when I opened the shipping bag, cards flew everywhere.

These seem like they’re legit, compared to some of the more obvious knockoffs.

I haven’t been thru the entire deck scrutinizing for dupes, but I’m betting there are several. And I’d be curious to know how much variety you’d get if you ordered 2 of these from the same seller.

All in all, this is a decent preview for a bunch of Pokémon cards. If your kids are just getting into the cards because “everyone else is” then this would be a great (and inexpensive) way to get them started.

-1 star due to how they were shipped. They will get damaged in shipping and the seller could make an effort to re-seal the boxes to protect the cards.

There are a lot of cool cards in here, but not exactly a great diversity in sets. Which is fine for just adding to a random collection or figuring out different play styles. They all came slightly bowed, but nothing tragic. Who knows, maybe hold on to them another 20 years and see where we are?

10 holo cards plus 100+ mix of common and uncommon cards, all in good condition. I did get some duplicates, as you can see in the full spread, including 2 duplicate holos (so 8 unique holos), but overall, not many duplicates. The description did specifically say that they try to LIMIT duplicates and not exclude them completely, so I'm okay with that.

My spread was 10 holo rares, 29 uncommons, and 73 commons, for a total of 112 cards. Of my 112, 11 were duplicates, so I had a total of 101 unique cards. Not bad for $22!

The oldest cards in this set were from 2016 XY Evolutions sets, and the newest seem to be copyright 2021. All in all, it was a good spread of cards, and I was pleased with how many stages of the same evolution tree I got.

Perhaps my only real complaint is that the deck box they arrived in was a bit battered, but it did its job protecting the cards, so I'm not really complaining there.

From the way the description was worded I was expecting ten packs of ten, suitable for giving as ten distinct party favors or similar. It’s just a stack of new-condition cards, not sorted in any meaningful way (so I’d have to think about how to best compose sets of ten from 100+ individual cards, and come up with my own packaging - clear sandwich bags aren’t too festive). I think it should have been made clear this is a set designed for individual collection-building. And the thin box isn’t even sealed in any way—the cards were falling out of the box and in danger of being damaged by the other items they shipped with.

There were Lots of duplicates, including four of the same holographic, and eight of the same common card. Still beats the cost of individual packs, but was a bit disappointed with this haul. Price was about $22.

Below are more detailed counts:

Grand total: 113 cards

Rares: 10
All Pokémon: 1 reverse holo (Vaporeon - Kanto!), 9 holos (1 is Lugia; 4 are Ho-Oh, the other 2 and 2, respectively, are the same)

Uncommons: 43
1 special energy (rapid strike), 18 trainers (2 double), 23 Pokémon (4 double, 1 quadruple) - 3 Pokémon are Kanto

Commons: 60
All Pokémon (4 double, 1 triple, 1 octuple) - 20 are Kanto (8 are shadow Koffing!)

I didn’t get a good photo of these cards before my kids snatched them out of my hands and started divvying them up and trading them - but they guaranteed that there was a good selection of different cards inside, and no doubles at all! Definitely worth it as a gift, no so sure if they work as party favors though, as they are altogether in one box, not in separate packages.

"The Ultimate PKMN Card Birthday Party Favor Pack - 100 Cards" is the second set of cards I've ordered from this brand. Like the other set, these seems to be real cards. That's fantastic and in a world of imposters, worth a lot.

Where this collection goes slightly south is in its selection of cards. The majority of these are Basic. And out of 100 cards, there were at least 7 sets of duplicates and 5 sets of triplicates. That's 29 cards out of 100 that are the same as each other. (Note, I didn't study the cards to find this out; rather, these were dupes that jumped out to me as I looked over the deck. So there may be more duplicates that I missed.) I do wish there were less repeats...

As for value, that's for you to decide. $22 for 100 average cards may or may not seem like a good deal to you. They're OK for my kids now, but if they ever start playing more seriously we may need to pay more to ensure better sets. I'm giving this set four stars.

I didn't know what to expect, buying these Pokémon cards. Would they be real? Quality? All duplicates, or just super common cards?

Well, my kids are telling me this is a good set by their reactions. They've each gotten one V card plus numerous other cards that excite them and they say are powerful. I'm afraid I don't know Pokémon so I can't tell you what that means! LOL But I can say that the cards appear legitimate; they look as real as the ones we bought from a main store nearby. So far we seems to have one duplicate pair (there are about 4 cards left - we've been revealing them slowly).

This has been a great set for us.

This item would be good only for parties where the kids don't care about getting the same cards as their friends, or for brand new collectors who just want to bulk up their numbers from very recent releases.  There were 10 of one card in the pack, so not an amazing variety.

received a box that was open in the package we received, and the cards were very common and the ultra rares weren't what we had expected and the holographics were promo cards from another box, wasn't very pleased based off of the photos of the cards they said you can possibly get. would not really recommend unless you are just starting out collecting and don't mind a lot of common cards and nothing too special inside.

Received a box of opened cards all thru my package to start...they were bent and only had 2 reverse holos inside that were very common and relatively new. No "ultra rares", and too many commons and energy cards...wouldnt recommend at all.

What I can absolutely say is that this set did contain the minimum guaranteed cards claimed in the description. They weren't super special or anything, but if I were to sell them, I'd probably earn a good portion of the cost of this pack back. Don't go into this expecting to get some super-high-value card out of it, but do expect to get plenty of new cards for your decks. I recommend this for collectors and resellers.

I ended up getting 91 commons/uncommons instead of 70, 20 rares, 19 holo/shiny cards instead of 20, and 3 holo rares. Of the 91 commons/uncommons, the extra 21 cards were all duplicates and under 30 were uncommons (including some of the dupes). There were also several instances where I had the same pokemon but a different card. The rares were concentrated in mostly just 4 types. Many of the cards had a slight curve in them and/or some type of residue on them, so the quality just wasn't there. And there weren't really any super popular pokemon that were standouts from the show or a video game.

My 5yo is just getting into Pokemon, so I thought it would be a fun little collection for him. But after thinking about it for a while, I don't know that I would recommend getting this at all if I was actually playing the game. There are no energy cards and very few trainer cards, and even many of the holo/shiny cards you can't play because they are Stage 1/2 and you don't necessarily have the supporting earlier stage cards. If I was hoping for a specific card in particular, I think I'd be better off going to my local card shop and getting just what I wanted and probably with a little better quality. I recognize there might be other people out there with different collecting strategies who might find these fun and/or useful, but for any purpose I would be interested in, I would not order something like this again.

Wow! I got this thinking that the variety would not be that great but I was very much surprised. I would have to buy 3 premium tins to get as many cards as this pack came with! Great value! Will buy more from this seller in the future!

Would not give as a gift in condition received.

When you have a puzzle with this many pieces, with the same color scheme throughout pretty much the entire puzzle, it could take months to complete. Fortunately, the pieces for the MaxRenard puzzles are color coded. There are 6 sections (about 166 pieces per section) in which the back side of the piece is a different color for each corresponding section. Where the colored sections meet, there are two colors. When you have picturesque backgrounds with a lot of the same colors, it is extremely hard to piece together. I like that I can do this in sections but I almost feel like the entire point of a puzzle is to make you think, so it's almost as if I am cheating. I find myself separating the colors to make it not as difficult.

The picture of the puzzle alone is very colorful and bright. The puzzle is a challenge but workable. There are so many pretty areas in the puzzle and it's looking nice as it comes along

A brightly colored beautiful puzzle.  The pieces are sturdy and interlock well.  For those who like to cheat, the back of each piece is color coded and the box comes with a divider so all like backside colors can be gathered together.

Other than minor spelling and labeling errors on the box such "carboard" instead of "cardboard" and "animal puzzle" when this is clearly not, everything else is great. On a challenge scale of 1 - 10 where 10 is the most challenging, this puzzle is an 8. The puzzle can be put together without using the back side color code. The bottom half is relatively straight forward with people and faces. However, the top half is more difficult with the white (slight shade differences) marble and the dark ceiling. The end result is worth it. The picture is clear and beautiful. The box comes with a large poster and six small boxes for sorting (based on the back side color of each piece).  The pieces are sturdy and they snap together. I really enjoyed assembling this puzzle.

Ever since COVID hit, I've been doing puzzles. This is a Max Renard puzzle. It's of the School At Athens. Not sure why it says animal puzzle on the top right corner.
Anyway, the pieces are well cut. No dust in the sturdy box. The pieces came in a plastic bag. It's not resealable, and that's too bad as I prefer a resealable bag for security of pieces.
The colours are muted (following the painting). The back of the pieces are various colours. This is for colour coding. It's the first puzzle I've had that used this.

There's a large blow up poster for detail work which is a nice touch, glue sheets if you want to save the puzzle and some cardboard pieces you can use to sort and isolate the pieces in the box or lid.

I really like the puzzle and I am very happy with the quality. I would definitely buy more of this brand.

the pieces look good and color makes it easier to put together

This puzzle takes a lot of patience to put together. I don't have to completed yet and will post a pic once finished. I started by doing to entire outside boarder and I've been working a long time to fill it in. I didn't realize in the beginning that the backside of the pieces are color coded. So it appears each section of the puzzle contains a different color on the back. Once I realized this I separated the pieces by color. This has helped tremendously but it's still not a puzzle that can be put together in a couple of hours, so many colors look the same. After working on this for weeks I'm only about 1/6 finished. I'm anxious to get this finished so I can hang it on the wall. The pieces are sturdy and go together easily...once you find the correct piece. It's nice to work on a puzzle in the evenings after work instead of being on the cell phone all the time. The outline of this puzzle is a pretty big size and with 1000 pieces this will entertain you and your children for a very long time. This puzzle is a great one for gift giving because everyone recognizes this design.

UPDATE - finally finished putting it together and I absolutely love this puzzle. I plan to frame and hang it. In the pic I had just glued it that's why there are paper towels around it. I had to contact the seller and the company was responsive and helped me immediately. Awesome puzzle.

The MaxRenard 1000-piece jigsaw puzzle of Rafael DaVinci’s ‘The School of Athens’ appears to be everything one would expect to find in a standard 1000-piece puzzle plus a few extras. Unlike many cheaper puzzles, where one needs to make constant reference to a small low-resolution box cover to assemble, this product conveniently includes a large high quality blow-up poster. As the backs of the pieces are all color coded, this should simplify the assembly process and assist sticking and mounting (mounting stickers and organizing inserts are also conveniently included). The pieces are solid and durable. What puzzle enthusiast wouldn’t enjoy piecing together such a masterful work of art and culture with friends or family?

What attracted us to this puzzle are the colors and we’re so glad we got it.  Aside from the puzzle itself, you also get stickers to permanently keep the puzzle together if you want and you get these cardboard dividers so you can organize your puzzle pieces.  The pieces themselves are sturdy and fit together nicely.  There are no letters on the back of the pieces though so no help on that front if you rely on those letters to solve the puzzle.  That’s okay though because you get this really pretty poster to help you out.  This is great as a family activity or as a gift.
This MaxRenard Statue of Liberty Jigsaw Puzzle is rather nice. It seems like it is of good quality cardboard for the pieces and is challenging enough for a 1000 piecer. Quite nice.

This is a great puzzle for those who love a good puzzle. It's got 1000 pieces which is a good challenge. The pieces have a nice weight and aren't shedding like others I've had. The backs are color coded if you want help separating them. Also there are some sorters if you want to keep them in the box but still be able to tell them apart. Also for those who like to save their puzzles this includes glue sheets to piece it together, keep and frame. I'd get more from this company. Great puzzle!
Fun puzzle with 1000 pieces. If you're a Van Gogh fan, you'll enjoy. If you're a puzzle connoisseur you'll also have fun doing this!

I love Raphael's Schoolof Athens, so I was happy to see this puzzle. The pieces fit together without issue and the color-coding of different areas on the back of each piece allows it to be completed with less difficulty. The stickers that can be adhered to the back worked well and holds the puzzle together. Great product.

The box was smaller than I expected but there was basically no fluff space which is great. These pieces are standard sized and similar to ravens burger puzzles I used before. The difference is that they are thinner but made from a different material that I’m willing to bet is stronger than cardboard. I haven’t had any issues with any of the pieces jamming or bending but then again I am pretty careful and wouldn’t want to just do that intentionally for a review. The puzzle comes with a bunch of goodies such as a paper stand (not sure what for), sticky paper, and a poster of the starry night. The details are great and the side that has the image is textured while the back of the pieces have 1 of 6 different pastel colors which lets you cheat. You can sort these using the back colors to do the puzzle in approximately 170 piece sections. It’s brilliant because this puddle is quite difficult and I was a bit overwhelmed when I first started. This is a great quality licensed puzzle and the quality is top notch.

Will post a picture when it’s done, hopefully sometime within the next month.

A lot going on in this photo so it's a bit of a challenge. The back is color-coded, in case you need a bit of help. It has relatively sturdy pieces in a variety of shapes. An almost full-sized photo is enclosed so you can see details, and something I'd never seen before: there is a sticky backing enclosed in case you want to mount the finished product.

This puzzle was very high quality, in my opinion. There were no fraying edges or broken pieces, and everything fit together smoothly. This was a pretty challenging puzzle, due to a lot of the pieces looking similar, however, if you want to make it easier you can just separate by color backing and do it in sections. The print image was excellent and was not pixelated. The only issue with this puzzle is that the image on the box and the image inside are not cropped in the same place as the puzzle is, so you might get a little confused if you are using the reference images to help set the edge pieces.
This puzzle is beautiful and well made. It was far more challenging then I expected too. Inhighly recommend any MaxRenard puzzles. They never disappoint.

Started this puzzle thinking it would be somewhat easier because it was a city picture but I was wrong. Definitely more challenging than expected, but I like the challenge. The puzzle is made very well and thick. Highly recommend it!

I do like a good puzzle, and have done several 1000 piece ones recently.  The quality of this one is just OK.  The pieces are slightly thinner than I'm use to.  Though it does have a few unusual features that I had not seen, such as the color coding the back of each piece to direct you to which quadrant it belongs.  Perhaps if you struggle with 1000 piece puzzles, this would be a good way to ease into them.  Honestly I could do without this feature, for it makes it difficult to know which side is up.  It also includes stickers to "glue" together the back to preserve the finished puzzle.  I can't see anyone wanting to do that, but if you're one that preserves completed puzzles then this might be a plus.  The large fold out poster is a nice feature that I've seen with other puzzles that come in compact boxes.  The box is not terribly small in this case, but still a nice touch.  One star off for cardboard quality and a slightly crushed box (does not appear Amazon was responsible for that during shipping), and the fact that for $20 you can likely find a better quality puzzle, such as those made by Ravensburger.  I would only recommend this one if the price was a bit lower.

This has been one of my favorite paintings for a long time, and this puzzle version is well done! Be warned, this one is a challenge to complete ... but look at the painting, folks, and you should be expecting it to be tough. The puzzle itself is well made, with sturdy pieces, and the six colors on the backside of the pieces is a huge help in narrowing down your placements. My only complaint ... the images on the box lid and enclosed poster are not cropped exactly as the puzzle itself, so if you're looking for visual cues along the edges, you might be misled.

Definitely a good one for puzzle enthusiasts!

The puzzle says it's for anyone age 14 and up. I put it together with my children, both age 8, and it was hard -- but they did it, and they were SO proud when it was done!

The puzzle is 1,000 pieces, but the back is divided into six colored sections to give puzzlers a significant boost toward separating the pieces. While there are very difficult patches in the puzzle -- areas of dark blue water, for instance -- the twins grew adept at finding the patterns, and it gave them a real sense of achievement every time they matched a piece.

Let's be honest, I did MOST of the work, but the twins thoroughly enjoyed the process, they were diligent in their efforts, and they felt amazingly proud of themselves when the last piece snapped into place! This was a great puzzle to do with them, and I look forward to the next one!

I think that most people would agree, that when you buy a teddyy bear you want it to be soft and cuddable. Do the manufacturers of these things actually think that adding a wide ribbon and toiling it around the bear's neck is going to make the bear more huggable? The ribbon is not soft, and I don't know about you, but I don't want to hug a ribbon. So, the first thing I had to do, was cut it off. Then, there is the tag coming out of the right ear. I read the tag and uploaded a picture of it, it has a "To" and "From" name tag where you can write the name of the person you are giving it to. But on the other side of the tag, it says, "Remove all tags before giving to a child". So, if they really want people to remove all tags from the bear before giving it to a child, why do they add a "To" and "From" name tag? Seems unnecessary. Anyhow, I wanted a soft with no ribbons stabbing me or tags sticking out, so I had to cut them all off immediately, and I've uploaded a picture of the naked bear without them. Looks a lot better if you ask me. Now, it's actually soft enough to hug. If the bear would have come with no crap on it to cut off, it would probably remove 5 stars, because it's rather cute.
oh...and btw...someone gave a 1 star review because the bear was made in China. I think it goes without saying, that unless the tag clearly says made in USA, it will be from China, regardless of what it is.

My sons watch Jurassic Park with me and both really like dinos, so this building set seems like a natural tie-in. It's a fairly fun build, and depending on LEGO experience, relatively easy too. Unlike LEGO however, the instructions for the jeep are on a single sheet of paper, so the illustrations are smaller. I don't see this as a bad thing, as it's substantially less paper, and my sons tend to agree. It was kind of odd that it came in a rather large non-descript bag. Overall it's a pretty fun and compact set.

This is an off-brand LEGO kit for an off-brand Jurassic Park jeep and you get what you pay for: it's a fun build with fairly clear instructions (they are a little small but plenty visible) and you end up with a jeep that looks a lot like the ones in the first Jurassic Park movie. The pieces don't all snap together as perfectly or as snugly as with LEGO but these are pretty decent. I've done a few other builds with this brand with my 5yo and it's a very nice second tier brick brand. No surprises here: everything works, looks like advertised and stays together when complete. Definitely recommend.

I was really excited to get into this Jurassic Car build once it arrived. Upon opening, all the pieces are neatly packaged into smaller plastic baggies. I was pleasantly surprised that it came with a brick removal tool. Definitely felt like an added bonus with the toy.

Although the kit suggest it's for ages 6 and up, I spent precisely an hour putting this thing together (I worked on it in my living room and just happened to be facing my wall clock. I started at 4pm and the final piece went on right as the clock reached 5pm). Having done so, I feel it's more appropriately made for someone who might be 10 or older.

The instructions aren't bad, but I just wish they were a little bigger. It's neat that they highlight each piece in each step of the instructions as they go onto car, but the diagrams are so small that I had to squint my eyes to make sure I'm snapping them in properly. Also, as you can see in the picture, the order of the steps tend to run all over the place. One page can run from top to bottom while the subsequent page can run left to right. I also noticed that steps 45 to 48 were out of order.

Given the issues with the instructions, if you worked slowly, it's not difficult to put together as it's a well designed kit. The final product looks really good and has some nice features like working doors. The quality of the bricks are also really good and on par with an actual Lego set.

Even though it's meant to model the Jeep from Jurassic Park, without any of the logos and markings, it makes for a handsome little Jeep Wrangler display piece.

Would absolutely recommend to anyone looking for a fun little kit.

All my reviews reflect my honest, personal experience with the reviewed item - your experience may be different.  I receive/accept NO free products or discounts that are not available to all shoppers.

We have quite the collection of giant outdoor games. They're a lot of fun when we host cookouts. The game of Sorry was a childhood favorite! The game board is a little more durable than the a disposable table cloth, but not as durable as the vinyl table cloths backed in felt. The pieces have to be put together, but then once assembled, they don't fit in the storage box. The game uses a spinner instead of dice. The large definitely has an appeal to it. There is room for improvement with this one.

We tried this recently on a rainy evening, and it was a fun family activity. However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.

[[VIDEOID:f5ccdd5c253cb3674461bb4a8a7d3581]] What little kid doesn’t love pretending to ride a speedboat? This is a lot of fun for the pool!

This raft doesn’t have holes for feet which can be a good and bad thing. If your kid wants to use their feet to kick around, that’s not an option, so either the parent has to pull the boat around or they have to try to use their arms or get a paddle. It is kind of easy to fall out of if you lean too much, so the arm paddling option poses that risk. On the flip side, my son didn’t want to “get wet,” so he was very happy that his legs didn’t get in the water and liked having mommy pull him around.

My other son has an inflatable boat that includes a little water gun attached to it, so my son was a little disappointed that this one didn’t have that. It would be kind of cool if it had a steering wheel or something.

Nevertheless, it’s well made, fun, and has well loved characters as the theme!

Knowles.  And now, if you are a parent, you stand just a little bit better chance than I did at beating my kids at this game which is aptly titled, Beat the Parents.  Basically, the kids and adults divide up into two teams and take turns drawing cards which have three questions designated for the kids and three for the adults.  Questions are asked of the other team until a wrong answer is given, and then the questioned team advances the number of spaces corresponding to the number of correct answers.  There's a few other twists, but that's basically it.  And, like most classic games, by keeping the rules simple, Beat the Parents winds up being a surprisingly fun game that even small children can participate in with older siblings (my six-year-old loves it).  And the best part: the questions seemed rigged so that the kids have an edge on winning--uless you happen to be an adult who knows what animals comprise the G-Force.  My kids love this game because, as the title promises, they get to Beat the Parents.

The concept is simple enough and as old as the hills: parents and children try to stump each other while showing off how smart they are, in a good-natured way. The object, aside from having fun, is to demonstrate the virtue of being knowledgeable.

Here, the publisher has attempted to turn the concept into a board game - and failed.

The first failing is the emphasis on popular culture. So many of the books, TV characters and movies relied on will be yesterday's news the day after tomorrow.

Second, is the production. Questions and answers are on the same side of the card. Uhmmm, there's a problem with that.

Third, the idea of a kid's game should be fun for the kids, even if - and in spite of - the parents (grownups!) are involved. This game edges toward feeling like a teacher's aid. I didn't think it was a lot of fun for my grandchildren - and neither did they.

The game mechanics are inane. Just a gigantic card deck with challenging questions and answers would be better, in my opinion.

Overall, I think the designers missed their mark. Not a whole lot of fun for kids or adults and, in the final analysis, not educational either.

We often have a family game night once a week where we play board games, so when I had a chance to try Beat the Parents through the Vine Program, I was more than happy to give it a try. My children are almost 6 (the minimum age for this game) and 10, so we thought this would be a fun game to play because my daughter would get a chance to participate. Oftentimes, group "family" games are geared towards older children, so seeing that "6 and older" was the age range for this game, it offered us hope that she could have fun as well. Within a few minutes of starting this game, disappointment abounded.

Unless you are an expert in pop culture, with specific knowledge in Harry Potter, Pirates Of the Caribbean, Disney movies, and extreme sports, you may be out of luck on the "parent" side of the questioning. Here is a quick sampling of questions that stymied me, and left my pawns stuck at the middle of the game board:

"In Star Wars, Episode 1, what is the name of the young queen of Naboo?" Queen Amidala
"What does Coraline's Other Mother have instead of eyes?" Buttons
"In Harry Potter, pickle, earthworm, and ear wax are flavors of which candy?" Bertie Bott's Every Flavor Beans
"How long can a snail sleep?" Two years
"What is the name of the alien girl in Race to Witch Mountain?" Sara
"How old is Carl Fredrickson in the movie Up?" 78
"Foofa, Plex and Toodee are characters in what show?" Yo Gabba Gabba
"What is hatched from Eragon's blue stone?" A dragon

The premise of the game claims that these are questions that kids would know, but might challenge the parents, and my kids could not answer any of these questions. We all sat there stunned at just how few questions ANY of us could answer.

On the kids side of the questions, a six year old, according to the manufacturers, should have been able to answer the following questions:

"What country does tartan come from?" Scotland
"Who wrote the Twilight series?" Stephanie Meyer
"What is the head of the mafia called?" The Godfather
"Fingernails and what other body part are made from the same thing?" Hair
"What is another name for an Alsatian dog?" German Shepherd
"What does R.E.M. stand for?" rapid eye movement
"What is a pirates sword called?" A cutlass
"What is a group of crows called?" A murder

OK, so these questions were more my speed, but they were meant for the kids. As you might imagine, the 6 year old gave up and left the game, and her 10 year old brother was stumped as well. The game dragged on forever, as neither team could answer enough questions to get their pawns to the other side of the board. I tried to look at it from an educational perspective, and as a chance to teach something to my kids. But most of the questions were the type where the answers were quickly forgotten, or they just didn't care enough about the topic to want to know the answer. Thankfully, the "kids" questions seemed a bit easier to answer in general, and eventually the kids made it to the other side of the board (with the help of their dad). But another flaw with the game is that once you go through the deck (303 questions total for each team), there isn't another pack you can buy, so you have exhausted the questions, and the game becomes redundant. If the goal of the game it to get a winner, and no one can answer enough questions to get across the board, then it is just not fun. Needless to say, we have not played this game again, and I doubt it is a game we will pull out again on family game night.

I wish I could make a recommendation for the correct age group that would enjoy this game, but 6 is definitely too young, and according to other reviews, teens are too old because the game is too easy. You would need to find the right mix of an older child with perhaps an 8 or 9 year old, and as a parent, you would need to be well versed on pop culture, which I am obviously not. Or maybe you just need to split in to teams and put one parent and one child together, but that defeats the purpose of the "kids versus adults" concept. If you are looking for a fun trivia game, I would stick with "Trivial Pursuit" or "Go to the Head of the Class".

There are a significant number of questions and answers that are FACTUALLY WRONG! It is teaching and passing on INCORRECT INFORMATION! This game has not been reviewed and verified by a credible source.

Here is some of what you can expect--

What CITY is the Pentagon in? They say Washington DC. It isn't. It's Arlington, VA. I used to live right around there during 9/11, plus Google says so.
Who won the 2010 Superbowl? They say the Saints. Please, it was the Packers.
What two SEASONS does the equator experience? They say RAIN AND DRY. Only two seasons? Since when are "rain" and "dry" SEASONS? And on the equator, ALL FOUR SEASONS HAPPEN (as they do all over the planet, funny how that works).

Maybe my family is a bunch of geniuses, but we knew enough correct answers to start finding these Q/As very fishy. We Googled everything to verify. The game is definitely wrong and misleading! There are more off questions than this, and with the Wild Cards that make sure you can't get to the end.... well, I'm amazed so many people enjoy the game. It was a decent attempt at a balanced trivia game for kids and adults, but it falls flat with strategy, execution, and content.
